entries: At 10th level, you learn to wait for the perfect moment to strike. Once per turn when you have temporary hit points and hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend up to half your fighter level in temporary hit points to deal that much additional damage to your target.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Improved Second Wind
entries: Starting at 15th level, your endurance is unrivaled in battles. When you gain health from your Second Wind feature, you can also gain temporary hit points equal to the amount healed.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Halt the Assault
entries: Starting at 18th level, when a creature within 5 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to use your temporary hit points to reduce the damage taken by the target by the amount of temporary hit points forfeited.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: The First Vampire
entries: You have made a pact with a powerful vampire cursed by the gods or born as a creature of the night. Hundreds of haunted beings serve this vampire, so why enter a pact with you? Because you can act in the light of day unhindered? To cull weaker vampires?

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Creature of the Night
entries: At 6th level, you can use your action to cast {@spell polymorph} on yourself, transforming into a {@creature bat} or {@creature wolf}. While you are in either of these forms, you retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all spent uses upon completion of a long rest.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Eldritch Appetite
entries: Starting at 10th level, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with your Life Drain feature, you can use your reaction to consume the last of their fleeting mortality. When you do, you regain one of your expended pact spell slots. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Eternal Night
entries: At 14th level, your vampire patron grants you a taste of true immortality. You no longer age, and you gain resistance to necrotic damage.
Additionally, once per long rest, you can use a bonus action to gain the following effects for one minute:

You regain {@dice 1d6} hit points at the start of your turn if you have at least 1 hit point and aren't in direct sunlight or running water. If you take radiant damage or damage from holy water, this trait doesn't function at the start of your next turn.
When using your Drain Life feature, you can use it as if you were expending a 1st-level spell slot.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: The Parasite
entries: Your patron is a cosmic parasite, draining the vitality out of whole peoples and worlds. Upon forging a pact with such a patron, you become host to one of its nascent offspring. As you grow in power, the boundary between your identity and the parasitic larva within you blurs.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Symbiotic Sentinel
entries: Starting at 6th level, your patron remains alert to all threats to its host at all times. You cannot be surprised and you have advantage on Dexterity ability checks made to determine initiative. You also gain advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed} and {@condition frightened}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Spawn Pawn
entries: At 10th level, you learn the {@spell dominate person} spell. It counts as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of spells you know. You can also cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

When you cast this spell, your patron enhances the magic, dealing psychic damage equal to your warlock level if the creature succeeds on a saving throw to end the spell. In addition, damage can't break your concentration on this spell.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Larval Regeneration
entries: Starting when you reach 14th level, when you die, a larval parasite bursts from your corpse the next turn on your initiative. You control the parasite, which disappears after 24 hours. The parasite is a Tiny creature, has an AC of 14, maximum hit points equal to half your maximum hit points, and a walking speed of 30 feet. It otherwise uses your statistics but cannot cast spells.

As an action, the parasite can cause a creature within 5 feet of it to make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (your choice) against your warlock spell save DC. On a failure, the parasite burrows into the creature dealing piercing damage equal to your warlock level. While burrowed inside a creature, the parasite cannot take any actions, cannot be targeted by attacks, and is immune to all damage except psychic damage.

On each of the creature's subsequent turns it can use its action to make a Constitution saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. If the creature succeeds, the parasite is ejected from its body and into an unoccupied space of the creature's choice within 5 feet of it. If the parasite is still burrowed inside the creature when its turn ends, the creature takes necrotic damage equal to twice your warlock level. If this damage reduces the creature to 0 hit points, it immediately dies, the parasite disappears, and you take over the body of the humanoid as if you had been targeted by the {@spell reincarnate} spell and rolled the race the humanoid had been.
If you are returned to life, such as by the {@spell revivify} spell, your parasite immediately disappears. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Way of Pride
entries: Monks of the Way of Pride value themselves above all others. These monks focus on mastering their form, ego, and destructive power. They use their monastic traditions publicly, with the intention of gaining the respect and admiration of "lesser beings."
The prideful traditions of this order include adorning oneself with jewelry, hiding their scars from prying eyes, and commanding respect from those that would oppose them.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Irrational Retaliation
entries: Beginning at 6th level, damage dealt to you is damage dealt to your pride, and that is something you simply cannot allow. Whenever a creature deals damage to you, you can use your reaction to expend 2 ki points to target that creature. Until the end of your next turn, all attacks you make against the target creature have advantage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Redoubled Efforts
entries: Additionally at 6th level, while your current hit points are equal to or less than half your maximum hit points, you can roll one additional Martial Arts die when determining the extra damage dealt by a critical hit.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Ever Prideful
entries: At 11th level, your muscle memory takes over. When your hit points are reduced to 0 you are not knocked {@condition unconscious}, but you must still make death saving throws and suffer all the normal effects of taking damage while at 0 hit points. At the beginning of each of your turns whilst in this state you can spend 1 ki point to remain in this state. If you do not spend a ki point at the start of your turn whilst at 0 hit points you suffer all the normal effects of being reduced to 0 hit points.
The following also apply:

items: You cannot speak.
You cannot cast or concentrate on spells.
Critical hits against you count as one failed death saving throw instead of 2.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Egotistical
entries: Beginning at 17th level, you gain the benefits of this class' features that state 'while your current hit points are equal to or less than half your maximum hit points' whenever you are below your hit point maximum instead, provided you have been damaged by a hostile creature within the past minute.

name: Way of the Leaden Crown
subclassFeatures: Way of the Leaden Crown|Monk|PHB|Leaden Crown|GHPG|3

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Way of the Leaden Crown
entries: In contrast to the esoteric ideals of other monastic traditions, monks of the Way of the Leaden Crown have practical aims: the self-governance of humanoid peoples. These monks see the history of the world as a series of clashes between groups of powerful beings, where humanoids were at best collateral damage and at worst disposable pawns. To break this cycle of dependence and destruction, monks of the Way of the Leaden Crown master mental powers to fight back against the otherworldly powers of the multiverse and protect humanoid sovereignty.

One component of this plan involves training to do battle with powerful outsiders. The other equally important component is ensuring that humanoid societies are prepared to overthrow those powerful outsiders already dominating them. To that end, these monks seek political positions that place them in or near decision-making roles where they can influence humanoids to fight back against arch seraphs, arch daemons, and primordials.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Unsubtle Strike
entries: At 6th level, when you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or monk weapon, you can force it to make a Strength saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failure, you can choose to push or pull the creature 10 feet. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Psychic Crush
entries: Starting at 11th level, each time you hit a creature with an unarmed strike it gains a pressure point. A creature loses all pressure points if you give a different creature a pressure point or 1 minute after the last time it gained a pressure point. As a bonus action on your turn, you can spend 1 ki points to telekinetically crush a creature with 1 or more of your pressure points.

When you do, the creature must make a Strength saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failure, the creature takes {@dice 1d8} force damage per pressure point they have and they are {@condition restrained} until the end of your next turn. On a success, they take half as much damage and aren't {@condition restrained}. Either way, the creature then loses all pressure points.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Psionic Mastery
entries: At 17th level, you have mastered the psionic disciplines necessary to defend mortals from outsiders. As an action, you can spend 5 ki points to cast {@spell dispel evil and good}, {@spell hold monster}, {@spell telekinesis}, or {@spell wall of force}. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells and you do not need to provide material components when casting them in this way.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Wretched Bloodline
entries: With every promise made to a fairy, contract signed with a devil, and pact with the unquiet dead, there's a chance someone doesn't keep their end of the bargain. The vengeance of immortal beings lasts much longer than one lifetime, and the lingering magic of these curses can affect the mortal's descendants.

These inherited magical afflictions may manifest as a plague, deformity, or aversion to the sun. In such families, a child may be born that learns to master the latent magic within their inherited curse, turning their bloodline's bane into a personal boon—these sorcerers are known collectively as the Wretched.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Share the Burden
entries: At 6th level, you learn the {@spell bestow curse} spell. This spell counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against your number of sorcerer spells known. When you cast the spell, you can choose to cast it by spending 3 sorcery points instead of a spell slot. If you cast the spell using sorcery points, its range changes to 60 feet for that casting and your concentration can't be broken as a result of taking damage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Terrifying Visage
entries: Beginning at 14th level, you can use a bonus action to adopt the terrifying visage of the being who cursed your ancestor for 10 minutes. During this time, you can use an action on each of your turns to cause each creature who can see you within 30 feet make a Wisdom saving throw against your sorcerer spell save DC. On a failure, a creature is {@condition frightened} of you until the end of your next turn.
In addition, while you have adopted the terrifying visage, you gain an additional benefit based on the creature type chosen with your Blood Ties feature.

entries.name: Fey
entries: You can use a bonus action to teleport up to 30 feet in any direction.

entries.name: Fiend
entries: You have resistance to cold and fire damage.

entries.name: Undead
entries: When you take damage that isn't radiant, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by an amount equal to half your sorcerer level.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Vengeful Summons
entries: Beginning at 18th level, your magic has become powerful enough that you can call and command a servant of those that cursed you. Choose one of the following creatures as a representative for your curse based on the choice you made with your Blood Ties feature: {@creature lamia} or {@creature troll} (fey only), {@creature barbed devil} or {@creature incubus}/{@creature succubus} (fiend only), {@creature ghost} or {@creature wraith} (undead only).

You can use an action and spend 5 sorcery points to summon your chosen creature. The creature appears in an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet, and disappears when it drops to 0 hit points, you use this feature to summon another creature, or after 10 minutes have passed.

Roll initiative for the creature, which has its own turns. When you summon it and on each of your turns thereafter, you can issue a verbal command to it (requiring no action on your part), telling it what it must do on its next turn. If you issue no command, it spends its turn attacking any creature within reach.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Apocalypse Sorcery
entries: {@i Hasten or Stall the End of the World}
Apocalypse Sorcerers have seen the shape of things to come. They may have visions of the Great Beast ushering in the end of Etharis or dreams of Gormadraug waking and devouring the land.

These prophecies besiege Apocalypse Sorcerers, plaguing and empowering in equal measure. Some find relief in putting these revelations into writing, producing texts that read as incoherent but slowly seep into the mind as sensible, even inevitable. When the apocalypse-bringer is freed to travel across Etharis unburdened, undoing the works of gods and men, magic will swell and pool, ripe for the taking. This sign of the end is also their gift.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bear Witness
entries: You have prepared your entire life for the end of the world. While your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Apocalyptic Inurement
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Force damage.

entries.name: Recite Scripture
entries: Once per active Innate Sorcery, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you can use a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} that has a spell with a casting time of {@variantrule Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Unflappable
entries: You are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Apocrypha
entries: Your obsessive reflections on the end of existence inspire your writing. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can create one {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} at no cost. It must be a spell of level 5 or lower that you can cast. This {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} disintegrates when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Forbidden Magic
entries: The end of Etharis is a time when magic is unbound and magical powers long hidden are unearthed. When you cast a Sorcerer spell using a spell slot, you can choose one option below.

entries.name: Excessive
entries: If the spell requires a Material component with a cost, you can cast the spell without the Material component. You take Force damage equal to four times the level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}

entries.name: Inexorable
entries: Taking damage can't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB} on the spell. When the spell ends, you gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level.

entries.name: Pyrrhic
entries: If the spell requires an attack roll, the spell automatically hits and the attack roll is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by an amount equal to four times the level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum returns to normal.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: The End is Nigh
entries: You loudly proclaim what will come to pass when the world ends. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you describe the end of days. When you do so, each creature of your choice in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 6d6} Psychic damage and {@damage 6d6} Force damage and has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only. A {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition on a successful save. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the creature can be revived only by a {@spell True Resurrection|XPHB} or a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you spend 6 Sorcery Points (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bulwark Warrior
entries: {@i Provoke Your Enemies, Protect Your Allies}

Those who learn the fighting prowess of the Bulwark Warrior Warriors protect their allies from certain death. With endurance and strength as their primary skills, these warriors are prepared to take lethal strikes for their companions.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Threatening Presence
entries: You can provoke your enemies into single-minded hatred of you. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, each creature of your choice that can hear you in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 5d6} Psychic damage and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against targets other than you. When you use this feature, you restore your use of Weather the Storm.
You can use this feature twice. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
When you reach Fighter level 15, you gain another use of this feature.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Aggressive Defense
entries: You know when to switch from defense to offense. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can lose {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to no more than half your Fighter level (round down) to deal extra damage to the target equal to the number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} lost in this way.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Improved Second Wind
entries: Your endurance is unrivaled. When you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} from Second Wind, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the roll's total.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Halt the Assault
entries: When another creature you can see within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to change the target to yourself. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage against that attack.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Carver Guild
entries: {@i Slay Monsters Fearlessly and Recklessly}

Since the beginning of time, the brave glared into danger's ferocious eyes and fought monsters. Those who survived were the ones smart enough to arm themselves properly and know precisely where to strike—or those who knew when to flee and return with a new plan.

Members of the Carver Guild are the Monster Hunters typically called upon when immediate danger threatens a settlement and there is no army or militia available. Carvers stride unflinchingly toward death, armed with years of training and the knowledge passed down from those before them.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: True Grit
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, and you are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition caused by creature types in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1}.

Additionally, when you hit a creature with an attack as part of a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can choose a {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature within 60 feet that can see you (including yourself). The condition ends on that creature.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Terrorize the Terrors
entries: Your reputation has become such that monsters preying on the fearful have come to fear you. When you hit a creature with an attack as part of a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. The DC for the saving throw equals 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Deadly Redirect
entries: Your strikes have become even deadlier. The extra damage of your Close Quarters increases to {@dice 3d6}. In addition, if you deal damage to a creature with Close Quarters, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all attack rolls until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Controlled Footwork
entries: You are such an effective combatant that you are always in control and never off balance. You can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} twice in a round instead of once.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Circle of Blood
entries: {@i Wreak Bloody Havoc}

The Circle of Blood is a keeper of the old ways. They remember how ancient Druids performed sacrificial rituals under a blood-red moon to appease the uncaring forces of nature. These Druids trade blood for life in a delicate balance to bolster their allies and destroy their enemies.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Blood Boon
entries: Whenever a creature you can see within 60 feet of you is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to claim the last vestiges of its vitality. You regain 1 spent {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die} and grant a creature you can see within 60 feet of you {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Druid level.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once). You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Blood Lust
entries: While your Blood Moon is active, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Improved Violent Strikes
entries: The extra Necrotic damage from your Violent Strikes increases to {@dice 2d6}.

items.name: Red Rage
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Exsanguinate
entries: When you use your Blood Boon, you regain spent {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} equal to half your Druid level and give {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Druid level to a number of creatures up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one creature) that you can see within 60 feet of yourself.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Circle of Entropy
entries: {@i Become an Instrument of Decay and Ruin}

Druids of the Circle of Entropy see doom as a constant of the natural world. Lives end, works erode, and the civilizations of Etharis ultimately come to ruin. The inevitable end of the old brings opportunity for the new. These fatalistic Druids see themselves as agents of ruin, ending those whose time has passed to make space for those whose time has yet to come.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Many Roads to Ruin
entries: Your mystic connection to catastrophe and destruction grows stronger. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Elemental Assault
entries: While your Ruin Incarnate feature is active, whenever you hit with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can cause it to deal your choice of Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Necrotic damage rather than its normal damage type.

entries.name: Increased Might
entries: While your Ruin Incarnate feature is active, you can add your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1) to your Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Shake the Earth
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can strike the earth with a thunderous tremor and grow. When you do so, your size increases by one category (from Medium to Large, for example) for 10 minutes. In addition, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from your new form must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. The tremor deals Bludgeoning damage to each structure in contact with the ground in the area. To determine this damage, roll a number of d10s equal to your Druid level, and add them together.
While your size is increased by this feature, your attacks with weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal an extra {@damage 1d4} damage on a hit.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Entropy's Apex
entries: You have mastered the ability to hasten the inevitable slide toward entropy. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Enhanced Ruinous Smite
entries: Until the end of your next turn, any creature affected by your Ruinous Smite suffers a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19-20 on the {@dice d20}.

entries.name: Improved Inexorable Onslaught
entries: While your Ruin Incarnate feature is active, you can attack with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} three times instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

entries.name: World Breaker
entries: You regain your use of your Shake the Earth feature when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Circle of Mutation
entries: {@i Mutate Into an Apex Predator}

Druids of the Circle of Mutation believe that nature should be improved in order to compete with the unnatural world. Their order hides in the darkest corners of swamps and forests, conducting experiments to warp the structure of their domain. They go unheard from for months, emerging from the wilds with twisted vines and mutated creatures at their side. These Druids have earned the scorn of other circles, discredited as those who have lost their way. In the eyes of these Druids, those who wish to preserve nature as it is simply fear what change brings.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Unnatural and Unnerving
entries: When you expend a level 2+ spell slot to gain Mutation Points, you regain one expended spell slot. The slot you regain must be of a level lower than the slot you expended and can't be higher than level 5.
In addition, while in Wild Shape form, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Unnatural Attacks
entries: Each of your attacks in Wild Shape form can deal its normal damage type or Force damage. You make this choice each time you hit with those attacks.

entries.name: Unnerving Aura
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} or {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) and Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}) checks.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Endless Evolution
entries: When you gain Mutation Points, you gain an additional number of Mutation Points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). In addition, you can now spend your Mutation Points on the following Mutations.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Apex Predator
entries: Your mastery of mutation has made you an apex predator, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Evolved Attacks
entries: Once per turn, you can deal an extra {@damage 2d10} Force damage to a target you hit with a Wild Shape form's attack.

entries.name: Mutate Beasts
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can touch a Beast and expend a spell slot, causing the target to mutate. You gain Mutation Points equal to the slot's level, which you must immediately spend on Mutations for the Beast. Unspent Mutation Points are lost. Mutations remain until the Beast is targeted by this feature again. A {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB}, {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} or similar magic ends the Mutations.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: College of Adventurers
entries: {@i Be a Master of Classes}

Bards from the College of Adventurers learn from heroes of old and stories of legend. Bards are jacks of all trades, and, for the College of Adventurers, this statement rings even truer. They combine all the skills of their companions into one, allowing them to be versatile and supportive. While not having a direct goal, many adventurer-studying Bards live to tell tales of other heroes or seek to create their own. Stories of great deeds, of desperate cunning, of magical anomalies, or of godly might fuel these Bards.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Well-Rounded
entries: You gain proficiency with one type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice, you gain proficiency in one skill of your choice, and you know one language of your choice.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Improvisational Talent
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can choose one adventurer's talent you know and replace it with one you don't.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: College of Fools
entries: {@i Laugh at Your Foes' Terror}

It's commonly believed the College of Fools is merely a front for a cult of Beleth. Bards in the College would say their relationship with the Arch Daemon of Fear is much more complicated. These Bards choose to laugh at Etharis's many horrors rather than be dismayed by them—a whimsical, if ghoulish, philosophy. Their delight in other creatures' terror encourages their obscene antics and cruel jests. One person's trick is another person's terror, after all.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Gallows Humor
entries: When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or killed outright, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to regain an expended use of your Bardic Inspiration. When you do so, choose a creature within 30 feet of you that can hear and understand you. That creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or gain the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn. If the creature succeeds on the Wisdom saving throw, you regain the use of this ability. Otherwise, once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Last Laugh
entries: When you become {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} or take damage while you are {@condition Bloodied|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to regain all expended Bardic Inspiration dice and break out into a cackling fit of fatalistic glee at your own impending doom. For 1 minute, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage. Also, when a creature within 60 feet of you hits you with an attack roll, you can expend up to three Bardic Inspiration dice to force the attacker to make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the creature takes Psychic damage equal to the total rolled on the Bardic Inspiration dice plus your Charisma modifier.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: College of Requiems
entries: {@i Sing the Songs of the Dead}

Performing macabre melodies filled with grief-stricken chords and mournful refrains, the College of Requiems stirs the very bones of the dead. Requiem Bards weave necromantic magic into their funerary songs to control and empower a host of Undead minions.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Stir the Bones
entries: You always have the {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} spell prepared. It counts as a Bard spell for you.

When you expend a use of Bardic Inspiration, choose Undead creatures under your control within 60 feet of yourself, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). The chosen creatures each gain a Bardic Inspiration die. These extra Bardic Inspiration dice do not count against your limit.

When an Undead creature under your control expends a Bardic Inspiration die on an attack roll, it can also add the number rolled on the Bardic Inspiration die to the attack's damage roll if that attack hits.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dual Death
entries: When you cast a Necromancy spell that targets only one creature, you can have it target a second creature within range.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending one use of your Bardic Inspiration dice (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Daemonologist
entries: {@i Steal Scraps of Divine and Infernal Power}

Through theological study, or perhaps an induction into a secretive cabal, Daemonologists have learned to cast divine magic without the need for faith or bargains. Their spellbooks are scribed with prayer fragments and blasphemous hymns, enabling them to siphon scraps of power from both Arch Seraphs and Arch Daemons. From their heretical research, they've come to believe such otherworldly beings are two sides of the same divine kin.
Daemonology is rarely practiced. If the nature of their abilities is discovered, they risk being persecuted not only by superstitious folk but also by celestial and infernal powers.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Borrowed Tongues and Hides
entries: Your ability to siphon power from Celestials and Fiends is enhanced. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Arch Daemon Boon
entries: While you are siphoning power from Arch Daemons, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage. In addition, Fiends that know languages can understand your speech and you can understand theirs, even if you do not share a language.

entries.name: Arch Seraph Boon
entries: While you are siphoning power from Arch Seraphs, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Radiant damage. In addition, Celestials that know languages can understand your speech and you can understand theirs, even if you do not share a language.

entries.name: Switch Sides
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can change which power you are siphoning from. Once you switch, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Unearthly Countenance
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you adopt an infernal or celestial countenance for 10 minutes. For the duration, your appearance gains aspects of the power you choose. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Commanding Presence
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks.

entries.name: Improved Spells
entries: When you expend a spell slot to cast a spell from the Arch Daemon or Arch Seraph table, the spell is cast as if you had spent a spell slot of one level higher.

entries.name: Unearthly Wings
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 60 feet.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Eternal War Eruption
entries: You use the powers at your command to call forth warring celestials and infernals. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you summon a manifestation of the war between Arch Daemons and Arch Seraphs in a 30-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point within 120 feet of yourself.

Each creature in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} must make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d10} Necrotic damage, {@damage 4d10} Radiant damage, and has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.
As part of the same action, you can change the power you are siphoning from, and you also regain 1 Wizard spell slot of your choice of 5th level or lower.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Devourer Guild
entries: {@i Gain Power by Consuming Monster Flesh}

Folk in Etharis don't always speak highly of Monster Hunters, and many consider them to be just as depraved and inhuman as the evils they vanquish. Many of the appalling tales about Monster Hunters can be attributed, directly or indirectly, to the Devourer Guild, who are accused of being monstrous cannibals.

The truth is barely any better. Devourers have spent their days consuming the flesh and blood of the monsters they slay, and, over time, their metabolism has changed to tolerate this disgusting practice. Devourers adopt mutations shortly after consuming their prey.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Synchronized Response
entries: Your ingestion of monsters heightens your understanding of them and their behaviour. You gain this additional effect when you consume a monster portion: For 1 minute, when you make an attack as part of a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you deal an extra {@damage 1d6} damage. This damage has the same type as the weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} used for the attack.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Gnawing Hunger
entries: Your hunger for your enemy allows you to partake of its essence during battle. When you deal damage to a creature with a melee attack using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the damage dealt. If the target is a creature type in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1}, you instead gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage dealt instead.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Alchemical Decoctions
entries: You can spend 1 hour and 20 GP worth of alchemical ingredients (such as special herbs or monster salvage) to use your {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} to convert a monster portion into a decoction. A decoction is a magic potion that grants the benefits of a consumed monster portion. You can have 4 unconsumed decoctions active. You can destroy a decoction as a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action.

A creature other than you can consume 1 decoction without adverse effects. A creature gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level for each decoction it consumes after the first. A creature must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before it regains the ability to safely consume a decoction.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Acquired Taste
entries: Your hunger for monster portions has increased to the point of being insatiable. You can now consume 1 additional portion safely. Additionally, for 1 minute when you consume a portion, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, on attack rolls made as part of a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

name: Eldritch Domain
subclassFeatures: Sing the Song that Ends the World|Cleric|XPHB|Eldritch|GrimHollowPG24|17

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Eldritch Domain
entries: {@i Wield the Power that Killed the Gods}

Even the most benevolent divine beings operate outside the bounds of mortal comprehension. These eldritch forces sing a siren song that calls to mortal worshippers through lucid dreams and terrible whispers. The Eldritch Domain empowers the followers of the unknown and distant forces of chaos, divine entities of eldritch oblivion, and dead gods.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Otherworldly Calm
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage and {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions.

Additionally, your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it. The attempt automatically fails, and the creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or take Psychic damage equal to your Cleric level.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sing the Song that Ends the World
entries: When a creature fails a Wisdom saving throw against your Prophecy of Doom feature, you can deal {@damage 10d10} Psychic damage to it. Once a creature takes damage in this way, it is immune to this effect for 10 minutes, after which it can be affected again.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Green Reaper
entries: {@i Slay with Nature's Venom}

Green Reapers are assassins who specialize in harnessing the toxic elements of flora and fauna. These Rangers often work as killers for hire utilizing their extensive knowledge to end lives discreetly or with gory panache, depending on the poison used and the client's wishes. Green Reapers exhibit a morbid curiosity when encountering a toxin they're unfamiliar with, typically followed by an enthusiastic application of the substance on their next foe.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Poison Control
entries: You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

In addition, you can cast the {@spell Protection from Poison|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot. You can do so a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Variegated Vexations
entries: Whenever you would deal Poison damage with a weapon attack, you can change that damage to be either Acid or Necrotic instead.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Pain Tolerance
entries: You have learned to quickly inure yourself against harm. Immediately before you take damage from a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage you take. If any of these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} remain at the end of your next turn, they vanish.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Haunted Sorcery
entries: {@i Commune with the Dead}

Unlike other Sorcerers, the circumstances of your birth were mundane and you have no arcane inheritance passed down from strange ancestors. Instead, you gained your sorcerous powers after you survived an experience that left you near death. Since that experience, you've had a preternatural sense for danger and a ghostly companion that either can't, or won't, leave you alone. Some Haunted, as Sorcerers who share your origin are called, develop cordial relationships with their phantom, while others find their spectral companion to be a relentless nuisance.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Strength of Spirit
entries: Your bond with your phantom companion empowers it. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your familiar's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by four times your Sorcerer level.
You can cast spells as if you were in the familiar's space.
When you use your action to cast a spell, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to command your phantom companion to use its Life Drain attack with its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Deathly Pallor
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage, and when you cast a Sorcerer spell that deals damage, it can deal your choice of Necrotic damage or its normal damage type.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Phantom Possession
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can direct your phantom companion to possess a creature of your choice within 5 feet of your phantom. The target makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, your phantom companion enters the target's body for 1 minute. On a successful save, the target resists the efforts to possess it, and your familiar can't possess it again for 24 hours.

Once the phantom companion possesses a creature's body, it controls that creature. The familiar's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and senses are replaced by the creature's. The phantom companion otherwise keeps its game statistics.

While the target is possessed, you have a telepathic link with your phantom companion as long as the two of you are within 100 feet. You can use this telepathic link to issue commands to your phantom companion (no action required) unless you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. Your phantom companion does its best to obey on its turn. If it completes an order and doesn't receive further direction from you, the phantom companion acts and moves as it likes, focusing on protecting itself.
You can command the target to take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} but must take your own {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to do so.
Whenever the target takes damage, it repeats the save, ending the possession on itself on a success, and your phantom companion reappears in the closest unoccupied space.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Become Death
entries: You can transmute your physical form into a spectral one when near death. When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead and gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum. At the start of each of your turns, you lose 10 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} and creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you take 10 Necrotic damage. While you have {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} granted by this feature, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage, a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet, can {@variantrule Hover|XPHB}, and you can move through occupied spaces as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. If you end your turn in such a space, you are shunted to the last unoccupied space you were in.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Highway Rider
entries: {@i A Steed Makes the Best Partner in Crime}

Stalking the backroads, the Highway Rider strikes fear into the heart of every traveler and penny-pinching merchant. They run down their prize astride a swift and loyal steed—and then make a quick getaway.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Horse Lord
entries: You can spend 1 minute grooming and caring for your mount, at the end of which it gains a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Rogue level.

In addition, your cunning extends to your steed. While you control a mount, it can take one of the following actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}: {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Dodge|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: True Grit
entries: You gain proficiency in Constitution saving throws. In addition, when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Desperado
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can use your Hair Trigger feature immediately before you fall {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Inquisition Domain
entries: {@i Cleanse the Heretics}
The Inquisition Domain reflects the order of the multiverse and the rejection of tainted magic—so far as certain celestial powers see it. Only the divine casters are pure and fit for use.

Since arcane magic is strong enough to challenge the gods, divine beings of this domain, such as the Arch Seraph Empyreus, demand magic-using mortals be kept in check. Most zealots root out all arcanists, while some strike fragile truces when complete removal isn't feasible.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Rebuke Invoker
entries: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} in response to a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself using a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast a spell, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 1d8} Force damage, plus another {@dice 1d8} per level of the spell slot the creature expended. Cantrips are considered level 1 spells for this ability. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage instead.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once). You regain all expended uses of this feature when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Supernal Safeguard
entries: Spell Shield can target a number of creatures up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one creature).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Living Crucible
entries: {@i Enhance Your Martial Prowess with Alchemy}

Fighters who become Living Crucibles have discovered an external means of power. While most Fighters train in martial traditions or study the art of war, Living Crucibles hone their craft of alchemy to endure compounds poisonous to others. In exchange for this rigorous physical and mental preparation, these Fighters are able to temporarily push their bodies past their natural limits. Under the influence of their alchemical compounds, these warriors can see in darkness, enhance their speed, inure themselves to magical attacks, and more.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Living Cauldron
entries: The number of compounds you can safely consume increases to three plus your Constitution modifier (minimum one).
At Fighter level 18, the number of compounds you can safely consume increases to five plus your Constitution modifier (minimum one).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Rapid Consumption
entries: When you use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to drink a compound, you can drink a second compound.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Toxin Transmutation
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage. Also, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on yourself.

When you end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on yourself in this way, you can choose to gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Fighter level. You regain the ability to gain these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} after completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Living Catalyst
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one compound you know with another one.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Misfortune Bringer
entries: {@i Curse Those You're About to Strike}

You've matched your penchant for illicit activities with the ability to mark your enemies for mishap and misfortune. Whether you were imbued with magic by spending time among the Fey or you learned the art of cursing from a long line of hedge Wizards, you are a Misfortune Bringer. Although not universal, many Misfortune Bringers possess heterochromia iridum—eyes of two different colors—and they use only one when glaring at targets they intend to curse.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Steal Luck
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself is about to make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to prevent the roll from being affected by {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. When you do so, you regain 1 expended Jinx Point.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Curse Caster
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and spend 3 Jinx Points to cast {@spell Bestow Curse|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Improved Steal Luck
entries: You can use your Steal Luck feature three times, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Nightwatcher
entries: {@i Take Back the Night}

Nightwatchers come from humble origins, often toiling as guards or investigators. Undaunted by dangers in the darkness, they stand firm against the growing night. Ever vigilant, they use the darkness to surprise and overwhelm foes much greater than themselves.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Size Up
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you assess a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, when that creature makes an attack roll against you or another creature within 5 feet of you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on that roll and give {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Night Stalker
entries: You are adept at tracking down enemies in the dead of night, giving you these benefits.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet for 10 minutes. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Slippery
entries: {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} against you. While entirely within {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, your movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Ready for Action
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10. When you roll 18-20 on an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll, you can take one additional action, except the {@action Magic|XPHB} action, on your first turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Beat Down
entries: Immediately after you miss a creature under the effect of your Size Up feature with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a melee attack against that creature if it's within range. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the new attack roll against that creature.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Oath of Pestilence
entries: {@i Gain Strength Through Suffering}

Clad in grime-soaked armor and wielding rusting weapons, Oath of Pestilence Paladins spread corruption, disease, and filth. Bound by an oath that infests their bodies with all manner of plagues, these heralds of decay lumber forward with unholy toughness and grim resolve.
These Paladins share the following tenets:

items: Spread plague to foster strength in the survivors.
There is nothing unnatural or immoral about the ending of life.
Might makes right.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Aura of Rampant Sickness
entries: You emit an aura of contagion and virulence. When a creature within your Aura of Protection is about to make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on that {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Disgusting Resilience
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can spend any number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice}, roll them, and reduce the damage taken by the total rolled on those dice.

In addition, if you are killed, your corpse explodes in a shower of pus and gore. Each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you makes Constitution saving throw gainst the Paladin's spell save DC, taking {@damage 8d6} Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Plaguebringer
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain the benefits below for 10 minutes, or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: One with Plague
entries: You are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Poison damage and the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition, and you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Bolstered by Rot
entries: Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum can't be reduced.

entries.name: Entropic Radiance
entries: Whenever an enemy starts its turn within your Aura of Protection, it takes Necrotic damage equal to your Charisma modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Oath of Slaughter
entries: {@i Revel in Unbridled Violence}

The only truth of war is death. The only virtue is to kill. The only victory is to survive. Heroism, honor, and glory are illusions. This is the creed of Tormach, Arch Daemon of Wrath, but this philosophy rings true for all warriors who devote themselves, body and soul, to the thrill of combat and the delight of bloodshed. Such champions find themselves at the forefront of armies, using the most violent methods at their disposal to bring battles to a swift close... or drawing out the war to sate their own appetites.
Paladins who take the Oath of Slaughter share the following tenets:

items: Violence is the end, not the means.
Break the body to break the spirit.
Revel in bloodshed, whether friend or foe.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bloodthirst Aura
entries: Your lust for blood infects those around you. When a {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} ally within your Aura of Protection makes an attack with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, it gains a bonus to damage. The bonus equals your Charisma modifier.

Additionally, when a {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} creature within your Aura of Protection makes a saving throw against a {@filter Sangromancy spell|spells|subschool=sangromancy}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the save.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Follow Through
entries: When a creature in your Aura of Protection becomes {@condition Bloodied|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and make an attack with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. This movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Blood Knight
entries: Your bloodthirst imbues you with preternatural strength and resilience, allowing you to keep sowing slaughter. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Crimson Armor
entries: When a creature within your Aura of Protection becomes {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} by an enemy, you gain 30 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Seeing Red
entries: When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make one melee attack against that creature, using a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: Wanton Slaughter
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can choose any number of creatures within 5 feet of the original target and within your reach. Each chosen creature takes Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Oath of Zeal
entries: {@i Eliminate Threats to Ideological Purity}

The Oath of Zeal is taken by paladins consumed by hatred for a specific group or ideology. Zealots, as these Paladins are sometimes called, pursue an inquisition against their enemies at all costs. They abandon compassion and honor as impediments to the more important work of ridding the world of those they deem dangerous or heretical.
These Paladins share the following tenets:

items: Reveal heresy and destroy those who practice it.
Show unwavering conviction and unflinching resolve.
Perform any sacrifice necessary to stop wickedness.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Aura of Clarity
entries: You and your allies have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a {@condition Blinded|XPHB} ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there. Additionally, you can see {@condition Invisible|XPHB} creatures within your Aura of Protection.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Compel Confession
entries: You can cast {@spell Zone of Truth|XPHB} without expending a spell slot. In addition, a creature that succeeds on its saving throw takes {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage at the start of each of its turns while in your Zone of Truth until it chooses to fail its saving throw instead.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Apocalyptic Revelation
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can reveal the true nature of your enemies for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required). You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Blinding Glory
entries: Enemies that start their turn within 5 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw against the Paladin's spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: See the Truth
entries: You have {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Smite the Heretic
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can choose a creature within 60 feet of yourself and reveal its weaknesses. You and your allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against that creature.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Occultist Guild
entries: {@i Hunt Mages and Magical Adversaries}

In Etharis, there are those who fear magic, and those who seek to understand it. Monster Hunters from the Occultist Guild know folk from both sides are equally dangerous. An Occultist investigates the arcane, the supernatural, and the uncanny, while avoiding the influence of superstition or ideology. Despite their reputation as mage hunters, Occultists don't burn their enemies at the stake—Occultists put them to the sword, as that's what swords are for. Knowledge and magic give Occultists an edge over their mystical adversaries. Their spells are used to detect and defend against dangerous arcana, and, above all, magic is used to destroy monsters that can't be harmed by steel.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mage Hunter
entries: You consider Humanoids that can cast spells as being a creature type in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1}.

Additionally, when you damage a creature type in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1} that is {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating}, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw it makes to maintain its {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Occult Knowledge
entries: Your knowledge of magic has increased so that you learn to cast Rituals. You can cast any spell as a {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} if that spell has the {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} tag and it's a spell you have prepared.

In addition, you learn two spells of your choice. These spells can come from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list or any combination thereof (see a class's section for its spell list). A spell you choose must have the {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} tag.

When you reach Monster Hunter level 14, you can replace one of the spells you know from this feature with another spell of your choice from any spell list. The new spell must have the {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} tag.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Magical Aegis
entries: You gain the ability to extend a protective charm. You radiate an unseeable aura in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that originates from you. The aura is inactive while you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. You and allies in your aura have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells cast by creature types in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1}.

Additionally, you always have the {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} spell prepared. You can cast {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot. Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Response
entries: You have learned to anticipate your enemies well enough to rapidly cast spells in response to their attacks. When you use {@classFeature Studied Response|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|2}, you can cast a spell. The spell must have a casting time of an action and must target only that creature.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Path of the Fractured
entries: {@i Two Personalities Are Better than One}

Barbarians are defined by their rage, channeling it to unleash brief but potent destruction. Few are brave or unwise enough to study esoteric psychological techniques that split their rage from the rest of their psyche, dividing their identity into two parts: ego and id. When their ego is in control, the Fractured—as these Barbarians are known—possess self-control and cunning beyond most other Barbarians. When they allow their id to take control, their countenance turns monstrous and their bodies swell with the power of rage made physically manifest.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Brains and Brawn
entries: While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is not active, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to every damage type except Force and Psychic.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Cunning and Brutal
entries: While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is not active, you can take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} or {@action Help|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, your attack rolls with {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Better Half
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead, and you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum. In addition, if your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} ends. If your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} was not active, you immediately activate your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} (even if you have no remaining uses of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1}). If any of these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} remain after 1 minute, they vanish.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Path of the Primal Spirit
subclassFeatures: Path of the Primal Spirit|Barbarian|XPHB|Primal Spirit|GrimHollowPG24|3

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Path of the Primal Spirit
entries: {@i Rage Alongside a Bestial Spirit}

Many Barbarians are in tune with the natural world, but few are as mystically intertwined with it as those who walk the Path of the Primal Spirit. These Barbarians forge powerful connections with beasts and nature spirits, inspiring such ethereal beings to manifest and journey on far-flung adventures.

Barbarians who follow this path have a deep reverence for the cycle of the natural world. Such Barbarians are as likely to accept quests and pleas for aid from local wildlife as they are from people. This respect for animals and spirits doesn't cross into naivety—few understand the delicate balance between the needs of predator and prey better than those who walk the Path of the Primal Spirit.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Kin to Beasts
entries: You always have the {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB} and {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB} spells prepared. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either spell in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for them.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Skinrider's Trance
entries: You take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to enter a trance and choose your primal companion or one Beast currently under the effect of your {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB} spell within 60 feet of yourself. For the duration of this trance, you possess the chosen creature.

Once you possess a creature's body, you control it. Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and senses are replaced by the creature's. You otherwise keep your game statistics. This possession ends if you choose to exit the trance (no action required by you), if the Beast you're possessing is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, or if you and the Beast are on different planes of existence.

While in this trance, your body falls into a catatonic state. You can't move or take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}, and you're unaware of your surroundings. You can remain in the trance for a number of hours up to half your Barbarian level plus your Constitution modifier.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending one use of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Shape of the Wild
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can choose a new form for your primal companion, causing it to transform instantaneously. When you cause your primal companion to transform in this way, its current {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} change to its new {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending one use of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} (no action required).

name: Path of the Wrathful Dead
subclassFeatures: Path of the Wrathful Dead|Barbarian|XPHB|Wrathful Dead|GrimHollowPG24|3
Death Is but a Door|Barbarian|XPHB|Wrathful Dead|GrimHollowPG24|10

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Path of the Wrathful Dead
entries: {@i Channel the Rage of the Unquiet Dead}

Barbarians who walk the Path of the Wrathful Dead commune with the spirits of the deceased and channel their spectral powers. These Barbarians are often preoccupied with the dead whispering in their ears, which urge them to act upon the whims and emotions of the haunting spirits. Some who walk this path learn to master the powers gifted to them; others find they've become servants to the unending chorus clamoring for their attention.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dark Doom Revisited
entries: Once per active {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1}, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to channel a traumatic death. When you do, choose one of the following options.

entries.name: Contamination
entries: At the start of their turn, each creature of your choice in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take Poison damage and gain the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute.

To determine the Poison damage, roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and add them together. An affected creature can use an action to end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on itself.

entries.name: Hypothermia
entries: At the start of their turn, each creature of your choice in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take Cold damage and have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} halved for 1 minute.
To determine the Cold damage, roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and add them together. A creature can use an action to end this effect on itself.

entries.name: Immolation
entries: At the start of their turn, each creature of your choice in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take Fire damage.

To determine the Fire damage, roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and add them together. As an action, a creature can extinguish the fire on itself by giving itself the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and rolling on the ground. The fire also goes out if it is doused, submerged, or suffocated.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Death Is but a Door
entries: Your familiarity with death has left you resistant to its call. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Hard to Kill
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws}. In addition, you must fail four {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws} to die instead of three as normal.

entries.name: Return the Spirit
entries: You can call the spirits of the deceased to restore life essence to a nearby creature. You can cast the {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB}, {@spell Raise Dead|XPHB}, or {@spell Revivify|XPHB} spell without providing Material components. When you do, you gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level for {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB}, 2 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels for {@spell Revivify|XPHB}, and 3 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels for {@spell Raise Dead|XPHB}. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for this feature.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend two uses of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Powered by Pathos
entries: Your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is empowered by the overwhelming emotions of the unquiet dead. Your Final Night Catharsis feature grants an additional effect based on the chosen emotion.

entries.name: Hate
entries: While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, your attacks with weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}.

entries.name: Jealousy
entries: Whenever a creature you can see starts its turn within 30 feet of you while your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to summon spectral assailants to Grapple the creature. The creature makes a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failure, the creature has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition until the end of its turn. On a successful save, the creature is not {@condition Grappled|XPHB}; however, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot for that creature until the end of its turn.

entries.name: Terror
entries: Whenever a creature you can see starts its turn within 30 feet of you while your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make that creature terrified until the start of its next turn. A terrified creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved and {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Plague Doctor
entries: {@i Plague Your Enemies with Magical Concoctions}

Blending spellcasting with science, you distill your magic into concoctions that harm or heal. Plague Doctors often wear grotesque masks protecting them from their toxic ingredients. Many fearfully regard the mask as a sign of pestilence, making Plague Doctors a source of both hope and trepidation.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bad Medicine
entries: When you craft a potion, you can choose to expend a spell slot without choosing a spell to craft a dose of Bad Medicine. When you create a dose, choose one effect per level of the spell slot expended.

items: The creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.
The creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved.
The creature takes an extra {@damage 1d4} Necrotic damage the first time it takes damage each turn.
The creature takes {@damage 1d6} Poison damage each time it takes an action, {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.
The creature takes Acid damage equal to the level of the spell slot expended at the start of each of its turns.

entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can hurl a dose of Bad Medicine at a point you can see within 30 feet. Creatures within 10 feet of that point must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target suffers one of the chosen effects for 1 minute. On each of its turns, the target can take an action and repeat the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Breathe It In
entries: Being persistently exposed to the deadliest ailments known has given you some small measure of resistance.
