entries: You can cast {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} or {@spell Revivify|XPHB} without a spell slot or components. When you cast {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} using this relic, all previous Undead created using this relic crumble into dust.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Magic Item Collection
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can magically produce a magic item. When you do so, all magic items previously created by this feature vanish. If a magic item you produce requires {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you can attune yourself to it the instant you produce it. You can produce the following magic items: a {@item Carpet of Flying|XDMG}, a {@item Cloak of the Bat|XDMG}, a {@item Flame Tongue|XDMG}, {@item Gauntlets of Ogre Power|XDMG}, an {@item Daern's Instant Fortress|XDMG|Instant Fortress}, a {@item Ring of Regeneration|XDMG}, a {@item Ring of Telekinesis|XDMG}, a {@item Sun Blade|XDMG}, or a {@item Wand of Wonder|XDMG}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Soul Jar
entries: You've secured the crown jewel of your collection: a lich's soul jar, or "phylactery." Though the original owner's soul has been expelled from this accursed artifact, it retains many of its magical properties.

This magic item is always attuned to you and doesn't count against your total number of attuned magic items. It has 5 charges and regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the soul jar, you can expend one or more charges to use the following abilities.

entries.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: You can expend 1 charge as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Investigator level.

entries.name: Trinket Recharge
entries: You can expend 1 charge as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to regain one expended use of your {@classFeature Trinkets|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|3}.

entries.name: Undead Fortitude
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can expend 2 charges to drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead. You can use this benefit only once per turn.

entries.name: Draining Touch
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 3 charges to make a melee spell attack. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 8d8} Necrotic damage and you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the Necrotic damage dealt. If the spell attack misses, these charges aren't expended.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Apothecary
entries: {@i Heal the Sick and Wounded}

Many practically minded Alchemists assume the role of the Apothecary, for adventuring parties always need a healer and Clerics are often in short supply. During their downtime, such Alchemists have a marketable skill to depend upon for income and can do an indisputable amount of good with their knowledge. Apothecaries constantly study potions and herbology, preferring to learn how to mend the body, rather than destroy it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Concentrated Healing
entries: When a creature regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} as a result of drinking one of your potions, it can choose up to half of the potion's dice after rolling them and maximize the number rolled on each die.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Alchemical Resurrection
entries: If you administer a {@item Potion of Superior Healing|XDMG} or a {@item Potion of Supreme Healing|XDMG} to a creature that has been dead for no longer than 24 hours, the creature returns to life with 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Miracle Serum
entries: Whenever a creature drinks one of your potions and regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} until the start of its next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dynamo Engineer
entries: {@i Build Gadgets for Arcane Magic}

If the energy of magic could be captured within physical substance, there would be no need for magic-users. Some Alchemists have founded their careers on this notion, inventing and iterating upon small devices known as Spell Dynamos which store and manipulate arcane energy. These dynamos can be configured to store their energy at a specific resonance, such that, when it is released, it perfectly replicates the effect of a spell. Indeed, these few Alchemists have begun to brave the frontier of spellcasting without an ounce of arcane talent; just a knack for tinkering and endless inventiveness.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcano Bomb [Formula]
entries: By adding an unexpended Spell Dynamo to your Bomb (and thus expending the dynamo's spell slot), you can change it into an Arcano Bomb. An Arcano Bomb deals Force damage instead of Fire damage, all of its damage dice are d12s, and it deals an extra {@damage 1d12} Force damage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Counter-Discharge
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself casts a spell that affects you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend a Spell Dynamo to release a wave of disruptive energy. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any saving throw you make against the spell and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to any damage it deals.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Recycler
entries: Immediately after a creature casts a spell that targets you or includes you in its area of effect, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to capture the essence of the spell in an expended Spell Dynamo. If you don't have any expended dynamos, you can choose one to expend as a part of this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. You regain the use of this dynamo and it becomes configured to the spell, using the slot level at which it was cast. The spell doesn't need to be a Wizard spell or one for which you have spell slots.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Maesters' Guild
entries: {@i Craft an Arsenal of Magic Items}

While most seasoned spellcasters will enchant a handful of magic items over the course of their careers, artisans belonging to the Guild of Arcane Maesters seek to become true masters of magic item creation. They rightly take seriously the forging of such powerful relics: each creation must be a masterwork in its own right to contain the potent magic woven into them. Despite laboring for months or even years to perfect their creations, seasoned maesters are always seen to be laden with dozens of magic items, attuned to a handful of rings, and carrying a Wand of Magic Missiles, just in case.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Strike
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with a casting of one of your Wizard cantrips that has a casting time of an action or with taking the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to use a magic item that requires that action.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sever Connection
entries: When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to one magic item to create a shield of magical force. Until the start of your next turn, you have a bonus to AC equal to your Intelligence modifier, including against the triggering attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you. The number of magic items you can attune to is reduced by 1 until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Magic Item Recharge
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can recharge a number of magic items up to your Intelligence modifier that have charges or properties that recharge at the next dawn.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Archivist
entries: {@i Expand Your Rituals Through Ancient Lore}

Though most Investigators fill their grimoires with hard-won knowledge borne from encounters with supernatural threats, some prefer to do bookkeeping instead. Such Archivists seek to accumulate knowledge, more so than trinkets, by spending untold hours digging through disparate tomes of occult secrets and compiling them into encyclopedic texts. Through their research, Archivists become academic masters of the arcane and priceless reservoirs of obscure knowledge.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Erudite Spell
entries: When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can give one target of the spell {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saves against the spell.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Rushed Incantation|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|2} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Encyclopedic Expertise
entries: You can identify any arcane effect from memory. Whenever you see or hear a spell being cast or investigate a magical effect, you can identify the spell that was cast, the magic item responsible, or the creature that produced the effect without an ability check. This feature fails to identify spells, magic items, and creatures that are utterly unique or are otherwise not recorded in arcane texts.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Eidetic Memory
entries: You can effortlessly duplicate spells you see or hear, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Ritual Recall
entries: If you see or hear an Investigator spell being cast, you can thereafter copy it into your grimoire.

entries.name: Spell Duplication
entries: When you see or hear a spell of level 5 or lower being cast, you can fix the spell in your mind. Within the next minute, you can expend a use of your {@classFeature Rushed Incantation|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|2} to cast the spell without a spell slot. Once you use this benefit to cast a spell, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Armigers' Guild
entries: {@i Build Invulnerable Armor}
The Guild of Armigers devote their skills to the art of armor smithing, with the firm belief that the right plate in the right place can make a warrior invincible.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Shining Steel
entries: Your imposing, shining armor makes you a clear target for your foes. When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can challenge any number of creatures within 30 feet of yourself that can see you to battle. Each creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on any attack roll against creatures other than you until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fortify
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can fortify your armor against attacks. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice, minimum of +1) and have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Masterwork Bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Colossal Slam
entries: When you use your Armored Slam, you deal an extra {@damage 2d10} Force damage, and a target that fails its saving throw against the slam has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. Additionally, you regain one expended use of Armored Slam when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Beastblood Guardian
entries: {@i Command the Fury of Beasts}

You have formed a bond with Beasts and have taken up the task of defending them. Your time among them has taught you their ferocity, tenacity, and animal instincts, allowing you to become a primal predator of the wilds.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Hunting Grounds
entries: You can move through the wilds as a Beast does, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Ignore Difficult Terrain
entries: {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} doesn't cost you extra movement.

entries.name: Climb and Swim Speed
entries: You have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} and a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Wild Pounce
entries: Once per turn when you hit a Large or smaller creature with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Slashing damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Aspect of the Beast
entries: You can assume the bloodthirsty visage of the Primal Beast. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain the benefits below for 1 minute or until you choose to end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Bloodied Frenzy
entries: While you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls.

entries.name: Bleeding Wounds
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can deal the target a bleeding wound. A creature with a bleeding wound can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and takes {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage for each of its wounds at the start of each of its turns. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}. A creature can take an action to staunch all of its bleeding wounds. A creature can have a maximum of six bleeding wounds at once.

entries.name: Furious Speed
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} doubles.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Big Game Hunter
entries: {@i Fire a Colossal Elephant Gun}

Armed with the largest guns possible, Big Game Hunters aim to bring down dangerous titans—such as dinosaurs, hydras, and giant beasts—before they can endanger smaller folk. Quarry as small as owlbears or as intelligent as giants are ill-suited to such as hunter's sensibilities, for they revel most in the conquest of titans and the smell of their Elephant Guns glowing red hot.

entries.subclassFeature: Broad Side of a Barn|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|Big Game Hunter|ValdaSpire24Extras|3

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Tracker
entries: You excel at trailing your quarry, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Footprint Identification
entries: By examining the footprints left behind by a creature as a {@action Study|XPHB} action, you can determine without an ability check the specific kind of creature that left it, how long ago it left the footprints, the creature's size, and whether the creature was missing any of its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} when it left the footprints.

entries.name: Survival Expertise
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Survival|XPHB} skill and you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} with that skill.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Legendary Shot
entries: When a creature you can see within 80 feet of you takes a Legendary Action, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an attack against it using your Elephant Gun. You can make this attack even if you've already made an attack using your Elephant Gun on your turn. On a hit, the Legendary Action is lost.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Exotic Caliber
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to chamber your Elephant Gun with one of the following types of ammunition. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending two Risk Dice (no action required).

entries.name: Buck Shot
entries: You load your Elephant Gun with dozens of lead pellets that scatter the next time the gun is fired. The attack becomes a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Each creature in the area makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Maneuver save DC, taking the Elephant Gun's damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Explosive Shot
entries: You load your Elephant Gun with a projectile that explodes the next time the gun is fired. The attack becomes an explosion. Choose a point you can see within 80 feet of you. Each creature within a 10-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Maneuver save DC, taking Fire damage equal to the damage of your Elephant Gun on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Piercing Shot
entries: You load your Elephant Gun with a conical projectile that penetrates through its target the next time the gun is fired. The attack becomes a 5-foot wide, 80-foot-long {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. Each creature in the area makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Maneuver save DC, taking the Elephant Gun's damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Black Magic
entries: {@i Wield the Dark Arts}

Black magic is associated with Hexes that cause suffering and spells that give rise to undeath. Harnessing such magic can lend you great power, but inevitably carries a cost. Darkness cannot be contained, after all; it merely seeps forth from wherever it is kept.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Undeath Command
entries: Your authority over Undead grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Quick Command
entries: When you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to command your familiar, you can use the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to issue a command to any Undead you control via the {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

entries.name: Undead Familiar
entries: Undead you control via the {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} spell gain the benefits of the Witch Familiar sidebar.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Life Tether
entries: When you take damage from a creature you can see within 60 feet, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to transfer some of that damage to a creature that is the sole target of your Hex. You take half the damage (round down) and the hexed creature takes the remaining damage.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Grim Sacrifice
entries: If your familiar is within 60 feet of yourself, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to dissolve its magical bond to this plane. Your familiar drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and unleashes necromantic energy in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. Each creature you choose within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature takes {@damage 8d10} Necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Black Rider
entries: {@i Command and Battle Atop a Skeletal Steed}

The rhythmic drumbeat of galloping hooves and the searing pinpoints of red eyes signal the arrival of a Black Rider. Such Necromancers embrace mounted combat, commanding their thralls from the back of a skeletal steed and terrorizing countrysides with unparalleled swiftness. Mastering this discipline means not only commanding an Undead mount, but also requires sure mastery over weapons while on horseback and on foot. However, the reward is immense: a Black Rider isn't a plodding marshal of shambling masses, but a wind of death that blows across the battlefield at a moment's notice.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

In addition, in place of one of those attacks, you can cast one of your cantrips that has a casting time of an action or, if you are riding a controlled mount, you can command your mount to take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an attack.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Gruesome Charge
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can give each of your thralls that isn't a controlled mount a spectral steed that it rides into combat. Each such thrall has a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 60 feet for 10 minutes.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dullahan [Lichdom]
entries: You have reached the pinnacle of Necromancy and transformed yourself into a lich. Through a vile ritual and a guillotine, you have severed your own head to act as your spirit jar, allowing you to see without eyes. Liches of your kind are known as dullahans or headless horsemen. You gain the following benefits in addition to those of your {@classFeature Lichdom|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|20} feature.

entries.name: Skull Jar
entries: Your spirit jar is your own magically preserved head. Even without your head, your senses aren't inhibited. You can see and hear from where your head once was and your disembodied voice booms from the stub of your neck.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: If you are carrying your skull jar, you have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet.

entries.name: Damage Resistance
entries: You and your mount have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

entries.name: Nightmare
entries: When you perform your {@classFeature Thralls|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|2|ValdaSpire24|Animate Thralls} ritual, you can summon a {@creature Nightmare|XMM}. You command this creature as your thrall and it counts as Undead for the purpose of your Necromancer features. In combat, it functions as an independent mount while you ride it (as defined in the rules on mounted combat).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bladeworkers' Guild
entries: {@i Craft Lethal Melee Weapons}
Blade and bow, axe and mace: these are the tools with which the Guild of Bladeworkers aim to change the world. They believe that the right blade in the right hand can make a warrior unstoppable.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Flex Grip
entries: During your turn, your reach is 5 feet greater with any Masterwork Melee weapon that has the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} or {@itemProperty V|XPHB|Versatile} property.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Defensive Disarm
entries: When a creature you can see within 5 feet of you makes an attack roll against you with a weapon, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to attempt to disarm the attacker. The target makes a Strength saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, it drops one item of your choice that it's holding. The object lands in a space you choose within 10 feet of the target. The target can replace the attack with one using a different weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}; otherwise the triggering attack misses.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Vicious Strike
entries: When you make an attack roll with a Melee weapon and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll, you can attempt a Vicious Strike. The attack roll instead has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. If this attack hits, it scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Blood Ascendant
entries: {@i Command the Powers of Vampirism}

Necromantic might comes in many forms, but a singular, ancient source is the blood curse of vampirism. Though it promises much—immortality, agility, charm—it comes paired with insidious drawbacks, from the stinging burn of sunlight to a perpetual thirst for blood. Necromancers that wish to capture a measure of this power without suffering its myriad weaknesses perform a special ritual with vampiric blood in order to become Blood Ascendants. In doing so, they fall deathly pale and lose their reflection within mirrors, but learn to slowly pry out vampiric powers without succumbing to the all-devouring curse.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Vampiric Transformation
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and expend 15 {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1} points to shape-shift into a bat or a cloud of mist. This transformation lasts for 1 hour or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition or you dismiss it (no action required). Your gear melds into the new form, and you can't use or otherwise benefit from your equipment while shape-shifted.

entries.name: Bat
entries: You transform into a bat. Your game statistics are replaced by the {@creature Bat|XMM} stat block, but you retain your creature type, {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, class features, languages, and feats.

entries.name: Mist
entries: You transform into a Medium cloud of mist. While shape-shifted, you can't speak, manipulate objects, or take any actions. You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 20 feet and can hover, and can enter and occupy the space of another creature. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, and {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws. You can pass through narrow openings, but treat liquid as though they were solid surfaces.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Children of the Night
entries: When you perform your {@classFeature Thralls|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|2|ValdaSpire24|Animate Thralls} ritual, you can summon one or more {@creature Wolf|XMM|Wolves}, {@creature Swarm of Bats|XMM|Swarms of Bats}, or {@creature Swarm of Rats|XMM|Swarms of Rats}. You command these creatures as your thralls and they count as Undead for the purpose of your Necromancer features.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Nosferatu [Lichdom]
entries: You have reached the pinnacle of Necromancy and transformed yourself into a lich. You have embraced the blood curse of vampirism to become a vampire lord in all but name: a nosferatu. You gain the following benefits in addition to those of your {@classFeature Lichdom|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|20} feature.

entries.name: Coffin Jar
entries: Your spirit jar is a coffin filled with grave dirt. When you drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you reform in your coffin after 1 hour. You are permanently weakened until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in the coffin. While weakened, your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced to 1, and you drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} if you begin your turn in sunlight.

entries.name: Regeneration
entries: At the start of each of your turns, you regain 10 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or are in sunlight.

entries.name: Spider Climb
entries: You can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check. Additionally, you gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your speed.

entries.name: Vampiric Speed
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Blood Magic
entries: {@i Fuel Your Curses with Blood}

Forbidden by most Witch covens, Blood Magic centers on the use of dark spells and Hexes that draw from the spellcaster's life essence. It is fundamentally more perilous than other Witch crafts, but its many risks come with copious rewards.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Deathseeker
entries: You can detect the location of each creature within 60 feet of you that is missing any of its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and you can see such a creature if it has the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks you make to track any creature that you or your familiar has damaged within the last 24 hours.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Hemomantic Recovery
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can perform a blood ritual to expend {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} and recover expended level 1-5 spell slots. The cost for each spell slot is given on the Hemomantic Recovery table.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sanguine
entries: When you cast a spell with a spell slot that deals damage to a creature that is the sole target of your Hex, you can choose to sacrifice your blood for power. You take 5 or more Necrotic damage and the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage for every 5 Necrotic damage you took, to a maximum of {@damage 6d8} Necrotic damage. This damage ignores your {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}, and bypasses your {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Blue Magic
entries: {@i Copy Any Spell That Affects You}

Compared to all other Witch's crafts, Blue Magic is unique, in that it reflects the essence of magic itself. Witches that specialize in Blue Magic absorb the energy of spells that affect them and let the arcana imprint upon their souls.

entries.name: True Blue Variant
entries: "True" Blue Magic Witches abandon the ability to prepare spells entirely. This variant allows a character to be fully shaped by their experiences and duplicate spells up to level 9.

True Blue Witches don't prepare additional spells after Witch level 1. Instead, each new spell must be prepared through {@subclassFeature Blue Magic Duplication|Witch|ValdaSpire24|Blue|ValdaSpire24Extras|3}.

As normal, a True Blue can't prepare more spells than listed in the Prepared Spells column of the Witch Features table. This number of prepared spells is increased by 4 at Witch level 3 (+4), and by 2 at Witch levels 5 (+6), 7 (+8), and 9 (+10).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Turquoise Efficiency
entries: You have greater mastery over spells you have prepared, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Prepared Advantage
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make against any spell that you have prepared.

entries.name: Siphon Spell
entries: If you succeed on a saving throw against a spell that you have prepared that is cast by another creature, you can regain an expended spell slot of the same level. Once you regain a spell slot with this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Copycat
entries: You can copy a creature's skills, in addition to its magic. When you see a creature within 60 feet of yourself makes an ability check using a skill or a saving throw in which it has proficiency, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to duplicate that proficiency. Until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you have proficiency in that skill or saving throw and can use the creature's bonus whenever you make that roll.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Cerulean Reflection
entries: When a creature casts a spell that forces you to make a saving throw to avoid damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to attempt to redirect some of the spell's energy to a new target. If you succeed on your saving throw against the spell, choose another creature you can see within the spell's range or up to 30 feet away from you, whichever is closer, to make a saving throw against the spell, using your spell save DC. The chosen creature can be the original spellcaster. On a failed save, the creature suffers the effects of the spell as if you had cast the spell and it had been the original target or been within the area of the spell.
You can use this feature and {@subclassFeature Blue Magic Duplication|Witch|ValdaSpire24|Blue|ValdaSpire24Extras|3} as a part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Brigand
entries: {@i Take What You Need at Knifepoint}

Brigands encompass all manner of highwaymen, pirates, raiders, and dastardly folk. No tactic, no matter how heinous, is off the table for a band of Brigands, whether that means roadside ambushes or taking hostages at knifepoint. Ultimately, most Brigands are driven to their thievery through desperation; it is fitting that they leave others as few choices as were afforded to them.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Take Hostage
entries: When you hit a Medium or smaller creature with an attack using a melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and reduce the target to a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} less than or equal to twice your Vagabond level, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to hold the target hostage. While held hostage, the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} conditions.

While holding a creature hostage, you have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover}. Attacks that miss you hit the hostage instead. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks against the hostage's allies.
You can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} in response to any creature's action to release the hostage or attack it with a weapon you are holding.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Underhanded Blow
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can give the target {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attacks it makes before the start of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} or finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Cutthroat
entries: Ruthlessness is second-nature to you. When you hit a creature with an attack roll and roll the highest number on any damage die, you can roll that damage die again and add it to the damage, rolling again if it is the highest number, and so on. You can roll each damage die up to a maximum of four times.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Brigand

entries: {@color {@style Cross-Compatible Subclass: This subclass originates from the {@color {@class Vagabond|ValdaSpire24Extras}|63A7A0} class|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style Note that cross-compatible subclasses might be stronger or weaker than other subclasses.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style The GM decides if a subclass should be cross-compatible in your campaign.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@i Take What You Need at Knifepoint}

Brigands encompass all manner of highwaymen, pirates, raiders, and dastardly folk. No tactic, no matter how heinous, is off the table for a band of Brigands, whether that means roadside ambushes or taking hostages at knifepoint. Ultimately, most Brigands are driven to their thievery through desperation; it is fitting that they leave others as few choices as were afforded to them.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Take Hostage
entries: When you hit a Medium or smaller creature with an attack using a melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and reduce the target to a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} less than or equal to twice your Vagabond level, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to hold the target hostage. While held hostage, the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} conditions.

While holding a creature hostage, you have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover}. Attacks that miss you hit the hostage instead. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks against the hostage's allies.
You can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} in response to any creature's action to release the hostage or attack it with a weapon you are holding.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Underhanded Blow
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can give the target {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attacks it makes before the start of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} or finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Cutthroat
entries: Ruthlessness is second-nature to you. When you hit a creature with an attack roll and roll the highest number on any damage die, you can roll that damage die again and add it to the damage, rolling again if it is the highest number, and so on. You can roll each damage die up to a maximum of four times.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Brigand

entries: {@color {@style Cross-Compatible Subclass: This subclass originates from the {@color {@class Vagabond|ValdaSpire24Extras}|63A7A0} class|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style Note that cross-compatible subclasses might be stronger or weaker than other subclasses.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style The GM decides if a subclass should be cross-compatible in your campaign.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@i Take What You Need at Knifepoint}

Brigands encompass all manner of highwaymen, pirates, raiders, and dastardly folk. No tactic, no matter how heinous, is off the table for a band of Brigands, whether that means roadside ambushes or taking hostages at knifepoint. Ultimately, most Brigands are driven to their thievery through desperation; it is fitting that they leave others as few choices as were afforded to them.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Take Hostage
entries: When you hit a Medium or smaller creature with an attack using a melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and reduce the target to a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} less than or equal to twice your Vagabond level, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to hold the target hostage. While held hostage, the target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} conditions.

While holding a creature hostage, you have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover}. Attacks that miss you hit the hostage instead. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks against the hostage's allies.
You can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} in response to any creature's action to release the hostage or attack it with a weapon you are holding.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Underhanded Blow
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can give the target {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attacks it makes before the start of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} or finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Cutthroat
entries: Ruthlessness is second-nature to you. When you hit a creature with an attack roll and roll the highest number on any damage die, you can roll that damage die again and add it to the damage, rolling again if it is the highest number, and so on. You can roll each damage die up to a maximum of four times.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Anonymity
entries: {@i Kill in the Shadows, Die in the Shadows}

Like other Martyrs, you were chosen to accomplish great things and die for a noble cause. However, you were not destined for glory; no one will ever know your name. Martyrs chosen for the Burden of Anonymity work in the shadows to influence the world for the greater good, and will inevitably die in the shadows, unknown to all. Your divinely-appointed task might be secret, such as assassination or infiltration, and your role as a Martyr might be incognito, even to your allies. Anonymous Martyrs might disguise themselves as Paladins, mercenaries, or Rogues with hidden agendas and abundant conspiracies.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Silent Sacrifice
entries: When you make an attack or damage roll that is improved by your Sacrifice feature against a target that can't see you, you don't take Radiant damage from using the feature and the target is magically silenced on a hit. Until the start of your next turn, the target can't speak, has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition, and can't cast any spell that includes a Verbal component.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: False Martyrdom
entries: When you take damage or use your Undying Conviction, you can convincingly fake your death. You teleport up to a known location within 10 miles of you at the same time that a duplicate corpse appears to take your place. The corpse is indistinguishable from you and wears nonmagical duplicates of your clothing and equipment. You can choose for the corpse to realistically bleed, mutter incoherently, and breathe shallowly for up to a minute. The corpse is unaffected by spells and other magical effects. The corpse and its clothing and equipment vanish after 10 days, or when you dismiss it as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action or use this feature again.

Furthermore, if you covertly notify the GM, you can also convince other players of your death. You can roll Death Saving Throws as normal, ignoring successes, temporarily prepare a new character sheet, and so on.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Cheating Death
entries: At the GM's discretion, Martyrs with the Burden of Anonymity can use their False Martyrdom to avoid their inevitable death detailed in the Final Martyrdom feature. This still concludes the character's story with a glorious sacrifice but leaves the potential for the character to retire or simply disappear into a crowd once their ultimate goal has been achieved.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Divine Assassin
entries: Your skill at remaining unseen grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Elusive Invisibility
entries: While you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws.

entries.name: Swift Disappearance
entries: You can cast {@spell Invisibility|XPHB} and {@spell Greater Invisibility|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You take half the normal Radiant damage from casting these spells.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Ascension
entries: {@i Ascend to Godhood}

The gods have set an arduous path for your life, replete with labors, challenges, and trials designed to test your morality and resolve. You likely won't succeed. However, if you best the gods' trials and die in marvelous glory, you will ascend to the afterlife as a demigod.

Perhaps the gods envision you as a replacement for a recently-deceased god, or perhaps they raise dozens of demigods to do their bidding across the planes of existence. Regardless of your status, immortality after death awaits.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Olympic Agility
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} and {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. Additionally, {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} doesn't cost you extra movement.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Relics of Legend
entries: Your legendary deeds have imbued your most iconic equipment with supernatural blessings. You choose three pieces of equipment to be your Aegis, Oracle, and Xiphos. These items might have been at your side for years, have been used to accomplish one of your labors, or even be trophies taken from your mightiest foes. Once you use your Aegis, Oracle, or Xiphos, you can't use that relic again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Aegis
entries: Your Aegis is a {@item Shield|XPHB}, an article of clothing, or a pelt that grants you divine protection. You can use your Aegis to cast {@spell Shield|XPHB} without taking Radiant damage or expending a spell use.

entries.name: Oracle
entries: Your Oracle is a stone, gemstone, or another accessory that allows you to communicate with the gods. You can use your Oracle to cast {@spell Commune|XPHB} without taking Radiant damage or expending a spell use.

entries.name: Xiphos
entries: Your Xiphos is a sword, spear, or other Melee weapon. Immediately after you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} with your Xiphos or reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} with it, you can move up your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and make another melee weapon roll using it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Demigod Ascendant
entries: The power of demigods flows through your veins, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Improved Herculean Surge
entries: Your Herculean Surge improves. When you use this feature, your Strength and Dexterity scores gain a +4 bonus, up to a maximum of 24, for 1 minute. You regain your use of Herculean Surge whenever you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance
entries: If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Atonement
entries: {@i Seek Redemption Through Sacrifice}

For all the wrong you have done in your life, the gods have graced you with an undeserved second chance. Your burden is to atone, to undo all the evils you have done in your life, and to seek redemption before the gods. How you accomplish this is your choice, so long as you remove any dark marks you leave behind. Ultimately, your final martyrdom might be a grand act, averting a great disaster or banishing a force of evil, or it might be as humble as redirecting the life of an evil person and causing them to seek redemption, passing the torch to a new Martyr of Atonement.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sin Eater
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to transfer negative effects from any number of willing creatures within 60 feet of yourself to you.

If a chosen effect forced the original target to make a saving throw to avoid or end it, you make that saving throw against it with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. On a success, the effect ends; on a failure, the effect ends for the original target and affects you instead as if you were the original target.
You can transfer multiple negative effects of the same type to yourself, affecting you only once each time you use this feature.
You can transfer the following negative effects.

items: 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level
A curse, including the target's {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to a cursed magic item
Any reduction to one of the target's ability scores
Any reduction to the target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum

The {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, or {@condition Stunned|XPHB} conditions

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Selfless Sacrifice
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Sacrificial Challenge
entries: When you use your Sacrificial Strike, you can choose for the target to have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls it makes against creatures other than you until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Sacrificial Luck
entries: When you use your Sacrificial {@variantrule Skill|XPHB} to turn a failure into a success, each ally that can see you within 30 feet of yourself adds {@dice 1d6} to the next {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} it makes before the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Ever-Vigilant
entries: You gain a special {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} that you can only take to use Reprisal or Redirection. You can only take one {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} per turn. Once you take this special {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can't take it again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Calamity
entries: {@i Leave Catastrophic Plagues and Disasters in Your Wake}

A grim task awaits those shouldering the Burden of Calamity. These Martyrs spark wars, conjure floods, raise plagues of locusts, call down fire and brimstone, and set apocalypses in motion. As benevolent as the gods might seem, their mercy is tempered with disasters such as these, events that the gods deem necessary to cleanse unjust societies or wipe the slate clean for new advancements. Martyrs of Calamity are therefore harbingers of doom, the first omen of terrible things to follow.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Apocalyptic Omen
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can manifest a harmless, temporary omen within a 1-mile radius of yourself for 1 hour. This might include creating an eclipse on command, forming the clouds into a terrible face, conjuring pests, transforming water into blood, or causing the earth to tremble. For the duration, you add {@dice 1d4} to {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} you make.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Denounce Arcana
entries: A creature with the Magic Resistance trait has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, instead of {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, on saving throws against your Martyr spells.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Doom Foretold
entries: You can call upon the gods' malice to create a sweeping disaster. You can cast {@spell Control Weather|XPHB}, {@spell Earthquake|XPHB}, {@spell Fire Storm|XPHB}, or {@spell Storm of Vengeance|XPHB} without taking Radiant damage or expending a spell use.
Once you use this feature to cast one of these spells, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Discord
entries: {@i Wreak Havoc and Disrupt the Status Quo}

Martyrs of Discord are chosen at random to sow chaos wherever they travel. They light things on fire, commit petty crimes, and even murder when the fancy strikes. Apt to follow their own predilections, Martyrs of Discord are unified only by their charge to disrupt the status quo as much as possible.

No one is certain why the gods make Martyrs of Discord in the first place. Perhaps it is at the whim of one capricious or evil god, or perhaps the gods desire a balance between chaos and law, and must sometimes stoke the fire to restore this balance.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Coin of Chaos
entries: You have a coin infused with the tides of chaos. Whenever you or an ally makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can flip a coin to add a bonus to the roll. The bonus equals +4 on heads, or +1 on tails.

Once you use the coin, the coin passes to the GM, who can use it to add a bonus to any {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} made by a creature under their control. Once the GM uses the coin, it passes back to you, and so on. When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you regain the coin, whether or not the GM has used it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Pandemonium
entries: You can use your Havoc! without taking Radiant damage and, whenever you roll on the Havoc! table, you can roll twice and use either number.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sacrificial Burst
entries: When you use your Sacrificial Strike, you can deal an extra {@damage 2d10} Radiant damage instead of 10 Radiant damage, or {@damage 4d10} damage instead of 20.

Additionally, if you roll the highest number of any damage die for this attack, you can roll another of that die and add it to the damage. You can add a maximum of 10 dice to the attack's damage roll in this way.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Fame
entries: {@i Get Famous}

You were destined to see your name in lights, to be the talk of the town, to be a superstar. Unfortunately, the gods also chose you to go out in a blaze of glory. The Burden of Fame entails a life of renown matched only by royalty, coupled with incredible duties undertaken in the public eye. Your flame burns brightly for half as long, but when your journey is complete, nobody will forget your name.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Entourage
entries: You gain a bonus to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equal to the number of creatures with the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition within 30 feet of you, to a maximum of your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Crowd Suggestion
entries: You can cast {@spell Mass Suggestion|XPHB} without taking Radiant damage or expending a spell use. Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

Whenever you start casting the spell, you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. If you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting and the spell can target up to 100 creatures within range.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Superstar Sanctitude
entries: Your unparalleled stardom grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Reactive Sanctuary
entries: When you use your Reprisal, you can cast {@spell Sanctuary|XPHB} on yourself without taking Radiant damage or expending a spell use as a part of the {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

entries.name: Superstar Aura
entries: Each Large or smaller enemy that ends its turn within 5 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Levity
entries: {@i Pull Pranks and Crack Jokes}

When bacchanal and trickster deities believe that the mortal realm has gotten too self-serious, they call upon a Martyr of Levity to lighten the mood. These impish Martyrs are given license to joke, prank, and romp about the world with extraordinarily vague directives. Perhaps they have been commanded to pull a prank or tell a joke so ludicrous that history remembers it forever. Or perhaps the Martyr is themselves the butt of a larger joke, a walking parable about fate's blunders. Sadly, the Martyr's death usually serves as a punchline.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Just a Prank
entries: Once per turn when a creature you can see makes an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you, you can make a melee attack against the creature. Your attack precedes the triggering attack.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Matador Backstab
entries: You can cast {@spell Mass Suggestion|XPHB} without taking Radiant damage or expending a spell use. Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

Whenever you start casting the spell, you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. If you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting and the spell can target up to 100 creatures within range.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Zany Misdirection
entries: When you use your Reprisal, instead of dealing Radiant or Necrotic damage to the attacker, you can force the attack to hit another creature other than the attacker within the attack's range.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Mercy
entries: {@i Heal the Sick and Wounded}

When the suffering of the world grows too heavy and the cries of the anguished grow too loud, the gods deliver a Martyr to ease the strife and bring peace to the masses. This burden, however, has no end. A Martyr may spend all their days healing the sick and driving demons out of the possessed, but they will scarcely impact the world at large. Indeed, the onus upon them is not to mend every wound or comfort every widow, but to provide hope in the darkest of times that the gods have not forsaken their people, that peace will soon reign, and that light will be victorious.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Virtuous Blessings
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose a number of creatures you can see up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1) to receive one of the following blessings of your choice. Each creature need not receive the same blessing. An unused blessing is expended when a blessed creature finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blessing of Alacrity
entries: The creature can expend this blessing to increase its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 30 feet until the end of the current turn (no action required).

entries.name: Blessing of Eloquence
entries: The creature can expend this blessing to gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} using Wisdom or Charisma (no action required).

entries.name: Blessing of Vigilance
entries: The creature can expend this blessing to gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Censuring Light
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you emanate a radiant light in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that lasts for 1 minute or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. Choose Aberrations, Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, or Undead.

Whenever the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} enters the space of a creature of the chosen type and whenever such a creature enters the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} or ends its turn there, it takes {@damage 4d6} Radiant damage. A creature takes this damage only once per turn.

Additionally, while in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}, creatures of your choice have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects created by creatures of the chosen type.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by taking 30 Radiant damage. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}, and bypasses {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Anointed Healer
entries: Whenever you cast a spell that restores {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to a creature, that creature regains additional {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} on the turn you cast the spell equal to your Martyr level. If this healing exceeds the creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum, it gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to excess healing, up to a maximum of your Martyr level.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Odyssey
entries: {@i Undertake a Journey of Discovery}

The gods have tasked you with exploring the far reaches of the world, to venture where no soul has gone before, and bring back the discoveries waiting to be found there. You might be tasked to map an undiscovered continent, discover a straight between distant cities, or sail the edge of the oceans, but peril and adventure regardless await. You are unlikely to return from your journey, but your expedition will not have been in vain as long as your odyssey is remembered.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Misty Transposition
entries: You can cast {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} without taking Radiant damage. When you do so, you can choose to teleport to a space occupied by a willing creature within range that doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. You both teleport, swapping places.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Zephyr's Stride
entries: Whenever you move into a space 30 feet or further away from where you started your turn, you are enveloped in a blur of speed. Until the start of your next turn, attack rolls against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} and you don't take Radiant damage from your Sacrificial Strike.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Argonaut
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can cast {@spell Haste|XPHB} on yourself without taking Radiant damage or expending a spell use. When you cast the spell, it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB} and, when the spell ends, you don't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} isn't 0.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by taking 30 Radiant damage (no action required). This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}, and bypasses {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Rebirth
entries: {@i Regenerate and Regrow the Natural World}

When the natural world is threatened by the needs of growing industry, the ravages of war, or a catastrophic event, the gods may choose a Martyr to protect the wild places of the world. Martyrs with this burden don't seek to prevent the destruction of the world; that would be impossible given the number of factors that threaten it. Instead, those tasked with the Burden of Rebirth give their lives to regenerate what has been razed, ushering in new life in places devastated by death.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Surefooted
entries: {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} doesn't cost you or allies within 30 feet of yourself extra movement. Additionally, you and allies within 30 feet of you are immune to the {@spell Entangle|XPHB}, {@spell Spike Growth|XPHB}, and {@spell Plant Growth|XPHB} spells.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Verdant Resilience
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can enter a state of natural regeneration, granting your the following for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Regeneration
entries: At the start of each of your turns, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1) if you have at least 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}.

entries.name: Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Turn of the Wheel
entries: Death is only the beginning for you. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Reincarnation
entries: You can cast {@spell Reincarnate|XPHB} without Material components or taking Radiant damage. When you cast this spell, you can choose the new body's species instead of rolling for it randomly.

entries.name: Reincarnated Return
entries: If you die without using your Final Martyrdom, you can return to life 24 hours after you die as if you were the target of the {@spell Reincarnate|XPHB} spell. You can choose your new body's species instead of rolling for it randomly. Once you return to life in this way, you can't do so again for 10 days.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Revolution
entries: {@i Liberate Others and Slay Tyrants}

Kings and leaders are bound by an unspoken covenant to the gods to govern their people justly and peacefully. When a monarch turns their back on the gods, embraces tyranny, or uses cruel measures against their own people, a Martyr is called to end their reign. Rarely does a Martyr of Revolution come with peaceful measures, for when a king must fall, only the sword can provide the necessary leverage.

Such Martyrs are not only called to battle kings; any person of influence that oppresses others and abuses their power might wrong the gods enough to earn the ire of a Martyr. In dark times, a Martyr might be tasked with clearing a continent of despots and oppressors, calling for a full-scale military campaign of liberation.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Aura of Tenacity
entries: You and your allies within a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} centered on you gain a bonus to {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1). The aura is inactive while you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Kingslayer
entries: Once per turn when you reduce an enemy to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, choose one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Assault
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can move up to 15 feet and make a melee attack.

entries.name: Break Spells
entries: All of the creature's spells and effects immediately end, including all spells with permanent effects. Additionally, {@spell Contingency|XPHB}, {@spell Clone|XPHB}, and other spells that occur in response to the target's death don't trigger.

entries.name: Shatter Morale
entries: Each ally of the creature within 120 feet of it that has a {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} less than the target's (or the target's level if it doesn't have a {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB}) has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} target makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, ending the condition on itself on a success.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Rallying Strike
entries: When you use your Sacrificial Strike, choose one of your allies within 30 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. The ally can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make one attack using a weapon.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of the End
entries: {@i Prevent a Looming Disaster, or Die Trying}

The gods have seen a great cataclysm on the horizon and tasked you with protecting the world from catastrophe. The coming end may entail the collapse of a kingdom, the arrival of an evil entity, or the quiet vanishing of a village, temple, or way of life. However destructive or temperate, the coming cataclysm disrupts the gods' plans or threatens their hold on the mortal plane. To this end, the gods imbue you with ancient and powerful spells, tools once gifted only to prophets. The life of a Martyr is always forfeit, so long as the cataclysm can be forestalled or defeated.

entries.subclassFeature: Burden of the End Spells|Martyr|ValdaSpire24|The End|ValdaSpire24|3

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Anointed Arcana
entries: The Radiant damage you take from casting spells listed on the End Spells table is reduced by 10, to a minimum of 5.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sacrificial Spell
entries: When you cast a level 1+ Martyr spell, you can take 10 Radiant damage to use one of the following benefits. This damage ignores your {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}, and bypasses your {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Heighten
entries: Once on each of your turns, when you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can give one target of the spell {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saves against the spell.

entries.name: Quicken
entries: When you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action, you can change the casting time to a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} for this casting. You can't modify a spell in this way if you've already cast a level 1+ spell on the current turn, nor can you cast a level 1+ spell on this turn after modifying a spell in this way.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Vindictive Spell
entries: When you take damage from an enemy you can see within 30 feet of yourself, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cast a level 1-3 Martyr spell. The spell must deal damage, have a casting time of an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, and target that creature or include it in its area. The Radiant damage you take from casting the spell is decreased by the amount of triggering damage (minimum 0).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Truth
entries: {@i Bring a Prophet's Message to the World}

Tasked with unveiling the world's deceptions and delivering to the people a profound truth, Martyrs carrying the Burden of Truth face an endless battle with disillusionment and lies. Such a Martyr must earn the people's hearts and minds, turning their favors away from evil influences and toward divine ones. It is an uphill battle, but one that rarely requires grievous violence except in the most dire of circumstances.

Martyrs of Truth are often deemed prophets, for their gods entrust them with knowledge of the future, insights into the past, and sagacious perspective on the present. Such information is proof of their messages' divine origin and is a necessary balm, for the truths such Martyrs are called to preach are often a bitter pill for listeners to swallow.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Seer
entries: You have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Word of Revelation
entries: You can cast {@spell Word of Force|ValdaSpire24}, {@spell Word of Terror|ValdaSpire24}, and {@spell Word of Frailty|ValdaSpire24} once each without taking Radiant damage or expending a spell use.

Once you cast one of these spells without taking Radiant damage, you must finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can cast the spell in that way again.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sacrificial Foresight
entries: When you use your Sacrificial {@variantrule Skill|XPHB}, you gain a +5 bonus to all {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} you make until the end of the current turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Burden of Tyranny
entries: {@i Rule with an Iron Fist}

When malevolent gods find the world pacified and defenseless, they send a Martyr of Tyranny to conquer its kingdoms, subjugate the weak, and spread misery with their blade. Once unleashed, this Martyr stops at nothing to establish an empire to rule over with an iron fist. They demand submission from their foes and pledges of fealty from their allies, taking gleeful satisfaction with every power grab and malicious turn. It isn't enough to rule: they must be feared, and any resistance must cower in their shadows. Only then will the gods let them die, likely stabbed in the back by someone crueler or more pitiless.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Death Stare
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, or as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action on your turn, you can lay a chilling gaze upon a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sacrificial Resilience
entries: Once on each of your turns, immediately after you use your Sacrificial Strike, you can gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the amount of Radiant damage you take.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Totalitarian Control
entries: You can cast {@spell Dominate Beast|XPHB}, {@spell Dominate Monster|XPHB}, or {@spell Dominate Person|XPHB} once without taking Radiant damage or expending a spell use. When you cast one of these spells using this feature, you gain the following benefits. Once you cast one of these spells without taking Radiant damage, you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can cast the spell in that way again.

entries.name: Overpowering Command
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its saving throw against the spell.

entries.name: Psychic Recoil
entries: When the spell ends, you can choose to deal {@damage 6d8} Psychic damage to the target.

entries.name: Iron Grip
entries: If you cast {@spell Dominate Beast|XPHB} or Dominate Person, you can numb the target to pain. The target doesn't repeat its saving throw against the spell when it takes damage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Calibarons' Guild
entries: {@i Design Dangerous Ranged Weapons}

Craftsmen of the Calibarons' Guild believe that gunpowder is the single greatest invention ever created by mortals. A sword may let a skilled wielder lay low a giant, and magic may let the savvy and the blessed stand up to the gods, but only a gun will let a common man put a dragon in its place.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Magazine
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can use your Crafting Tools to modify a Masterwork Ranged weapon that has the {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading} or {@itemProperty RLD|XDMG|Reload} property. If it has the {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading} property, it instead has the {@itemProperty RLD|XDMG|Reload} property. If you use such a modified weapon that has the {@itemProperty RLD|XDMG|Reload} property, a mechanical mechanism automatically reloads it from a belt or hopper of ammunition you are carrying (no action required).

entries.name: Reload
entries: This weapon can be used to make a number of attacks before it must be reloaded. If you are proficient with the weapon, reloading it takes an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}; otherwise, reloading it takes an action. The number of attacks is determined by the size of the weapon's damage die or dice, as shown on the Reload Attacks table.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Suppressive Fire
entries: Once per turn when you make a ranged attack roll, you can cow the target. That creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Stopping Power
entries: When you roll damage for an attack you make with a Masterwork Ranged weapon, you can treat any damage die as if it rolled half of the largest number on the die. For example, if you roll a 1-4 on a {@dice d10}, you can treat the roll as a 5.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Carrion King
entries: {@i Command an Army of Vermin}

A champion of vermin, you are called to defend the lowliest creatures of all: insects, rats, spiders, and other pests. These creatures mean no harm; they're merely trying to survive in a world too large for them, and so they flock to your side. Unmistakably, your coming is signaled by the scrambling of little claws and the cawing of the crows. Legions of pests wait at your command to swarm, bite, and infest anyone who might thin their numbers.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Swarm Cloud
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you surround yourself with countless flying pests in an {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you. You choose whether the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} extends 5 feet, 10 feet, or 15 feet. This area is {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|XPHB} and has one of the following effects of your choice, which lasts for 10 minutes or until you end it (no action required).

entries.name: Deafening
entries: Creatures you choose entirely within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} have the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Difficult Terrain
entries: The area of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for creatures other than yourself.

entries.name: Heavily Obscured
entries: The area of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} for creatures other than yourself.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Plague Vector
entries: Whenever you use your {@classFeature Interrupt|Warden|ValdaSpire24|5}, the target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the end of the current turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Lord of the Flies
entries: You can call a colossal swarm of vermin to your aid.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain the benefits below for 1 minute or until you choose to end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blinding Bites
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace one of your attacks with commanding your vermin to blind a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take {@damage 2d10} Piercing damage and have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, a {@condition Blinded|XPHB} target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Infesting Swarm
entries: When you use your {@subclassFeature Infest|Warden|ValdaSpire24|Carrion King|ValdaSpire24Extras|3} while your {@subclassFeature Swarm Cloud|Warden|ValdaSpire24|Carrion King|ValdaSpire24Extras|6} is active, you can target any creatures of your choice within your {@subclassFeature Swarm Cloud|Warden|ValdaSpire24|Carrion King|ValdaSpire24Extras|6||Swarm Cloud's} {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Clockworkers' Guild
entries: {@i Build and Command Clockwork Minions}

Masters of machinery, the tinkers and gearsmiths of the Clockworkers' Guild study and perfect the art of fashioning Constructs. Their designs are as elegant as they are functional, translating single ticking movements through a kaleidoscope of gears and pistons to create lifelike, even a seemingly intelligent, clockwork creatures. Nearly all Clockworkers are attended by a pair of their Construct servants that serve a dual purpose as attentive assistants and relentless bodyguards. Veteran Clockworkers, however, walk astride Constructs taller than themselves, great gear-driven golems of formidable strength.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mechanized Attachments
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can use your Crafting Tools to affix one of the following attachments to a suit of Masterwork armor or one of your Clockwork Constructs, or to replace an attachment with another one. Each armor or Construct can have one attachment at a time.

entries.name: Clockwork Lantern
entries: A Bullseye Lantern casts {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 60-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 60 feet. The {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} of light follows wherever you look. The wearer can light or extinguish the lantern as a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Mechanized Grappling Hook
entries: This launcher contains 80 feet of rope affixed to a {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB} Hook. As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, the wearer can launch the {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB} Hook at a railing, ledge, or another catch within 80 feet of itself, and the hook catches on if the wearer succeeds on a DC 13 Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) check. A mechanized winch then retracts the rope and up to 350 pounds of attached weight at a rate of 10 feet per round (100 feet per minute).

entries.name: Ram Helm
entries: A pneumatic Portable Ram is integrated into this helm, which can be used without hands.

entries.name: Springheels
entries: While wearing this armor, the wearer's jump distance is doubled.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Death Burst
entries: A dead man's switch is integrated into each of your constructs. When one of your Clockwork Constructs drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it detonates in a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. Each creature within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} makes a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}), taking {@damage 6d6} Fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a failed save.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Construct Enchantments
