subclassFeaturesFull.name: House of Bishops
entries: {@i Wield Greater Arcane Magic}

The House of Bishops adopts Warmages with arcane potential and teaches its members traditional spellcasting. Such Warmages might be mistaken for Wizards or Sorcerers, for they wield many of the same spells, but bishops prioritize excellence in their spellcasting over a wide repertoire of spells.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mystical Companion
entries: You always have the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell prepared, which doesn't count against your number of prepared spells. When you cast the spell, you choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: {@creature Imp|XMM}, {@creature Pseudodragon|XMM}, {@creature Quasit|XMM}, or {@creature Sprite|XMM}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Siege Casting
entries: Your Warmage and Wizard spells deal double damage to objects and structures. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on spell attack rolls against targets that are 100 or more feet away from you.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Spell Sculpting
entries: When you cast a spell with a spell slot that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one). The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Dominance
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a number of spell slots with a combined level of 6+ to regain one expended use of your {@classFeature Arcane Surge|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|5}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: House of Cards
entries: {@i Push Your Luck With Hands of Cards}

Warmages who join the House of Cards approach combat the same way they do games of chance: with high stakes and calculated gambles. Each Warmage of this house wields a special deck of cards tied to the very threads of fate, through which they can empower their magic with deft flurries of hands. However, while these Warmages command incredible power, their magical surges are at the whims of the cards, and so they must make strategic, ingenious plays to master them.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: High Stakes
entries: On your turn, you can choose any number of cards from your hand and place them on the bottom of your {@subclassFeature Deck of Fate|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|Cards|ValdaSpire24|3} (no action required), losing 2 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} per card you choose. You then draw until you have five cards in your hand again.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dealer's Choice
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to gain one of the following benefits, chosen by the GM. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Resistance
entries: You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Teleportation
entries: You teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of you.

entries.name: Demiplane
entries: You vanish into a safe, endless demiplane. At the start of your next turn, you reappear in the space you left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Card Reading
entries: Once on each of your turns when you draw a card from your deck as part of your {@subclassFeature Deck of Fate|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|Cards|ValdaSpire24|3} feature, you can declare a suit (Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, or Spades) and check the top card of your deck. If you guessed the suit correctly, you can take the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Utilize|XPHB} action as part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} used for the feature.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Ace in the Hole
entries: Whenever you would draw one or more cards from your deck, draw twice as many. Put half of the cards drawn on the bottom of your deck and the other cards in your hand.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: House of Darts
entries: {@i Make Bullseye Shots with Ranged Cantrips}

Every Warmage understands the importance of precision, but the House of Darts flaunts a competitive excellence when it comes to landing shots. Daggers, bolts of magic, and of course, darts are their weapons of choice, but they don't stop at mere bullseyes. A wire array of trick shots set these Warmages apart from their contemporaries, even if they lack the grand strategies or discipline of the more martial colleges.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dagger Climb
entries: You can cast {@spell Magic Daggers|ValdaSpire24} to summon a pair of daggers to your open hands, helping you scale surfaces. You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} for 10 minutes.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Intercepting Shot
entries: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when an attacker you can see within 60 feet makes an attack against you or an {@variantrule Ally|XPHB} you can see within 30 feet of yourself, you can make a ranged spell attack using {@spell Magic Daggers|ValdaSpire24} to interrupt the attack. If the result of your roll is greater than the result of the attacker, you can reduce the attack roll targeting you by 5 (to a minimum result of 1).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Vanishing Toss
entries: You master the house's signature technique for recovering darts. Whenever you cast the {@spell Magic Daggers|ValdaSpire24} cantrip, you can replace one of your spell attacks with throwing a special teleportation dagger to a point you can see within the spell's range. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to teleport to the dagger as long as you are within 500 feet of it. The dagger disappears after 10 minutes or if you use this feature to teleport or throw another teleportation dagger.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dart Burst
entries: If you have recorded ten or more unique numbers using your {@subclassFeature Bullseye|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|Darts|ValdaSpire24|3} feature, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to clear all of your recorded numbers and throw a burst of darts. Each creature in a 60-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 1d8} Force damage for each unique recorded number on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: House of Dice
entries: {@i Tempt Fate with Chaotic Die Rolls}

The House of Dice throws out the Warmage convention of meticulous, deliberate spellcasting in favor of wild, chaotic magic that presses the odds. Everything from their magical bursts to their enchanted sets of dice can fail horribly, so it's auspicious that they often keep their fingers on the scales of fate. These Warmages have mastered not only a repertoire of cantrips, but also techniques to manipulate fortune itself, allowing them to risk everything, and more than often come out on top.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Loaded Dice
entries: You can subtly cheat your dice. Once on each of your turns when you roll a {@dice d6}, you can flip the die upside down. Note that on a balanced {@dice d6}, the top and bottom numbers add up to 7, so you can determine the bottom number by subtracting the top number from 7.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Twisted Fate
entries: When you make an attack roll or ability check with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on your turn, you can attempt to invert fate as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. Expend a {@subclassFeature Dice of Fate|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|Dice|ValdaSpire24|3|ValdaSpire24|Die of Fate} and roll it. On a 5, you ignore {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the roll. On a 6, you instead have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Roll the Bones
entries: You can channel the chaotic energy of your dice in an instant. As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when you take damage from a creature you can see, you can expend two {@subclassFeature Dice of Fate|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|Dice|ValdaSpire24|3} to make a {@subclassFeature Chaos Roll|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|Dice|ValdaSpire24|3}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Steal Luck
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, roll a {@dice d6}. You steal that many {@subclassFeature Dice of Fate|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|Dice|ValdaSpire24|3} back from the GM.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: House of Go
entries: {@i Dominate Your Foes Through Cunning Formations}

The renowned House of Go predates the other Warmage colleges by centuries. Unlike its successors, the strategies pioneered by the House of Go focus upon formations and cooperation, rather than individual excellence. Which isn't to suggest that Warmages of this college are anything other than brilliant strategists—they rival the House of Kings in this regard. Rather, the footsoldiers of the House of Go are greater than the sum of their parts, fluidly adopting motions to isolate and flank their foes.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Opening Strategy
entries: You can spend 10 minutes planning an encounter in exact detail. When you do so, you can share your plan with up to six {@variantrule Ally|XPHB|Allies} within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you and who can understand you. Each {@variantrule Ally|XPHB} that understands the plan can gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on an attack roll or ability check it makes within the next 10 minutes. If an {@variantrule Ally|XPHB} rolls {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} during this time, it can't use this feature to gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} after the end of the first round of combat.
Once you use this feature to make a plan, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Hardened Formations
entries: While you are in a formation, any {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against you or an {@variantrule Ally|XPHB} in your formation becomes a normal hit.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Chain of Liberties
entries: Your formation moves as if your {@variantrule Ally|XPHB|Allies} were links in a chain. Whenever you move on your turn, any number of willing {@variantrule Ally|XPHB|Allies} in your formation can move the same distance.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: End Game
entries: On your turn, when you reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} with a {@filter Warmage cantrip|spells|level=0|class=warmage (VSS'24)}, you can cast another cantrip as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You can apply {@classFeature Warmage Edge|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|1} to this cantrip, even if you have already used it on your turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: House of Kings
entries: {@i Lead Your Allies with Brilliant Stratagems}

Warmages who train in the House of Kings specialize in tactics and strategy, learning age-old maneuvers to gain an edge in combat. Natural-born leaders, Kings work best with a cadre of supporters to perform their tactics and overwhelm the enemy. Moreso than all other Warmages, those in the House of Kings treat life and death as a game of strategy to be understood and conquered.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Lead from the Front
entries: {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} doesn't cost you extra movement. {@variantrule Ally|XPHB|Allies} that can see you within 120 feet of you also gain this benefit.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Tactical Master
entries: {@variantrule Ally|XPHB|Allies} within 10 feet of you add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1) to their saving throws against spells and magical effects.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Checkmate [Maneuver]
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend one Battle Die as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to direct an {@variantrule Ally|XPHB} within 60 feet of yourself that can see or hear you to strike. The {@variantrule Ally|XPHB} can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cast a cantrip or make one attack with a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. The ally adds the Battle Die to one damage roll of the attack or cantrip.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Grandmaster
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, choose a number of {@variantrule Ally|XPHB|Allies} up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one) within 60 feet of yourself that can see or hear you. Give each {@variantrule Ally|XPHB} a Battle Die without expending it.

Once within the next minute when the {@variantrule Ally|XPHB} fails a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, it can roll the Battle Die and add the number rolled to the {@dice d20}, potentially turning the failure into a success. A Battle Die is expended when it's rolled.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: House of Knights
entries: {@i Wield Blades of Fire, Lightning, Frost, and Force}

The House of Knights has a long and storied tradition of melding swordplay with the Warmage's potent spellcasting. Unlike other warriors, however, Knights carry neither swords nor shields into combat, for they can forge both out of magical force at a moment's notice.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fighting Style
entries: You gain a {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS} of your choice. Whenever you gain a Warmage level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Knight's Ward
entries: You can raise a hardened magical barrier between you and your foes. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Warmage level.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Tactical Maneuver
entries: You can spend up to 30 feet of movement to teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. The destination can be a number of feet away from you equal to half the movement you spend.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Field of Blades
entries: You can summon a whirlwind of mystical weapons for a flurry of strikes. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can make a melee spell attack against up to five creatures you can see within 30 feet of you. Make a separate attack roll for each target. On a hit, a target takes Force damage equal to {@dice 2d10} + your Intelligence modifier.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: House of Pawns
entries: {@i Master Cantrips and Warmage Tricks}

By far the most prominent Warmage house is that of the Pawns. Warmages who join the House of Pawns learn to stretch their skill with cantrips to its limits. Pawns can master any cantrip or strategy, for they embody the adaptability to which all Warmages aspire.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Pawn Storm
entries: You can add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1) to {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls. Additionally, when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Multidiscipline
entries: You can add half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (round down) to any saving throw you make that doesn't otherwise use your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Pawn Wall
entries: Whenever you deal damage with a {@filter Warmage cantrip|spells|level=0|class=warmage (VSS'24)}, you and up to two {@variantrule Ally|XPHB|Allies} within 5 feet of you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage type until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fundamental Mastery
entries: Your magic always finds its way to your foes' most vulnerable spots. Once per turn when you roll damage for a {@filter Warmage cantrip|spells|level=0|class=warmage (VSS'24)}, you can choose one damage die and treat it as having rolled its maximum value.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: House of Rooks
entries: {@i Practice Furtive Magic and Mystical Stealth}

The clandestine members of the House of Rooks make adept spies, assassins, and scouts, though they might just as easily pick up jobs run by rogues and brigands. In addition to their suite of cantrips, Rooks are light on their feet and know a few tricks to magically open doors in utter silence.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Covert Magic
entries: You learn a suite of furtive magic practiced by Rooks. You can cast each of the following spells without using a spell slot or Verbal components: {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB}, {@spell Invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell Knock|XPHB} (silent when you cast it using this feature), {@spell Silence|XPHB}, and {@spell Spider Climb|XPHB}.

Once you cast a spell using this feature, you can't cast it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can expend a use of {@classFeature Arcane Surge|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|5} to regain your use of all of these spells (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fleeting Decoy
entries: When you take damage from a creature you can see, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to raise a defensive illusion that protects you from further harm. Attacks made against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Elusive Step
entries: If you move more than 5 feet on your turn, any subsequent movement you make doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Assassin
entries: You can cast {@spell Greater Invisibility|XPHB} targeting yourself only without a spell slot or spell components. While you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: House of Roulette
entries: {@i Spin the Wheel, Gambling on Your Lucky Numbers}

Like the Houses of Dice and Cards, Warmages of the House of Roulette are masters of the calculated gamble. Bearing a number of magical chips, they can push the odds when the need arises, pulling off longshot plays that other Warmages could only dream of.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Lucky Number
entries: Pick a Lucky Number from 1 to 100 If you roll that number on any {@dice d100} roll of your {@subclassFeature Spin the Wheel|Warmage|ValdaSpire24|Roulette|ValdaSpire24|3} feature, you gain the benefit of betting that number as a Single. You can change your Lucky Number whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Spinning Shield
entries: When a creature you can see makes an attack roll against you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to conjure your roulette wheel between yourself and the attacker. You and the attacker each roll a {@dice d100}. If your roll is equal or higher than that of the attacker, the attack misses, and you can't use this ability again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Cash Out
entries: You can unleash the energy stored within a Chip of Fate to escape a tight spot. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a Chip of Fate to teleport up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Everything on Black
entries: Whenever you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you regain 4 expended Chips of Fate. Additionally, whenever you expend one or more Chips of Fate to bet on a Single and win, you regain all of your expended Chips of Fate.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Infernum
entries: {@i Bargain with Fiends for Infernal Powers}

The Infernum are Investigators in league with Fiends, either willingly to pursue nefarious ends or unwillingly as the result of an infernal bargain. Each is given a set of enigmatic goals and a fiendish overseer (often an Imp), then left entirely to their own devices. Many search and scrounge for a solution to their fiendish bargain or opt for malicious compliance, delivering upon their infernal directives while undermining their broader schemes. Others, however, revel in their dark alliance, gleefully hoping to climb the fiendish ranks.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Infernal Bargain
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can strike one of the following bargains with your infernal masters. You can also discuss new bargains with your GM. The bargain lasts until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blindsight and Blindness
entries: You have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet. Beyond this range, you have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Damage and Actions
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can choose to take Necrotic damage equal to twice your Investigator level to take an additional action. This action can only be used to take only the {@action Attack|XPHB} (one attack only), {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, {@action Hide|XPHB}, or {@action Utilize|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Resistance and Vulnerability
entries: Choose two of the following damage types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, Psychic, and Thunder. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the chosen damage types. The GM chooses another type from the list; you have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to that damage type.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Binding Contract
entries: You add Geas to your grimoire for free. When you cast the spell using this feature, you can modify its casting to draft a binding contract. Instead of giving a verbal command, you write a legal contract that can contain up to 10 commands and conditions. You can include clauses that end the spell early or extend its duration to a maximum of 90 days. Instead of targeting a creature that you can see within range, the spell targets any creature that signs the contract within the duration.

A creature that willingly signs the contract as a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action automatically fails its saving throw against the spell, whether or not the creature understands the nature of the contract.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fiendish Transformation
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to shape-shift your {@subclassFeature Fiendish Familiar|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|Infernum|ValdaSpire24|3} into one of the following forms: {@creature Barbed Devil|XMM}, {@creature Incubus|XMM}, {@creature Succubus|XMM}, or {@creature Vrock|XMM}. It remains transformed for 1 minute or until you end it (no action required). While transformed, your familiar can attack.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Inquisitor
entries: {@i Drive Out Fiends and Root out Heresy}

The church has long been the first line of defense against the tide of impending darkness. Yet, the clergy's stubborn devotion to righteousness impedes them where it counts: you must sometimes be willing to do evil to counter evil. That's where the inquisition comes in.

As a righteous Inquisitor, you are tasked with rooting out heresy, exorcising demons, and stamping out any sign of the occult, and you are offered clemency for any action you take in the defense of the greater good. You may investigate anyone or anything you deem to be in line with the forces of evil, for you alone are a holy blade in the dark, the arbiter of your church.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Divine Strike
entries: Once on each of your turns when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action and hit a creature with a weapon, you can cause the target to take an extra {@damage 1d8} Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Rote Piety
entries: You can use your {@classFeature Holy Trinkets|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|7} three times without expending a use of your {@classFeature Trinkets|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|3}. You regain these uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Excommunication
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can emblazon a mark of condemnation upon a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be marked for 1 minute. While marked, the target takes {@damage 6d6} Radiant damage at the start of each of its turns, can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and can't have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests}. A marked target can repeat its saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Once you mark a creature using this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Rushed Incantation|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|2} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Jolly Roger
entries: {@i Command Your Crew on the High Seas}

The skull and crossbones of the Jolly Roger need no introduction: it means thieves, brigands, treasure, and adventure on the high seas. Moreover, it means the strong backs of a crew working in unison, piloting a ship from horizon to horizon under the command of a fierce captain and their first mate.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fancy Footwork
entries: Your elegant swordplay puts enemies where you want them. Whenever you hit a creature of Large size or smaller with a Melee weapon, you can force the target to move to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it, and you can move 5 feet. This movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dirty Tactics
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Melee weapon, you can use one of the following effects.

entries.name: Flank
entries: Your Cohort has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next melee attack roll it makes against the target while you are within 5 feet of it before the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Pocket Sand
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its next attack roll before the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Trip
entries: The target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition if it is Large or smaller.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: All Hands on Deck
entries: At your directive, your crew works in perfect unison. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can issue a series of directives to allies within 30 feet of yourself that can see or hear you. Each ally has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next {@dice D20} test it makes before the start of your next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Jolly Roger

entries: {@color {@style Cross-Compatible Subclass: This subclass originates from the {@color {@class Captain|ValdaSpire24}|3B7DAF} class|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style Note that cross-compatible subclasses might be stronger or weaker than other subclasses.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style The GM decides if a subclass should be cross-compatible in your campaign.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}

entries: {@b Level 10: Dirty Tactics.} The Flank benefit applies to any ally, instead of your Cohort.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Kid Sleuth
entries: {@i Solve Mysteries with Your Talking Animal Sidekick}

Though Kid Sleuths are not all literally youths, they are all amateur detectives with a knack for solving tricky crimes. Assisted by their ubiquitous animal sidekicks, Kid Sleuths will happily dive into the details of a grim crime scene to emerge with a handful of clues and a lead on the bad guy. These sleuths generally prefer to run away from trouble, rather than engage head-on, since mysteries only get harder to solve with more dead bodies, but they are more than capable of defending themselves if backed into a corner.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Split Up, Gang
entries: When you use your {@classFeature Exploit Weakness|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|5}, you can immediately move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. Alternatively, you can choose one ally you can see within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you. The ally can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Cunning Companion
entries: When your familiar takes the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Hide|XPHB} action, you gain the benefits of that action on your next turn. You must be {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} or behind {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover} or Total cover, and you must be out of any enemy's line of sight to gain the benefits of the {@action Hide|XPHB} action.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Meddling Kids
entries: Whenever an enemy within 30 feet of yourself makes an attack roll against one of your allies, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on that roll.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Occultist
entries: {@i Command Arcane Pact Magic}

Vampires, demons, lycanthropes, and Aberrations all have one thing in common: they are all magical threats, best combated through magical means. To meet these foes on a level playing field, Occultists indulge in arcana, filling their grimoires with magical secrets and mastering a handful of spells. Occultists are the most likely Investigators to cavort with Warlocks, borrow tricks from Wizards and magicians, and dabble in dark magic to defeat their foes.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Eldritch Ruin
entries: You can cast one of your Warlock cantrips as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Eyes of Another World
entries: Magical perception grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: See Invisibility
entries: You see creatures and objects that have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. You can also see into the Ethereal Plane. Creatures and objects there appear ghostly.

entries.name: Sense Spellcasters
entries: You can sense if a creature you can see has the ability to cast spells.

entries.name: Discern Otherworldly Origins
entries: You can determine if a creature you can see is an Aberration, Celestial, Elemental, Fey, or Fiend. You can also determine the creature's plane of origin, if it is native to a different plane of existence than the one you're on.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Maleficium
entries: When you use your {@classFeature Exploit Weakness|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|5}, you can cast {@spell Bestow Curse|XPHB} on the target as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} without a spell slot or components.

Once a creature fails a saving throw against this spell, you can't use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Rushed Incantation|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|2} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Knight Errant
entries: {@i Uphold Your Chivalrous Values}

Knights that have failed, forsaken, or betrayed their masters are known as Knights Errant. Though they no longer follow the dictates of a lord, these knights are usually reluctant to abandon their vows of ethics entirely. Many wander the lands seeking out honorable quests and worthy adversaries, for disgraced knights are knights nonetheless.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Inspiring Battlecry
entries: When you become {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you can give {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} to yourself and allies who can see or hear you within 30 feet of yourself (no action required).
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Redirection
entries: When a creature you can see hits an ally within 5 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force the attack to hit you instead. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage dealt by the triggering attack.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Surge of Valor
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to summon up a well of determination. Until the start of your next turn, you gain the following benefits. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending two Battle Dice (no action required).

entries.name: Unbreakable
entries: Whenever you take damage from an enemy, you can roll a Battle Die without expending it and reduce the damage taken by that roll.

entries.name: Undaunted
entries: Whenever you fail a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can roll a Battle Die without expending it and add it to the roll, potentially causing it to succeed.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mage Brand
entries: {@i Burn Magic Into Your Flesh}

Searing runes and arcane geometry into one's skin is an agonizing practice known as spellbranding. Though it was once used by tyrannical giants to imbue their conscripts with a mote of magical potential, spellbranding has long since been disparaged in polite society. However, a few that are willing and desperate enough to burn themselves with magical runes might still utilize that magic today. The so-called "Mage Brands" need none of a mage's intellect or a priest's faith; they need only tenacity and a tolerance for pain.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Strike
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with a casting of one of your {@filter Sorcerer cantrips that has a casting time of an action|spells|level=0|subclass=vagabond: mage brand (vss'24+)|cast time=action}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Desperate Ward
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects while you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Imprinted Spellscar
entries: When a creature casts a spell of level 5 or lower that deals damage to you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to temporarily imprint the spell upon yourself. You have this spell prepared and can cast it by expending a number of Battle Dice equal to the spell's level. The spell imprint vanishes after you cast it or when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can have a number of spell imprints up to your Charisma modifier at one time.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Lion Banner
entries: {@i Lead with Heroism and Zeal}

Captains who fly the Lion Banner are consummate leaders with forceful personalities and a penchant for heroics. Such Captains lead from the front, flying their banner high in battles where valor and luck turn the tide in their favor.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: High Morale
entries: You can use your Morale Boost maneuver when two or more creatures, including yourself, simultaneously fail a saving throw against the same effect, such as a dragon's breath weapon. Each creature that failed its saving throw gains the benefit of Morale Boost, and you only expend one Battle Die.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Vengeful Gambit
entries: When a creature under the effect of your Challenge maneuver hits you with an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the attack's damage for that attack and make an attack against that creature using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} as a part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Heroic Leadership
entries: When you use your Bolster or Rally maneuver, the target gains {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} if it doesn't already have it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mad Bomber
entries: {@i Blow Things Up}

While many "Mad Bombers" aren't actually mad, it takes a special kind of crazy to devote one's life to studying explosives. Most Alchemists who specialize in this field are incorrigible pyromaniacs who take great pleasure in burning, blasting, and blowing things up. Mad Bombers are always working to improve their {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bombs'} effectiveness.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Timed Demolition
entries: You can take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to set one of your {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bombs} with a timed detonation. Choose a duration of any number of rounds (any increment of 6 seconds) up to 10 minutes. The {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24} detonates using the {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bomb's} {@itemMastery Explode|ValdaGunslinger} property at the start of your turn after the chosen number of rounds. If a creature is within the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} of more than one {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24|Bomb's} explosion simultaneously, the creature is only affected by one {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24} of your choice.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Blast Shield
entries: Choose one damage type from among Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Overloaded Charge
entries: Whenever you use your {@classFeature Prime Bomb|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|2} and expend the maximum number of {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} you can expend, as shown in the Prime Bomb column for your Alchemist level, the {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24} is further empowered. You can add two additional {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} to the {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24} without expending them.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mechanauts' Guild
entries: {@i Pilot an Enormous Crab Tank}

For centuries, the pinnacle of mechanized vehicles was the Apparatus of the Crab, a singular device capable of exploring inhospitable environments, from the sea floor to lava-strewn volcanic fields. However, ambitious Craftsmen from the Mechanauts' Guild have drawn up designs for a new vehicle, mightier and more customizable than the old apparatus. This device is a walking tank, equipped with savage fists, scuttling legs, and climate control enhancements—a vehicle to dwarf all others, a true feat of engineering.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Frame Upgrade
entries: You gain one of the following upgrades of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace the chosen option with another one.

entries.name: Arachnotron Legs
entries: The apparatus has a Climb speed equal to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Diving Bell
entries: The apparatus has a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and contains a supply of air that allows creatures within it to breathe while it is underwater.

entries.name: Heavy Suspension
entries: The apparatus's jump distance triples, and it takes no damage from falling less than 100 feet.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Ejector Seat
entries: When you take damage while you're piloting the apparatus, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to eject yourself and any other creature inside of the apparatus. Each ejected creature lands in a space of its choice that it can see within 30 feet of the apparatus.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Magitech Upgrade
entries: You gain one of the following upgrades of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace the chosen option with another one. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Masterwork Bonus. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} and all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Ballista Cannon
entries: While piloting your apparatus, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to fire the apparatus's integrated heavy ballista in a 120-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. Each creature in the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} makes a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}), taking {@damage 10d6} Force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Missile Pod
entries: While piloting your apparatus, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to launch a salvo of micro-missiles in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the apparatus. Each creature you choose within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} takes Force damage equal to {@dice 5d6}.

entries.name: Rocket Engine
entries: While piloting your apparatus, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to light the apparatus's installed rocket engine. Until the end of your turn, the apparatus's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} doubles, it has a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and you can attack three times when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action using the apparatus on your turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Medium
entries: {@i Foretell the Future and Commune with the Dead}

As conduits between the living and dead, Mediums offer an essential glimpse past the veil of mortality. Using their auguries, séances, and divinations, Mediums can retrieve morsels of information from the afterlife to settle debts between the living or dead, and to assist ongoing investigations. This information, however cryptic, can point an interested party toward clues or evidence that only the deceased are able to provide.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Foretold Demise
entries: Once per turn when you deal damage with a weapon, you can replace one of the damage dice with a foretelling roll.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Whispers from Beyond
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can receive a hint from beyond. The GM gives a one-word hint pertaining to your best course of action, a fruitful line of inquiry, or some other useful direction.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Rushed Incantation|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|2} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Third Eye
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to cast {@spell True Seeing|XPHB} without a spell slot or components. When you cast the spell with this feature, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the first attack you make on each of your turns for the duration of this spell.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Musketeer
entries: {@i Lead Your Allies with Blades and Bullets}

You believe that camaraderie and glory go hand-in-hand, that you and your allies are undefeatable as long as you stand together. As a Musketeer, you have trained with blades and firearms in tandem so that you might battle shoulder-to-shoulder alongside your allies. Your place isn't taking shots from afar, but charging into the fray such that you might all succeed or fail as one.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Morale Boost
entries: When you use the {@optfeature Bite the Bullet|ValdaGunslinger} maneuver, choose up to 5 allies you can see within 30 feet of yourself. Each chosen ally gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to one roll of your Risk Die plus half your Gunslinger level (round down).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mobile Tactics
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack, the target can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you until the start of its next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: All for One
entries: Whenever an ally within 10 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a ranged attack using a weapon against the attacker.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mutagenist
entries: {@i Mutate Yourself to Adapt to Any Situation}

The study of alchemy is fundamentally the study of transformation. All Alchemists transmute mundane materials into magical substances—potions, elixirs, and bombs—yet some take it one step further. You have discovered the secrets of the mutagen, the keystone of transmutation, which allows you to transform your very body, gaining supernatural strength or speed, sprouting additional limbs or claws, or thickening your skin into a stony aegis.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Shared Mutagen
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1||Reagent} to inject an ally within 5 feet of you with a Mutagen of your choice. A creature can only be under the effect of one Mutagen at a time. Once you have injected another creature with a Mutagen, you can't do so again until the original Mutagen ends.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Advanced Mutation
entries: Whenever you inject yourself with a Mutagen, you can also gain one of the following mutations of your choice.

entries.name: Hyperelastic
entries: Your flesh takes on a rubbery quality, allowing you to bend and stretch with ease. Your reach is 5 feet greater than normal. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks and saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Mucilaginous
entries: Your skin secretes a thick, extremely sticky substance that helps you adhere to objects. You can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings, while leaving your hands free. You also have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Polybrachia
entries: You grow a pair of additional arms. These arms are fully functional and can be used to hold weapons and shields (allowing you to wield two {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} weapons, or four one-handed weapons), perform Somatic components of spells, and perform other actions, though the arms themselves don't grant you any additional actions.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mutated Blood
entries: Choose Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution. The chosen ability score increases by 2, to a maximum of 22. When a Mutagen is applied to that ability score, its maximum increases to 25. You can change this ability score increase when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Necrodancer
entries: {@i Groove Down}

Neon lights, thumping beats, and impeccable fashion are the calling cards of Necrodancers, spellcasters that see the potential for {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} to create the greatest troupe of backup dancers of all time. A Necrodancer's minions don't shamble aimlessly, but instead move in perfect rhythm with one another, busting moves and empowering their master through choreography.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Graveyard Tango
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 5 {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1} points to bestow your grace and style on an ally. Choose an ally within 30 feet of yourself that can see or hear you to gain the bonus to AC, damage rolls, and {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} that use Dexterity or Charisma from your {@subclassFeature Backup Dancers|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|Necrodancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|3} feature until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Disco of the Dead
entries: Whenever one of your thralls takes the Dance action, you can choose for it to enter the Ethereal Plane until the start of its next turn. While on the Ethereal Plane, it can affect and be affected only by creatures, objects, and effects on that plane. An ethereal thrall is faintly visible in a blur of disco lights.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Thriller [Lichdom]
entries: You have reached the pinnacle of Necromancy and transformed yourself into a lich. You appear ageless, with smooth, alabaster skin, and boast supernatural grace and rhythm. You gain the following benefits in addition to those of your {@classFeature Lichdom|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|20} feature.

entries.name: Dance-Off
entries: You take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and expend 20 {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1} points to magically challenge up to ten creatures you can see within 60 feet of you to a dance competition. Each creature you challenge makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC, taking {@damage 8d6} Psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Moonwalk
entries: You can cast {@spell Freedom of Movement|XPHB} on your thralls or yourself without a spell slot.

entries.name: Smooth Criminal
entries: Your Dexterity and Charisma scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Nightgaunt
entries: {@i Side With the Forces of Undeath}

Blood-drinkers, Undead, and other creatures of the night are often feared and hunted, and few stand in their defense; except, of course, the grim and terrible Nightgaunts. Tales of Nightgaunts cast them as hunters of clerics and goodly vampire slayers. Their appearances always presage long nights and great rises in hungry Undead.

You felt the calling of the moon bringing you to the graveside of living corpses. Though vampires, zombies, and skeletons are mighty, they are always outnumbered, hunted, and turned by Clerics—never given a chance to repose in peace. They require an ally among the living to continue their ceaseless lives, and you have risen by moonlight to the task.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Innate Necromancy
entries: You can cast any of the following spells once without a spell slot: {@spell Darkness|XPHB}, {@spell False Life|XPHB}, {@spell Gentle Repose|XPHB}, and {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this feature (choose the ability when you cast the spell). Once you cast a spell using this feature, you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Undying
entries: You can use your {@classFeature Survive|Warden|ValdaSpire24|9} three times and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Gravelord
entries: You can invite necromantic energies into your body. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain the benefits below for 1 minute or until you choose to end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Frightful Aura
entries: You emit an aura of terror in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from yourself. Whenever an enemy starts its turn in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. {@action Attack|XPHB} rolls against the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Vampiric Strike
entries: As a part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you take to use this feature, you can cast {@spell Vampiric Touch|XPHB} without a spell slot as a level 5 spell. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace one of your attacks with making the spell's melee spell attack.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Ooze Rancher
entries: {@i Brew Bottled Ooze Minions}

Unsurprisingly, Oozes, jellies, and slimes are a fascinating subject for Alchemists who wish to figure out how inanimate chemicals can form together and rise up in a moving, hungry mass. The answer to this question may very well be at the heart of alchemy itself. Alchemists who choose to research slimes in depth are called Ooze Ranchers, for they breed and keep numerous slimes upon which to experiment.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bottled Oozes
entries: Whenever you brew potions, you can spend 2 {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} to create a Bottled Ooze, which contains a {@creature Gray Ooze|XMM}. This item retains potency until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, after which it becomes inert. This item counts toward the number of potions you have brewed at one time.

An Ooze produced by your Bottled Oozes uses your Intelligence modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} for its attack rolls. If the Ooze forces a creature to make a saving throw, it uses your Alchemist save DC.

entries.name: Improved Bottled Oozes
entries: At higher Alchemist levels, you can distill more powerful slimes into Bottled Oozes that you create, as shown on the Improved Bottled Oozes table. An Ooze by your Bottled Ooze can't take the Split {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sacrificial Slime
entries: Whenever you are targeted by an attack while an allied Ooze is within 5 feet of you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force the attack to target the Ooze instead.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore one use of it by expending 2 {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Elemental Oozes
entries: Whenever you create a Bottled Ooze, choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder damage. The Ooze has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to that damage. Whenever it is subjected to that damage type, it takes no damage and instead regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the damage dealt.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Overlord
entries: {@i Command an Army of Obedient Undead}

There are few ambitions that capture the imagination more than the power to rule. From peasantry to nobility, many dream of a world in which they are in charge. Some Necromancers, known as Overlords, view their magic as a means to accomplish this pervasive dream. Seeking control both on and off the battlefield, Overlords leverage their dark magic to bolster their allies and manipulate their foes.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Despotic Discourse
entries: You gain a bonus to Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}, {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, and {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sacrificial Thralls
entries: When you're hit by an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force that attack to instead hit one of your thralls that is within 5 feet of you.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Tyrant [Lichdom]
entries: You have reached the pinnacle of Necromancy and transformed yourself into a lich. Your desire for control has warped your transformation, transforming you into a tyrant lich. Your flesh and bone decay, reducing you to nothing more than two glowing dots beneath a hood. You gain the following benefits in addition to those of your {@classFeature Lichdom|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|20} feature.

entries.name: Possession
entries: If you drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can choose to possess a nearby body instead of reforming at your spirit jar. When you do so, choose a Humanoid or one of your thralls within 120 feet of yourself. A Humanoid must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC or be possessed. A creature that succeeds its saving throw against your {@variantrule Possession|XPHB} is immune to your {@variantrule Possession|XPHB} for 24 hours.

When you possess a body, you control it, but a Humanoid target retains awareness. Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the body, though you retain your alignment and your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You retain your own class features and feats. If the target has any class levels, you can't use any of its class features.

A possessed Humanoid can repeat its saving throw every 8 hours. On a success, the {@variantrule Possession|XPHB} ends and you are ejected from the body. The {@variantrule Possession|XPHB} also ends if the body drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or you choose to end it as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Domination Spells
entries: You can expend Charnel Touch points to cast one of the spells from the Domination Spells table without a spell slot.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Pale Master
entries: {@i Achieve the Archetypal Powers of Lichdom}

When the need for superiority drives a Necromancer, there is no end to their ambition. Such Necromancers, known as Pale Masters, work feverishly to master every corner of necromantic magic, less out of the desire to improve themselves and more out of spite for their rivals.

This perhaps speaks to a dirty secret of Necromancy: most Necromancers hate each other. Bitter rivalries, grudges, and insignificant slights motivate Pale Masters to embrace lichdom with unequaled fervor, for to master Necromancy means to accept no equals.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Chilling Disposition
entries: You begin assuming the terrible aspect of a lich, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Intelligent Intimidation
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} skill, if you didn't have it already. Additionally, you gain a bonus to checks using this skill equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

entries.name: Frightening Gaze
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 10 {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1} points to fix your horrific gaze on a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Thrall Rush
entries: Whenever you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can empty the contents of your {@classFeature Dead Space|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|2} and each of your thralls can move up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Archlich [Lichdom]
entries: You have reached the pinnacle of Necromancy and transformed yourself into a lich. Your skin clings tightly to your bones, your muscles wither, and your eyes turn milky and dull. Yet, through the veil of weakness, your body exudes unbelievable arcane power. You gain the following benefits in addition to those of your {@classFeature Lichdom|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|20} feature.

entries.name: Devour Soul
entries: When you reduce an enemy to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can immediately devour its soul (no action required). Roll a {@dice d8} and regain expended spell slots of your choice whose combined level is no greater than the number rolled. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
A creature whose soul is devoured can't be restored to life by any means short of a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Paralyzing Touch
entries: When you deal 30 or more damage with {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1}, the target has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Pharaoh
entries: {@i Embrace Pseudo-Divinity}

The godlike monarchs of ancient kingdoms practiced a unique style of Necromancy, forgotten to time. Through the extraction of organs, the desiccation of flesh, and innumerable enchantments, those ancient pharaohs were able to rule their subjects as divine, Undead beings, long past their mortal deaths. While those kingdoms have been lost to the shifting sands and wild jungles of the world, their methods have been preserved in the carvings of colossal temples and revived by modern Necromancers, who take on the guise of the erstwhile pharaohs. Their magic is a hybrid of divine and arcane influences, the legacy of deific monarchs from a forgotten age.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mock Divinity
entries: You can convincingly reflect the trappings of a demigod walking the earth. When you cast {@spell Thaumaturgy|XPHB}, you can use any number of its effects. Additionally, you can create the following effects.

entries.name: Avatar
entries: At a point within range, you manifest a Huge illusory avatar for 1 minute. You determine the avatar's appearance. It mimics your movements and projects your speech in a booming voice.

entries.name: Gathering Storm
entries: Clouds gather and churn overhead for 1 minute. You determine the appearance of the clouds and whether they are accompanied by thunder, lightning, or a light rain.

entries.name: Sun and Moon
entries: You can brighten or darken the sun or moon for 1 minute. Within range, you can change {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB} to {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} to {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}, or vice versa.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Scarab of Judgment
entries: You can expend a use of your {@subclassFeature Channel Divinity|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|Pharaoh|ValdaSpire24|3} to transfer life from the Undead to the living. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can touch one of your thralls and choose a willing Humanoid you can see within 60 feet of you. The Undead is destroyed and reduced to dust, and the Humanoid regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the Undead's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Once a creature regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} in this way, it can't do so again until it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mummy Lord [Lichdom]
entries: You have reached the pinnacle of Necromancy and transformed yourself into a lich. This entails undergoing the ancient funeral rites of the pharaohs, removing your organs and entombing your body in a sarcophagus amongst your worldly possessions. You become the oldest and most exalted type of lich: a mummy lord. You gain the following benefits in addition to those of your {@classFeature Lichdom|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|20} feature.

entries.name: Canopic Jars
entries: Your spirit jar is a set of four canopic jars containing your stomach, lungs, intestines, and liver. Each one has a specific weakness, which you must discuss with your GM. Your rejuvenation is only stopped when all four canopic jars are destroyed. When you are destroyed, you reform at your sarcophagus.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Mummy Rot
entries: When you deal 20 or more damage with {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1}, the target is cursed. While cursed, the target can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum doesn't return to normal when finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, and its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum decreases by {@dice 3d6} every 24 hours that elapse. A creature dies and turns to dust if reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} by this attack.

entries.name: Whirlwind of Sand
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can transform into a whirlwind of sand, move up to 60 feet, and revert to your normal form. While in whirlwind form, you are Immune to all damage and to the {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, {@condition Prone|XPHB}, {@condition Restrained|XPHB}, and {@condition Stunned|XPHB} conditions. Equipment you are wearing or carrying remains in your possession.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Pigmentist
entries: {@i Splash Paint Everywhere to Support Your Allies}

One of the lesser-known duties of Alchemists is synthesizing new and increasingly vibrant pigments from mundane and magical materials—in many cases, creating entirely new colors. Alchemists that specialize in this field are called Pigmentists. An artful and imaginative lot, they seek to brighten the world with their newly-invented hues, or failing that, simply splatter it with marvelous combinations of paint.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Palette Portals
entries: You mix your paint with conjuration magic. Once on each of your turns, you can spend 10 feet of your movement to enter any area of wet paint within 5 feet of you, emerging from another area of wet paint within 60 feet of you. Both areas of paint must be at least the same size as you and must have been coated within the last minute.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Pigment Potions
entries: Whenever you brew a potion, you can add a pigment from the Magical Pigments table. When a creature drinks this potion, they also gain the benefits of a {@item Potion of Resistance|XDMG} of the corresponding damage type for 1 minute.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Splatter Bombs
entries: Your Paint Bombs are improved in the following ways:

entries.name: Rainbow Blast
entries: You can add up to three colors from the Magical Pigments table when you throw a Paint Bomb.

entries.name: Selective Splatter
entries: The extra damage of your Magical Pigments improves to {@dice 1d8}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Pistolero
entries: {@i Fire Six-Shooters with Incredible Speed}

Bullets are power, and you have long believed that more bullets equal more power. Your expertise is in delivering a hail of deadly fire to pulverize your enemies. Not every bullet needs to be accurate to make a difference.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Disarm
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} and trigger your {@classFeature Gut Shot|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|5} feature against a creature, you can disarm the target instead of lodging a projectile in it. The target drops one object of your choice that it's holding, with the object landing in a space of your choice up to 15 feet away from the target.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Showdown [Maneuver]
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can expend one Risk Die to draw a Ranged weapon and make an attack using it. Add the Risk Die to the damage roll. On a hit, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against creatures other than you on the first round of combat.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bullet Time
entries: Once on each of your turns when you make a ranged attack using a weapon, you can gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Plague Doctor
entries: {@i Cure Sickness with Brutal Medical Practices}
As maladies sweep the countryside, plague doctors follow close behind. Wielding brutal medical instruments and techniques to balance the humors, plague doctors inspire hope and fear in equal measure.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Imbalance Humors
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can imbalance its humors using one of the following options. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend one Battle Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

entries.name: Choleric
entries: Until the start of your next turn, the target has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and attack rolls against it also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Melancholic
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} it makes before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Phlegmatic
entries: The target can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} until the start of its turn.

entries.name: Sanguine
entries: The next time the target takes damage before the start of your next turn, it takes extra Necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Battle Die without expending it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Analgesic Remedy
entries: When you use your Remedy maneuver, you can give yourself or the ally {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Vagabond level.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bloodletting
entries: You learn the Wounding Strike maneuver. If you already know it, you learn a different maneuver of your choice.

You can use your Wounding Strike maneuver by expending 1-3 Battle Dice. You add only one Battle Die to the attack's damage roll, but the target gains a number of bleeding wounds equal to the number of Battle Dice expended.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Plague Doctor

entries: {@color {@style Cross-Compatible Subclass: This subclass originates from the {@color {@class Vagabond|ValdaSpire24Extras}|63A7A0} class|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style Note that cross-compatible subclasses might be stronger or weaker than other subclasses.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style The GM decides if a subclass should be cross-compatible in your campaign.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@i Cure Sickness with Brutal Medical Practices}
As maladies sweep the countryside, plague doctors follow close behind. Wielding brutal medical instruments and techniques to balance the humors, plague doctors inspire hope and fear in equal measure.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Imbalance Humors
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can imbalance its humors using one of the following options. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend one Battle Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

entries.name: Choleric
entries: Until the start of your next turn, the target has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and attack rolls against it also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Melancholic
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} it makes before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Phlegmatic
entries: The target can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} until the start of its turn.

entries.name: Sanguine
entries: The next time the target takes damage before the start of your next turn, it takes extra Necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Battle Die without expending it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Analgesic Remedy
entries: When you use your Remedy maneuver, you can give yourself or the ally {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Vagabond level.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bloodletting
entries: You learn the Wounding Strike maneuver. If you already know it, you learn a different maneuver of your choice.

You can use your Wounding Strike maneuver by expending 1-3 Battle Dice. You add only one Battle Die to the attack's damage roll, but the target gains a number of bleeding wounds equal to the number of Battle Dice expended.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Plague Doctor

entries: {@color {@style Cross-Compatible Subclass: This subclass originates from the {@color {@class Vagabond|ValdaSpire24Extras}|63A7A0} class|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}

{@i Cure Sickness with Brutal Medical Practices}
As maladies sweep the countryside, plague doctors follow close behind. Wielding brutal medical instruments and techniques to balance the humors, plague doctors inspire hope and fear in equal measure.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Imbalance Humors
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can imbalance its humors using one of the following options. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend one Battle Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

entries.name: Choleric
entries: Until the start of your next turn, the target has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and attack rolls against it also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Melancholic
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} it makes before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Phlegmatic
entries: The target can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} until the start of its turn.

entries.name: Sanguine
entries: The next time the target takes damage before the start of your next turn, it takes extra Necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Battle Die without expending it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Analgesic Remedy
entries: When you use your Remedy maneuver, you can give yourself or the ally {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Vagabond level.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bloodletting
entries: You learn the Wounding Strike maneuver. If you already know it, you learn a different maneuver of your choice.

You can use your Wounding Strike maneuver by expending 1-3 Battle Dice. You add only one Battle Die to the attack's damage roll, but the target gains a number of bleeding wounds equal to the number of Battle Dice expended.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Plague Lord
entries: {@i Harness the Vile Power of Sickness and Rot}

If elemental Necromancy thrives anywhere on the Material Plane, it is perhaps at a miniscule size of a bacterium. There, the greatest of plagues are born to ravage entire kingdoms and continents with inexorable sickness. Necromancers that seeks to harness this form of Necromancy are known as Plague Lords, commanders of vermin and disease alike.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Projectile Spew
entries: Your reach with {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1} and spells with a range of Touch is 10 feet greater than normal, as magically imbued projectile vomit delivers the effect.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bloated Thralls
entries: When one of your thralls is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or you release it, you can cause it to explode in a shower of toxic gore. Each creature you choose within 5 feet of the thrall makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} Poison damage and has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much Poison damage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Corpulent Lich [Lichdom]
entries: You have reached the pinnacle of Necromancy and transformed yourself into a lich. Your obsession with disease and rot has affected your transformation: you bloat like a waterlogged corpse and your skin turns a sickly green. You gain the following benefits in addition to those of your {@classFeature Lichdom|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|20} feature.

entries.name: Gore Burst
entries: When you drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, your body explodes in a shower of necromantic energy.

Each creature you choose within 20 feet of you makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Necromancer spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 5d10} Poison damage and {@damage 5d10} Necrotic damage and has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Master of Disease
entries: When you deal 25 or more damage with {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1}, the target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and is cursed for 1 minute. Choose two of the following effects which afflict the target while it is cursed. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, ending the curse and the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on a success.

entries.name: Bleeding
entries: Each time the target takes damage, it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage

entries.name: Disadvantage
entries: Choose one ability. The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ability checks and saving throws made with that ability.

entries.name: Garbled
entries: The target can't speak coherently or cast spells with a Verbal component.

entries.name: Red-Eye
entries: The target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition beyond 10 feet.

entries.name: Unsteady
entries: The target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition at the end of each of its turns.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Pugilist
entries: {@i Crush Foes with Your Fists}

Knuckles crack and a meaty fist rears back to crush bone. Pugilists are hand-to-hand brawlers with a tolerance for pain and a willingness to inflict it at a moment's notice. Unlike martial artists that emphasize speed and precision, Pugilists leverage brute force in their blows. Why strike several times when once will do?

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Intimidating Blow
entries: You learn the Horrific Strike maneuver. If you already know it, you learn a different maneuver of your choice.

When you use Horrific Strike, you can perform a frightening display in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you. Each creature you choose in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Maneuver save DC or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Desperate Endurance
entries: When you fail a saving throw while you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you can choose to succeed instead.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Knockout [Maneuver]
entries: When you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend three Battle Dice as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to attempt to knock the target out. Add the Battle Dice to the attack's damage roll. If the target has fewer {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} than three times your Vagabond level after taking damage, it has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition until it regains any {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
