subclassFeaturesFull.name: Purple Magic
entries: {@i Enchant and Beguile Your Foes}

Purple Magic holds sway over the domains of illusions and enchantments that take hold over people's minds, as well as anything that is not quite as it seems. Practitioners of this craft are puppet masters, shaping the apparent reality around them with the ease of a marionette.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: False Authority
entries: When you cast {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB}, you can modify it so that you appear as a figure of authority to anyone who sees you. You don't choose your appearance; rather, your appearance varies from observer to another. For example, a blacksmith might see you as a guild master, whereas a soldier might see you as a captain.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Deceitful Transposition
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to create an illusory disguise over two creatures within 60 feet of yourself, making it seem as if they have teleported and switched places. The disguise extends to the target's voices, sounds, smells, etc. Disguised creatures don't perceive any part of the illusion.

A creature can take a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a magically disguised creature and make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC. On a success, the creature can see both illusory creatures for what they are.

This illusion lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if either disguised creature takes an action that the other can't take (such as casting a spell), if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or if you dismiss it (no action required).
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Waking Nightmare
entries: You can warp everything a creature sees into a hellscape full of terrible creatures. When a creature fails its saving throw against your {@spell Hex: Hallucination|ValdaSpire24} cantrip, you can further distort its mind. The creature has the Frenzied condition. A creature with the Frenzied condition loses the ability to distinguish between friend and foe, regarding all creatures it can see as enemies. While Frenzied, the creature chooses the targets for its attacks, spells, and abilities randomly from among the creatures it can see within range, and it must make an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} if any creature provokes one. The Frenzied condition ends after 1 minute, or when the spell ends.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Reanimator
entries: {@i Stitch Together Terrible Minions}

Through bubbling test tubes and sparking electrodes, you have discovered the true heart of Necromancy: mad science. You've experimented in far-reaching disciplines of surgery, alchemy, and physics, using your animated minions as gruesome test subjects and walking surgical dummies. Most crucially, you have discovered that lightning can imbue almost anything with a semblance of life, from the smallest severed muscle to the most towering golems.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Lazarus Bolt
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can drive a bolt into the torso of a creature within 5 feet of you that has died within the last minute and shock it back to life. That creature revives with 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} and gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Necromancer level. This feature can't return to life a creature that lacks a heart, a creature that has died of old age, or a creature that is missing vital organs.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending 20 {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1} points (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Quick Stitch
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can apply a {@subclassFeature Spell-Stitch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|Reanimator|ValdaSpire24|3} to one of your thralls, expending {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1} points as normal. This stitch lasts for 10 minutes and can exceed the thrall's maximum of two stitches.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Patchwork Golem [Lichdom]
entries: You have reached the pinnacle of Necromancy and transformed yourself into a lich. Through abominable works of alchemy and surgery, you have constructed an artificial body to act as the vessel for your soul. You gain the following benefits in addition to those of your {@classFeature Lichdom|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|20} feature.

entries.name: Golem Body
entries: Your spirit jar is your artificial golem body. It has a specific weakness, which you must discuss with your GM. Your rejuvenation is only stopped when your body is completely destroyed using its weakness. When you drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you temporarily die and reanimate with half of your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} after 1 hour.

entries.name: Gruesome Physicality
entries: Your Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores become 20 if they weren't already higher.

entries.name: Damage Resistance
entries: You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

entries.name: Self-Stitches
entries: You can apply any number of Spell-Stitches to yourself as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, expending {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1} points as normal. {@subclassFeature Spell-Stitch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|Reanimator|ValdaSpire24|3|ValdaSpire24|Spell-Stitches} applied in this way last until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Reaper
entries: {@i Become One with the Shadows}

The oblivion of death is the wellspring Necromancy, a dark abyss into which all Necromancers stare. Those few Necromancers who forsake their souls outright might become Reapers, figures of shadow and demise that beckon others to the afterlife. For performing this deed, they strengthen their connection to that distant oblivion until they are but tenebrous shadows: harbingers of an inevitable end.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Umbral Form
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can flatten your body into a shadow upon the floor. You remain in Umbral Form until you end this effect as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. While in Umbral Form, the following rules apply.

entries.name: Inactive
entries: You can't take any action, {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, other than to leave the form.

entries.name: Immunities
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Prone|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Difficult Target
entries: Attacks against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Invisible in Darkness
entries: While entirely in {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition to any creature that relies on {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} to see you in that {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} doubles and you gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. You can move across difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without needing to make an ability check. As a shadow, you can only move along surfaces; you can't jump or fly.

entries.name: Gear
entries: Your equipment merges with your Umbral Form and has no effect until you leave the form.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Wraith Flight
entries: Each of your thralls gains a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. If it already has a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB}, its {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} is doubled. Additionally, your thralls don't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} while flying.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Harbinger [Lichdom]
entries: You have reached the pinnacle of Necromancy and transformed yourself into a lich. You have become an embodiment of death itself. Clad in shadows, you seem little more than a skeletal presence in a foreboding robe, a sight that all people fear to behold. You gain the following benefits in addition to those of your {@classFeature Lichdom|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|20} feature.

entries.name: Death's Touch
entries: When you use your {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1} and roll an 11 or higher on the {@dice d20} for the attack roll, you hit the target, regardless of its AC.

entries.name: Fell Flight
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 60 feet.

entries.name: Grim Harvest
entries: When you kill a Medium or Small creature that isn't Undead using {@classFeature Charnel Touch|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|1}, you rip its soul from its body, which animates as a {@creature Specter|XMM} under your control and counts as one of your thrall.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Red Magic
entries: {@i Lay Your Foes to Waste with Arcane Fury}

Arcane magic tied to channeling the elements is deemed Red Magic, and is extremely hazardous when used. Witches that specialize in this craft are among the deadliest spellcasters in existence, channeling their curse into unhindered arcane wrath.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Convolute Energy
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself deals Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage to one or more creatures, you can change that damage type to one of the other listed types (no action required).
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Invulnerability
entries: When a creature that you can see hits you with an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage you take from the attack by 50, to a minimum of 0.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 4+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Elemental Annihilation
entries: When you cast a level 1+ Witch spell that deals Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage, you can expend another spell slot of equal or higher level to deal maximum damage with that spell on the turn you cast it.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Resonator
entries: {@i Use Acoustics to Shape the Battlefield}

The explosive force of an Alchemist's {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24} isn't just fire—it is a wave that can be shaped and focused. Alchemists who realize this and pursue the science of waves are deemed Resonators for their oft-revisited subject, resonant frequencies. Perhaps such frequencies are at the center of all alchemical pursuits, for with the right frequencies, a Resonator can warp explosions, concuss dragons, and vibrate steel to pieces.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Flashbang
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can throw a concussive explosive at your feet. Each Large or smaller creature of your choice within 10 feet of you can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} until the start of your next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (a minimum of once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Audio Enhancer
entries: Because of your thunderous Bombs, you have created a listening device to aid your hearing, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: You have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet.

entries.name: Thunder Immunity
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Thunder damage and the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Reverb Explosions
entries: When you use its {@itemMastery Explode|ValdaGunslinger} property, you can expend 4 {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1} to create a reverb explosion. If the {@item Bomb|ValdaSpire24} deals damage, all of its damage dice decrease by 1 step (d12s → d10s → d8s → d6s → d4s, to a minimum of d4s). At the start of your next turn, the explosion occurs again with the same area and damage, but its damage dice are decreased by a further 1 step.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Rimekeeper
entries: {@i Channel the Polar Winds}

Your call was the howling, icy winds of a remote arctic land. As a Rimekeeper, you defend the people of these frigid lands from colossal creatures that thrive in the frost and invaders that hail from warmer places. Wherever you travel, the north wind follows, summoned at your fingertips with hailstones and ice.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Ice Blast
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can unleash a burst of ice from your hands. You can use this ice to create one of the following magical effects of your choice within 5 feet of you. If an effect calls for a saving throw or ability check, the DC equals 8 plus your Constitution modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Black Ice
entries: You can create a slick area of ice covering the ground in a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} centered on yourself. When the ice appears, each creature other than yourself standing in its area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. A creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there must also succeed on that save or fall {@condition Prone|XPHB}. This ice melts after 1 minute or if you create this effect again.

entries.name: Freeze Shut
entries: You freeze over a closed door, window, gate, container, or hatch, causing it to become stuck. A Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check can force the object open again. This ice melts after 10 minutes.

entries.name: Frostbite
entries: You bombard a creature you can see with frost. The target makes a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 2d12} Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. This damage increases by {@dice 1d12} at Warden levels 11 ({@dice 3d12}) and 17 ({@dice 4d12}).

entries.name: Snowbank
entries: You deposit enough snow and ice in a 10-foot-wide bank to provide {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} for two Medium creatures. This bank melts after 10 minutes.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Snowclad
entries: You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Constitution modifier at the start of each of your turns if you don't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Hoarfrost Herald
entries: You can embrace the bitter chill of hoarfrost. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain the benefits below for 1 minute or until you choose to end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Cold Immunity
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage.

entries.name: Frostbite Strike
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace one of your attacks with a use of the Frostbite option of your {@subclassFeature Ice Blast|Warden|ValdaSpire24|Rimekeeper|ValdaSpire24Extras|6}.

entries.name: Iceclad
entries: You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Constitution modifier at the start of each of your turns if you don't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Rōnin
entries: {@i Master the Sword to Survive in a Harsh World}

You were once an honorable blademaster without peer. But those days are long gone. Disgraced and despised, people know you only as a dangerous swordmaster—someone to be feared. You may search for purpose, a way to redeem the black mark on your honor, or simply to survive another day in your endless journey. Perhaps your broken vows still guide you, or perhaps you have abandoned all semblance of honor; only your conduct and your blade define you.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Lone Wolf
entries: You're used to being outnumbered, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Outnumbered, Not Outmatched
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and there are more enemies than allies in the {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} order, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll.

entries.name: Stand Alone
entries: While no ally is within 5 feet of you and you don't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, enemies can't have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against you.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Killing Stroke
entries: When a creature you can see within 5 feet of yourself makes an attack against you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make one attack with a Melee weapon against the attacker. You can draw a weapon as a part of this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. Resolve your attack before the triggering attack. On a hit, the triggering attack automatically misses you.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend two Battle Dice (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Swordmaster
entries: Once per turn when you miss with an attack roll, you can repeat that attack against the same target.

entries.name: Outnumbered, Not Outmatched
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and there are more enemies than allies in the {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} order, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll.

entries.name: Stand Alone
entries: While no ally is within 5 feet of you and you don't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, enemies can't have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against you.

{@i Master the Sword to Survive in a Harsh World}

You were once an honorable blademaster without peer. But those days are long gone. Disgraced and despised, people know you only as a dangerous swordmaster—someone to be feared. You may search for purpose, a way to redeem the black mark on your honor, or simply to survive another day in your endless journey. Perhaps your broken vows still guide you, or perhaps you have abandoned all semblance of honor; only your conduct and your blade define you.

entries: You're used to being outnumbered, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Outnumbered, Not Outmatched
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and there are more enemies than allies in the {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} order, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll.

entries.name: Stand Alone

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Siegeball Jersey
entries: {@i Cheer and Coach Your Team to Victory}

Siegeball is a beloved sport, and Captains adorned with a Siegeball Jersey live and breathe it. Such Captains view the entire world through sports metaphors and place themselves in the privileged position of the team captain or perhaps the coach. Foes are naturally the opposing team, the referees, or even a rowdy crowd. Quests are no different from a sports season, in which the team is destined to break records and bring home the cup. For Siegeball Captains, sportsmanship and rowdy competition go hand-in-hand. One can expect rousing speeches and inappropriate jeers meted out between downfield sprints and breathtaking tackles.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Game Plan
entries: When you use your Blitz feature, you can direct your Cohort or an ally within 60 feet of yourself to take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to use one of the following options.

entries.name: Defensive Tackle
entries: The chosen ally moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and uses the Grapple or Shove option of its {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: Go Long
entries: The chosen ally moves up to twice its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Take Cover
entries: The chosen ally moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and takes the {@action Hide|XPHB} action. It has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on its Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Athletic Constitution
entries: When you make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw, you can make a Constitution saving throw with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} instead.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend one Battle Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Game-Winning Play
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to delay the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition. You can immediately move up to twice your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} and take an action and a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. Taking damage causes {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} failures as normal, and three {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} failures can still kill you. Following this, you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition if you still have 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Skull Banner
entries: {@i Command a Loyal Undead Cohort}

Captains who fly the Skull Banner are grim heralds of an Undead tide. Their Cohorts and followers are shambling corpses or ethereal ghosts, hellbent on consuming and corrupting the living. Necromancers by any other name, Captains of the Skull possess little of the arcane talent beyond what is necessary to command an Undead army; little else is needed to make them formidable adversaries.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Undead Horde
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, can cast {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} without a spell slot targeting the corpse of a Medium or Small Humanoid that has died within the last minute. When you cast the spell in this way, the Undead counts as your Cohort for your Captain features and uses your Charisma for its attack and damage rolls. This Undead lasts for 10 minutes, after which it crumbles into dust.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sacrificial Thralls
entries: Whenever you are targeted by an attack while an Undead you control is within 5 feet of you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to command it to dive in the way of the attack, causing the attack to target the Undead instead.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend one Battle Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Necromantic Burst
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can release a burst of negative energy in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} centered on a corpse you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Each creature you choose within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} makes a Constitution saving throw against your Maneuver save DC, taking {@damage 10d8} Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Undead you control within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half of the Necrotic damage dealt.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sky Magic
entries: {@i Soar Through the Sky With Ease}

Although all Witches appreciate a good {@item Broom of Flying|XDMG}, Sky Magic Witches embrace the power of the winds. Known colloquially as "Cloud Witches", they spend as much time aloft as they do on the ground, floating over their contemporaries with a breezy disposition.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Corvid Familiar
entries: When you summon your familiar, you can transform it into a crowlike hybrid with black feathers and beady eyes. It gains the following benefits.

entries.name: Flight
entries: It gains a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 50 feet (unless it already has a faster {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB}).

entries.name: Aerial Agility
entries: While the familiar is flying, it has a +2 bonus to its AC.

entries.name: Common
entries: It can speak and understand Common.

entries.name: Flyby
entries: The target doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Vortex
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can create a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of twisting wind originating from you. The {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} lasts for 1 minute, until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or you dismiss it (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required). The {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} has the following effects.

entries.name: Difficult Terrain
entries: The {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for creatures you choose.

entries.name: Disadvantage for Ranged Attacks
entries: Ranged attacks through the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. Heavy projectiles, such as boulders and ballista bolts, are unaffected.

entries.name: Disperse Gasses
entries: The {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} disperses gasses and vapor within its area.

entries.name: Windswept
entries: Small or smaller flying creatures can't move through the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Cloud Dancer
entries: Whenever you are hit by an attack while you are flying or falling, roll a {@dice d4}. On a 4, the attack misses you.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Spy
entries: {@i Infiltrate, Assassinate, and Lie with Aplomb}

Infiltration, disguise, and lying through their teeth: these are the principal skills of a Spy. A talented Spy rarely needs to draw a dagger to silence someone, for their honeyed words and agreeable disposition are all that is needed to draw out someone's secrets. Of course, when they do strike, it is decisive and without warning. Such skills are invaluable for governments and organizations of all types, used for stealing confidential information, sabotage, monitoring persons of interest, and everything in between.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Cloak and Dagger
entries: When you deal damage during the first round of combat, you can deal extra Force damage to the target if the target hasn't taken a turn yet or if you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll against the target. The Force damage equals your Investigator level.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Body Double
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can assume the identity of a Humanoid or a corpse of a Humanoid that you touch that has been dead for no longer than 24 hours. An illusion causes your appearance to perfectly match the target, including clothing, armor, weapons, and other belongings. If the target is a corpse, you resemble the Humanoid as it appeared in life. Additionally, the corpse, its blood, clothing, and other physical evidence of its death, become magically {@condition invisible} for 8 hours.

To discern that you are disguised, a creature must take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to inspect your appearance and succeed on an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Rushed Incantation|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|2} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Glib
entries: You can cast {@spell Glibness|XPHB} without a Verbal component. You can also cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. For the spell's duration, you can take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Star-Spangled Banner
entries: {@i Represent the Greatest Democracy in the Multiverse}

Captains that wave the Star-Spangled Banner represent the ideals of Justice, Freedom, and Democracy wherever they travel. These values reflect the promise of a mythical land in which all people are prosperous and equal, which may or may not exist somewhere in the multiverse. With a unique shield-fighting technique and a penchant for diving headlong into danger, such Captains are either reckless idealogues or selfless heroes, depending on the situation.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn. You can't use Blitz and use this feature on the same turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Freedom of Movement
entries: You can cast the spell {@spell Freedom of Movement|XPHB} on yourself and your Cohort without a spell slot.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Wings of Liberty
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} action, you can transform into an embodiment of freedom: a red, white, and blue spirit resembling a bald eagle carrying an enormous sword or gun. You gain the following benefits for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend three Battle Dice (no action required) to restore your use of it.

entries.name: Deft Maneuver
entries: You gain a special additional {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} that you can take once on each of your turns. You can take this special {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} only to use a maneuver.

entries.name: Flight
entries: You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet, and can hover.

entries.name: Liberty or Death
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can expend one Battle Die to drop to a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the number rolled on the die plus your Charisma modifier.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Steel Magic
entries: {@i Cut Down Foes with the Soulsword}

Secret covens throughout the Material Plane practice their magic by drawing spells into their blades. Maniacally cackling and whirling their way across the battlefield, these Witches weave their curses into a bloody tapestry whenever they bring their steel to bear.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.
In addition, you can cast one of your cantrips (including your Hexes) that has a casting time of an action in place of one of those attacks.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Insidious Smite
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with your Soulsteel weapon, you can expend a level 5 or lower spell slot to deal extra damage equal to {@dice 1d8} per level of the spell slot. This damage is your choice of Force, Necrotic, or Radiant.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Hexplate
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage dealt by an enemy that is the sole target of your Hex.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Stoneheart Defender
entries: {@i Become an Unmovable Obstacle}

Your call was the steadfast rumble of mountains, a pull which dwarves and gnomes have felt for generations. As a Stoneheart Defender, you protect the stones from those who would despoil them, from within and without. You might protect old dwarven walls, patrol high mountain lookouts, or stand in defense of remote villages. You are unmovable wherever you plant your feet: a mountain in mortal form.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Roots of Rock
entries: Your attunement to the mountains grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Immovable
entries: You can't be pushed, pulled, or teleported against your will.

entries.name: Prone Immunity
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition unless you choose to have it or have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Legendary Interruption
entries: When an enemy you can see takes a Legendary Action to make an attack, you can use {@classFeature Interrupt|Warden|ValdaSpire24|5} to prevent that attack.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Stoneforged Champion
entries: You can encase yourself in rock to become a living mountain. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain the benefits below for 1 minute or until you choose to end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Earthshatter Stomp
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can use your {@subclassFeature Earthshatter|Warden|ValdaSpire24|Stoneheart Defender|ValdaSpire24|3} without replacing one of your attacks.

entries.name: Giant Strength
entries: Your Strength increases by 4, to a maximum of 25.

entries.name: Immortal Resolve
entries: While you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Storm Sentinel
entries: {@i Become Imbued with a Roaring Storm}

Your call sounded like furious storm clouds and the flash of lightning. As a Storm Sentinel, you protect wayward sailors and coastal villages from the wrath of the tempests and the arrival of pirates and other raiders. From your fingertips, you deliver the awe of lightning and the roar of thunder, and with practice, you can fly among the squalls and rain thunderbolts from above.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Storm Wings
entries: At the start of each of your turns, you can gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} until the end of the current turn (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Lightning Step
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can teleport inside a bolt of lightning to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet. Immediately before you teleport, each creature within 5 feet of the space you appear in makes a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}), taking {@damage 4d8} Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Interrupt|Warden|ValdaSpire24|5} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Stormlord
entries: You can imbue yourself with the storm's fury. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain the benefits below for 1 minute or until you choose to end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Call Lightning
entries: As a part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you take to use this feature, you cast {@spell Call Lightning|XPHB} without a spell slot. When you cast the spell in this way, its duration is 1 minute. On subsequent turns, you can replace one of your attacks with calling down lightning again.

entries.name: Fly Speed
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 60 feet.

entries.name: Improved Thunderblast
entries: The damage of your Thunderblast increases to {@dice 3d8}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Grey Watchman
entries: {@i Perform Lethal Maneuvers in Combat}

Ever-vigilant and unceasing in your duties, you are a watcher of the realms of Humanoids, called to keep guard over a fortress or wall. As a Grey Watchman, trained in the arts of combat, you have honed your skills to a razor's edge to repel any invaders that might challenge your land. You needn't keep watch over the same castle your entire life, but, wherever you travel, you are dedicated to keeping your land safe from invading armies, marauding monsters, and other external threats.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Unyielding Surge
entries: When you become {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you can regain an expended Battle Die (no action required).
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} or finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Hold the Line
entries: When you use the Grasp option of your Guardian Tactics, while in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}, you and your allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Unbreakable Sentinel
entries: You can become a paragon of battle. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain the benefits below for 1 minute or until you choose to end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Martial Recovery
entries: At the start of each of your turns, you regain one expended Battle Die.

entries.name: Deadly Strike
entries: When you hit with a maneuver, add an extra Battle Die to the damage roll without expending it.

entries.name: Deft Maneuver
entries: You gain a special additional {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} that you can take once on each of your turns. You can take this special {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} only to use a maneuver.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Tea Magic
entries: {@i Glimpse and Shape the Future Through Tea Leaves}

Witches that practice Tea Magic learn to brew magically delicious and restorative tea, as well as to glimpse the future in their tea leaves. They are among the calmest and friendliest of Witches, at worst cranky (if forced to drink their tea in a hurry) or twitchy (after too much tea).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Shapes and Omens
entries: You can see deeper glimpses into the future through your tea leaves. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can examine the shape of your tea leaves. The GM tells you a shape that hints at future events. For example, if you see a tower in your tea leaves, you might encounter a wizard on the following day. If you see a serpent, you might encounter a lair or a monster. When you encounter an event hinted at by your tea leaves, you gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Herbal Remedy
entries: When a creature drinks your tea as a part of your Tea Ceremony, it can gain one of the following benefits of its choice. Once it gains a benefit from this feature, it can't do so again until it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Invigoration
entries: The creature gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Witch level.

entries.name: Purification
entries: The creature has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and also has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws it makes to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on itself. This benefit lasts until the creature finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Restoration
entries: The creature gains the benefits of either the {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB} or the {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} spell.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: As Foretold
entries: You regain all expended uses of your Tasseography feature when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Technicolor Magic
entries: {@i Make Friends and Sing Songs}

Technicolor Witches draw their magic from the power of friendship. They have a penchant for collecting adorable animals of all shapes and sizes, which they will never endanger, no matter how dire the situation. Above all, these Witches are defined by their relentless positivity, which empowers their arcana and spurs on their {@variantrule Ally|XPHB|Allies}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Friendship Bracelet
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can weave a small magical bracelet of string, beads, or some other inexpensive material. You can have a number of these bracelets up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). If you make another one, you must render an existing bracelet nonmagical. A creature wearing one of your bracelets gains the following benefits.

entries.name: Helping Hand
entries: You can take the {@action Help|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to assist a creature wearing one of your bracelets. Once you do so, you can't use this benefit to assist that creature again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sense Location
entries: You can always determine the location of a creature wearing one of your bracelets, as long as you and it are on the same plane of existence.

entries.name: Targetable
entries: You can target a creature wearing one of your bracelets with spells and effects, even if you can't see it, as long as the target is within range.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Positivity
entries: You can leverage your bonds of friendship for protection. When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain a bonus to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equal to the number of friendly creatures within 5 feet of you (to a maximum of +10), potentially causing the attack to miss you instead.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Redemption Arc
entries: You can redeem your foes instead of slaying them. When an enemy you can see is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to protect the creature from further harm. Instead of dropping to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the creature drops to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} and has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition. The condition ends early for it if it regains any {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. When the creature awakens, any magical effect causing it to be {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, cursed, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, or possessed ends. Furthermore, the creature becomes {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you and your {@variantrule Ally|XPHB|Allies}.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Thunderlords' Guild
entries: {@i Charge Your Weapons with Electricity}

From the earliest days of life, storms (and particularly lightning) have struck the creatures caught in them with awe and terror. The Thunderlords' Guild, by contrast, draws wild inspiration from the majesty of nature, and seeks to, quite literally, capture lightning in a bottle.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Electric Armory
entries: When you create or modify a Masterwork Weapon, you can add the {@itemMastery Jolt|ValdaSpire24} property to any weapon, even one that doesn't deal Lightning damage. You gain the following benefit with any weapon that has the {@itemMastery Jolt|ValdaSpire24} property.

entries.name: Arcing Jolt
entries: Once per turn when you use the {@itemMastery Jolt|ValdaSpire24} property, you can expend one Charge Point to cause an arc of electricity to leap to a creature that you can see within 5 feet of the target. This creature is affected by the {@itemMastery Jolt|ValdaSpire24} property and makes a Dexterity saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, a creature takes Lightning damage equal to the damage dealt to the initial target, or half as much damage on a successful save.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Static Charge
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can store an electric charge in a suit of Masterwork armor you are wearing until the end of your next turn. If a creature hits you with a melee attack while your armor is charged, it takes {@damage 3d6} Lightning damage and the armor is no longer charged.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Ball Lightning
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 3 Charge Points to create a 1-foot diameter ball of electrified plasma in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. The ball lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature again or dismiss it (no action required).

The ball emanates an electric field in a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. When a creature enters the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} for the first time on a turn or begins its turn there, you can choose for metallic weapons it is carrying to gain an electric charge until the end of the creature's turn. Whenever a creature deals damage with a charged weapon, it deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Lightning damage.
At the start of each of your turns, the ball moves up to 15 feet in a direction you choose.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Time Operative
entries: {@i Manipulate Time to Solve Mysteries}

Time Operatives are agents from the future bestowed with a series of cryptic goals and a well of chronomantic magic. Some operatives hail from far-off utopias or crumbling apocalypses, while others simply receive a message across space and time and dedicate themselves to its mission. To prevent paradoxes, these Time Operatives receive only the barest clues pertaining to their mission. They know only the gravity of the situation, and that it is inherent upon them to change the course of history.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Rewind
entries: When you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} and fail, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to rewind time to the moment before the attempt. Reroll the {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} and you must use the new roll.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Echo of Yesterday
entries: You can take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast your senses up to 24 hours back in time at your current location. You can see and hear this location as if you were there, but the past appears dreamlike and shadowy. While perceiving the past, you can look in any direction, but you can't move or speak. This glimpse into the past lasts for 10 minutes, but it ends early if you dismiss it (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Steal Time
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or reduce an enemy to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you regain a use of your {@subclassFeature Borrowed Time|Investigator|ValdaSpire24|Time Operative|ValdaSpire24|3}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Tower Banner
entries: {@i Fortify Yourself and Your Allies}

The fortified defenses of Captains who fly the Tower Banner are legendary. Their tactics emphasize fortification and survival, as well-protected soldiers cannot only win battles, but entire wars. Thinking long term is key to any defensive strategy, as Captains of the Tower know the answer is never how they shall counterattack, but when.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Armored Redirection
entries: When a creature you can see hits an ally within 5 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force the attack to target you instead. If the attack roll equals or exceeds your AC, the attack hits you instead; otherwise, it misses.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend one Battle Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mettle
entries: Your determination allows you to shrug off effects that would otherwise harm you. When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. Your Cohort also gains the benefits of this feature.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Iron Retribution
entries: Whenever a creature within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack roll, you can strike them with a {@item Shield|XPHB} if you're carrying one (no action required), dealing {@damage 3d6} Bludgeoning damage to the attacker.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Tower Banner

entries: {@color {@style Cross-Compatible Subclass: This subclass originates from the {@color {@class Captain|ValdaSpire24}|3B7DAF} class|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style Note that cross-compatible subclasses might be stronger or weaker than other subclasses.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style The GM decides if a subclass should be cross-compatible in your campaign.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}

entries: {@b Level 10: Mettle.} You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Toymaker
entries: {@i Trap Souls Within Handmade Toys}

Toymaking is not unlike Necromancy. Painting details in miniature, carving faces, stitching clothing, and stringing up limbs require a meticulousness and obsession also well-suited to animating the dead. Necromancers, after all, devise their own playthings and meticulously fashion them, albeit using more gruesome materials. It should come at no surprise, therefore, that Necromancy enjoys a strong tradition of toymaking. Practiced necromantic Toymakers can animate their dolls as slaymates, adorable but lethal minions that strike in overwhelming numbers.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Soul Doll
entries: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when a creature you can see within 60 feet of you dies, you can capture the creature's soul and trap it within a Soul Doll. The creature controls the body of the doll using the statistics of a {@creature Slaymate|ValdaSpire24}, but it can't attack and retains its alignment, personality, languages, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores.

You don't control the Soul Doll and it doesn't count as one of your thralls. It is under no compulsion to cooperate with you, especially if you are antagonistic toward it or it recognizes you as an enemy.

While the creature's soul is trapped in a Soul Doll, it can't return to life. The soul leaves the doll when the Soul Doll is reduced to {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or when you release it as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action. You can have up to five Soul Dolls at one time. If you attempt to create a new Soul Doll, you can release another doll as a part of the {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} used to create the new doll.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Miniature Minions
entries: When you perform your {@classFeature Thralls|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|2|ValdaSpire24|Animate Thralls} ritual, you can choose for any thrall you create to be Tiny and have a toylike appearance of your choice. A Tiny thrall has a +3 bonus to AC.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Clockwork Lich [Lichdom]
entries: You have reached the pinnacle of Necromancy and transformed yourself into a lich. As part of the Rite, you transfer your soul into a body of ticking clockwork, a stuttering but immortal form. You gain the following benefits in addition to those of your {@classFeature Lichdom|Necromancer|ValdaSpire24|20} feature.

entries.name: Clockwork Body
entries: Your soul is bound to a Construct body with your statistics. Your type is Construct, instead of Undead.

entries.name: Clockwork Immunities
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, and {@condition Stunned|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Spell Immunities
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to three spells of your choice, which you select when you build the clockwork body.

entries.name: Backup Body
entries: You can spend 10 days and materials worth 1,000+ GP to build an additional clockwork body to act as a safeguard against death. Whenever you die, your soul transfers to another clockwork body of your choice that you have built. If you have no clockwork bodies available, you reform at your spirit jar in the body of a {@creature Slaymate|ValdaSpire24}, but you retain your alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, and the ability to build a clockwork body.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Trappers' Guild
entries: {@i Deploy a Minefield of Lethal Traps}

Craftsmen are no strangers to turrets, bombs, and clockwork mechanisms, but members of the Trappers' Guild raise this to a level of artistry. Given enough time and resources, a trapsmith can veritably blanket a room in dangerous implements, setting the stage to slay an intruder in a half-dozen unique ways. While the traps do the dirty work, the trapsmith is free to lounge about some distance away, enjoying a cold beverage and dreaming up new, dangerous designs.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Booby Trap
entries: You can conceal one of your traps over the course of a minute. A creature that takes a {@action Search|XPHB} or {@action Study|XPHB} action can detect a concealed trap with a successful Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check, respectively, against your Traps save DC. When a concealed trap activates, its damage dice are doubled.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Escape Plan
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when an enemy moves within 5 feet of you to move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} and deploy one trap in an unoccupied space at any point during the movement.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Masterwork Bonus. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} and all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Rapid Deployment
entries: You can take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to deploy up to three traps.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Troubadour
entries: {@i Inspire Your Allies Wherever You Travel}

A lyre, a flute, or perhaps a set of bagpipes at their side, a Troubadour sets out on the open road, playing music wherever they go. While Troubadours often travel in musical troupes, they might also ply their trade alone, wandering between taverns and street corners in search of an audience, coin, and perhaps fame.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fast Friends
entries: You can take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action to attempt to befriend a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself that can hear or see you. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus Charisma modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute or until it takes damage. While it has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition, it is friendly to you and your allies.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend one Battle Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Scathing Retort
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself misses you with an attack roll or forces you to make a saving throw and you succeed, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to insult the creature. The target takes Psychic damage equal to {@dice 1d10} plus half your Vagabond level (round down).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Marvelous Troupe
entries: When you use your Inspiring Tune maneuver, you can target a number of allies up to your Charisma modifier. Each chosen ally gains a Battle Die.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Troubadour

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Venomsmith
entries: {@i Cripple Your Foes with Deadly Poisons}

For every Alchemist that devotes their life to healing the sick, another hears a darker calling. Commonly called poisoners or Venomsmiths, these Alchemists are masters in the art of crafting deadly and debilitating poisons. Whether employed by an assassin's guild or performing assassinations themselves, a Venomsmith's presence is usually accompanied by untimely death.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Alchemical Assassin
entries: You have a specially-designed needle ring for poisoning others. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to apply a contact or injury poison to the ring. On subsequent turns, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to deal 1 Piercing damage to a creature within 5 feet of you, subjecting the creature to the poison on the ring. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} and {@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks made to conceal and use this ring.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mithridatism
entries: By administering small doses of poisons and toxins, you've learned how to diminish the effectiveness of poisons. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Poison Immunity
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage and the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Poison Resistance Extract
entries: A creature that drinks one of your potions also gains the benefits of a {@item Potion of Poison Resistance|XDMG}

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Toxic Recompense
entries: Whenever a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to unleash a spray of poisonous vapor. The attacker must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your Alchemist save DC or have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. While it has the condition, the creature takes {@damage 2d10} Poison damage at the start of each of its turns. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Verdant Protector
entries: {@i Protect Nature with Interlopers}

You heard the call of the wind through the trees and the loam beneath your feet. As a Verdant Protector, you are the champion of the green things in nature, defending them against those who would despoil the wilds. Plants sprout at your command to assist you, entangling and ensnaring foes for you to dispatch.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Nature's Emissary
entries: You can cast any of the following spells once without a spell slot: {@spell Goodberry|XPHB}, {@spell Plant Growth|XPHB}, {@spell Spike Growth|XPHB}, and {@spell Speak with Plants|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this feature (choose the ability when you cast the spell). Once you cast a spell using this feature, you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Verdant Resilience
entries: When you use your {@classFeature Survive|Warden|ValdaSpire24|9}, you and allies within 10 feet of yourself gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Warden level.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Oak Sentinel
entries: You can grow the gnarled oak of a treant. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain the benefits below for 1 minute or until you choose to end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Armor of Thorns
entries: You gain a +4 bonus to AC. Whenever you take damage from an enemy within 5 feet of you, the enemy takes {@damage 4d6} Piercing damage and the AC bonus decreases by 1, to a minimum of +0.

entries.name: Entangling Transformation
entries: When you use this feature, plants and vines sprout from the ground in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you. Each creature you choose in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. A {@condition Restrained|XPHB} creature can take an action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check against this benefit's save DC, ending the condition on itself on a success.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: White Magic
entries: {@i Heal and Mend a Broken World}

White Magic is fundamentally good and benevolent for all living things. Witches that adopt this craft, in spite of the hateful curse that infects them, often dedicate themselves to healing and caretaking.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Talisman of Protection
entries: You can craft a magical talisman that wards off harm. Creating a talisman takes 1 hour of work, which can be done during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can only have one of these talismans at a time; crafting a new talisman causes the previous one to become nonmagical. Any creature wearing the talisman adds a {@dice d4} to all saving throws it makes.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Benevolent Surge
entries: When you, your familiar, or an {@variantrule Ally|XPHB} you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cause that creature to regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 1d10} plus your Charisma modifier.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Witch's Gift
entries: Whenever you cast a spell or use a Witch feature that restores a creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, that creature gains a +3 bonus to its {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Wintercarvers' Guild
entries: {@i Sculpt Elegant Weapons from Solid Ice}

Many Craftsmen are accustomed to extreme cold, but only a few have learned the ephemeral art of ice-crafting. The Guild of Wintercarvers specializes in sculpting ice into majestic and dangerous forms and working with supercooled material that possesses strange, unconventional properties.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Frigid Armory
entries: Your {@subclassFeature Winter Core|Craftsman|ValdaSpire24|Wintercarvers|ValdaSpire24Extras|3} supercools your weapons, improving the following mastery properties when you use them.

entries.name: Numb
entries: The target can't take {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB|Bonus Actions} until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Sap
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its next {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, instead of only its next attack roll.

entries.name: Slow
entries: The target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 20 feet instead of 10.

entries.name: Topple
entries: The target automatically fails its saving throw.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Frostburn
entries: While you're holding your {@subclassFeature Winter Core|Craftsman|ValdaSpire24|Wintercarvers|ValdaSpire24Extras|3}, you can cast {@spell Fire Shield|XPHB} without a spell slot or Material components. You can only choose the chill shield option when you cast the spell using this feature. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for the spell.
Once you cast the spell using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sub-Zero
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon created with your {@subclassFeature Ice Sculpting|Craftsman|ValdaSpire24|Wintercarvers|ValdaSpire24Extras|3}, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to attempt to coat the target in ice. The creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn or until it takes any damage.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Masterwork Bonus. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} and all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Witchbane Hunter
entries: {@i Hunt Mages and Supernatural Foes}

Where there is magic, there is evil. Witches, warlocks, and hags lurk in the shadows, plying their myriad curses upon the innocent. But your ever-vigilant sword is ready for them, ready to defend the nonmagical folk from evil spellcasters the world-over. You slay vampires, hexers, devils, and fey with impunity, for anyone who might despoil the world with magic shall be hunted and put to the stake.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Otherworldly Eye
entries: Your well-trained eye can detect the slightest hint of magic, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Detect Latent Magic
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can sense if a spell was cast within 30 feet of yourself within the last 24 hours and what spell was cast.

entries.name: See Invisibility
entries: You see creatures and objects that have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. You can also see into the Ethereal Plane. Creatures and objects there appear ghostly.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Rebuke
entries: You can cast {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} without a spell slot. If the target fails its saving throw against this spell, it takes {@damage 4d8} Force damage. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell when you cast it with this feature (choose the ability when you cast the spell).

Once you use this feature to cast this spell, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Interrupt|Warden|ValdaSpire24|5} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Anti-Mage
entries: You can imbue yourself with an antimagic aura. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain the benefits below for 1 minute or until you choose to end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Antimagic Field
entries: As a part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you take to use this feature, you cast {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB} without a spell slot. When you cast it in this way, its duration is 1 minute and the 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originates from you. Additionally, you choose which creatures and objects are affected by the {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}.

entries.name: Branding Challenge
entries: When you hit an enemy targeted by the Challenge option of your {@classFeature Guardian Tactics|Warden|ValdaSpire24|2} with a weapon, the target takes an extra {@damage 2d8} Fire damage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Xenoalchemist
entries: {@i Harvest Monsters and Attach Grafts}

A small number of renegade Alchemists elect to experiment on themselves, modifying their anatomy or even outright attaching new body parts. These experimenters are often considered unethical and dangerous, even by other Alchemists, and those that practice them are branded Xenoalchemists for their efforts. As Xenoalchemists progress in their studies, they invariably stumble upon the dangerous practice of alchemical necromancy, which allows them to imbue life upon amalgamations of body parts.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Examine Specimen
entries: You can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a creature as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You learn the target's creature type and make a DC 15 Intelligence check using a skill from the Examine Specimen table, corresponding to the target's creature type. If you succeed, you learn one of the following pieces of information of your choice about the target: its AC, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, or whether it is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.

Whether you succeed or fail, you can't use this feature again to target that creature or another creature of its specific kind (such as humans or unicorns) until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.caption: Examine Specimen
rows: Aberrations, Constructs, Elementals, Fey, and Monstrosities

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Necromantic Organs
entries: You've augmented your body with reanimated organs that persist after your death. If you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but not killed outright, you can drop to a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Alchemist level.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: It's Alive!
entries: Your research into necromancy has culminated in golem stitched together from discarded body parts. This golem uses the {@creature Alchemy Golem|ValdaSpire24} stat block.

entries.name: Creating or Replacing the Golem
entries: You can make a golem using 3 Humanoid corpses in a process that requires 8 hours of work, which can be done during a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. If you already have a golem from this feature, the old one dies when the new one is completed.

entries.name: Golem in Combat
entries: The golem is under your control and is an ally to you and your allies. In combat, it takes its turn immediately before or after your turn each round (your choice). You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to mentally command the golem if it is within 500 feet of you. If you issue no commands, the golem takes the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action and moves only to avoid harm.

entries.name: Golem Grafts
entries: You can attach up to three {@filter monstrous grafts|items|type=monstrous graft} to the golem.

entries.name: Restoring the Golem
entries: If the golem has died within the last hour, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to touch it and expend 1 {@classFeature Reagents|Alchemist|ValdaSpire24|1||Reagent}. The golem returns to life with a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 1d10} plus your Intelligence modifier.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Yellow Sign
entries: {@i Enthrall Your Friends and Foes with Eldritch Madness}

The Yellow Sign is a twisting symbol of eldritch chaos, the signature of an otherworldly leviathan ready to consume all of reality. Captains bearing its distinctive mark upon their Shields and armor aren't commanders—they are cult leaders dedicated to incomprehensible alien masters. Their objectives are as secretive as they are disquieting, but undoubtedly demand indoctrination of more thralls to spread their master's sign and influence.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Pallid Aura
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to trace the Yellow Sign in the air and create a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of psychic energy centered on yourself for 1 minute or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. Once per turn, when a creature within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can roll {@dice 1d6} and subtract it from the roll (no action required).

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend one Battle Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Maniacal Influence
entries: Your eldritch master's influence grows, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Frenzied Ally
entries: When a creature has the Frenzied condition of your Frenzied Strike, it regards you and your Cohort as allies while it has the condition.

entries.name: Frenzied Blitz
entries: When you use your Blitz feature, you can direct a creature that has the Frenzied condition, even if that creature isn't an ally.

entries.name: Extended Frenzy
entries: Whenever a creature that has the Frenzied condition of your Frenzied Strike ends its turn, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Maneuver save DC. On a failed save, the Frenzied condition doesn't end for that creature. On a success, the condition ends for that creature.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Nightmarish Glow
entries: While the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of your Pallid Aura is active, you and your allies within the Emantion deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage when hitting an enemy with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Yellow Sign

entries: {@color {@style Cross-Compatible Subclass: This subclass originates from the {@color {@class Captain|ValdaSpire24}|3B7DAF} class|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style Note that cross-compatible subclasses might be stronger or weaker than other subclasses.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}
{@color {@style The GM decides if a subclass should be cross-compatible in your campaign.|small-caps; large; bold}|e40707}

entries: {@b Level 10: Frenzied Blitz.} Replace with "You can give a creature that has the Frenzied condition {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its attack rolls."
