subclassFeaturesFull.name: Acrobat
entries: {@i Strike with Gymnastic Speed and Momentum}

Acrobats vault, walk tightropes, and backflip over their foes to find new angles of approach. Such Dancers often perform with circuses or work for criminal organizations, and find endless applications for their skills in dungeon-diving. Moreover, an Acrobat can convert the momentum of their gymnastics into crushing force when a foe proves otherwise intractable.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Tumbling
entries: While your Agile Movement {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style} is active, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Fall Safely
entries: The first time you fall each turn, reduce any damage you take from the fall by an amount equal to five times your Dancer level.

entries.name: Ignore Difficult Terrain
entries: {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} doesn't cost you extra movement.

entries.name: Speed Increase
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Evasive Speed
entries: When you move 30 feet or more during your turn, you can take the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Deadly Momentum
entries: You can have up to three {@subclassFeature Momentum|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Acrobat|ValdaSpire24Extras|3} at a time and you don't lose {@subclassFeature Momentum|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Acrobat|ValdaSpire24Extras|3} at the end of your turn while your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} is active. When you hit a creature with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend up to three {@subclassFeature Momentum|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Acrobat|ValdaSpire24Extras|3} at once.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Cheerleader
entries: {@i Encourage Your Allies with Acrobatics and Cheer}

Pom-pom-wielding Cheerleaders are an essential component of siegeball games, which sell out stadiums wherever teams clash. Cheerleaders bound from the sidelines, energizing the crowd and their team with upbeat chants and daring acrobatic displays. Indeed, on some siegeball teams, the most impressive athleticism occurs on the sidelines with human pyramids.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Squad Warmup
entries: When you begin your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2}, choose a {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style} other than {@subclassFeature Inspiring Chant [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Cheerleader|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Inspiring Chant}. Each ally that can see or hear you within 10 feet of yourself gains the benefits of that {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style} until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Athletic Dexterity
entries: When you make a Strength or Constitution saving throw, you can make a Dexterity saving throw instead.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Spirited Start
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can give yourself and each ally that can see or hear you within 60 feet of yourself a special instance of {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} that vanishes after the first round of combat. A creature can have this instance of {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} and another instance at the same time, but can only use one {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} per roll.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Contortionist
entries: {@i Dance with Mesmerizing Flexibility}

Balancing on their shoulders and folding their body into perplexing configurations, Contortionists represent the very pinnacle of flexibility. Contortionists, with practice, can leverage their flexibility to evade attacks and respond from expected directions with the grace and lethality of a serpent.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Backbend
entries: You can enter the space of a Small or larger enemy and end your turn there. While in this creature's space, you have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} against attacks and effects that originate outside of your space, and the creature can't have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against you.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Twisting Redirection
entries: When a creature you can see misses you with a melee attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force the attack to target another creature other than the attacker within the attacker's reach. Use the existing attack roll against the new target's AC, dealing damage as normal on a hit.

You can take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum of once). You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Reactive
entries: While your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} is active, you have an additional {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, which you regain at the start of each of your turns. You can't take two {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} on the same turn. Additionally, once you take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, such as an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} or casting a Spell with a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} trigger, you can't take that {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Courtesan
entries: {@i Enthrall Others with Your Grace}

Dressed in finery, Courtesans are the very picture of cultured elegance. Rather than dancing like a jester for others' amusement, Courtesans leverage their unearthly grace to twist the affections of others. Most ingratiate themselves into high society, for a melodic tone and captivating glance is enough to enrapture most nobles.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sociable Start
entries: During the first round of combat, you can take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks you make using that action.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Beguiling Charm
entries: When you give a creature the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition, you can choose one of the following effects for the creature while it has the condition.

entries.name: Bad Influence
entries: The target subtracts your Dance Die from Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws it makes.

entries.name: Friend of My Friends
entries: The target subtracts your Dance Die from all its attack rolls.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Heartbreaker
entries: Whenever a creature succeeds or fails its saving throw against your {@subclassFeature Enthralling Movement [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Courtesan|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Enthralling Movement}, you can deal Psychic damage to the target equal to two rolls of your Dance Die.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Danseur Macabre
entries: {@i Raise the Dead with Your Necromantic Dance}

The "Danse Macabre" is a lament, a dirge from the recently deceased that causes the spirits of the dead to stir and join in. The spectacle is one of grim frivolity—a single living person among jovial skeletons that vanish upon the danse's final note.

Only a few Dancers called "Necrodancers" or "Danseurs Macabre" learn this morbid footwork. Usually, it calls for those with a morose disposition and a fascination with death, the very same attributes that make for a fine necromancer.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dance with the Dead
entries: You can cast {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} without a spell slot. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell. When you cast the spell in this way, the corpse gains enough of a semblance of life to move and dance with you for the duration of the spell, if it is able. The corpse will generally move where you ask it to, but can't take actions or deal damage. You can also take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to change the target of the spell to a different corpse within range. You can ask a total of five questions, no matter how many corpses you target.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Danse Fatale
entries: Your {@subclassFeature Danse Macabre [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Danseur Macabre|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Danse Macabre} {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style} improves in the following ways.

entries.name: Avoidance
entries: If one of your {@creature Skeleton Spirit|ValdaSpire24Extras|Skeleton Spirits} is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save and half damage if it fails. It can't use this trait if it has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Improved Spectral Bolt
entries: The damage of your {@creature Skeleton Spirit|ValdaSpire24Extras|Skeleton Spirits'} Spectral Bolt becomes {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Grim Troupe
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet dies while your {@subclassFeature Danse Macabre [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Danseur Macabre|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Danse Macabre} {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style} is active, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cast {@spell Create Undead|XPHB} targeting that creature without expending a spell slot or components. The {@creature Ghoul|XMM} is under your control and uses the following rules.

entries.name: Charismatic Attacks
entries: The ghoul's attack bonus equals your Charisma modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Choreographed Command
entries: When you use the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} of your {@subclassFeature Danse Macabre [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Danseur Macabre|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Danse Macabre} {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style}, you can command the ghouls animated by {@spell Create Undead|XPHB} as a part of the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Rhythmic Unlife
entries: When your {@subclassFeature Danse Macabre [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Danseur Macabre|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Danse Macabre} {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style} is no longer active, the ghoul dies.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dramaturge
entries: {@i Perform with Arcane Magic}

Wearing extravagant costumes or archetypal masks of comedy and tragedy, Dramaturges channel the power of the stage into performative magic. Their spells manipulate minds and create illusions to bolster their performances, transforming the world around them into a great play in which they are the star.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Strike
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with a casting of one of your Bard cantrips that has a casting time of an action.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Comedy and Tragedy
entries: You have a pair of enchanted theater masks. You can put on either your Comedy Mask or your Tragedy Mask when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, granting you the following benefits until you remove the mask or replace it with the other one.

entries.name: Comedy Mask
entries: Whenever an ally you can see or hear within 60 feet of yourself regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to regain the same number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or gain the same number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, respectively.

entries.name: Tragedy Mask
entries: When an ally you can see or hear within 60 feet of yourself takes damage that causes it to become {@status Bloodied|XPHB} or drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the damage type the ally took until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} or use this benefit again.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Encore
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn while your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} is active, you can cast a spell that has a casting time of an action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fencer
entries: {@i Parry and Thrust with Lethal Poise}

Postured, graceful, and utterly deadly, Fencers favor one-handed parries and thrusts to whirling Daggers and Darts. Their repertoire of movements constitute a dance of footwork and bladework that can overcome most foes with a few precise movements and pinpoint strikes.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fencing Maneuvers
entries: While your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} is active, you can perform the following maneuvers.

entries.name: Disarm
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can attempt to disarm a creature you can see within 5 feet of you. The target makes a Strength saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, it drops one item of your choice that it's holding. The object lands in a space you choose within 10 feet of the target.

entries.name: En Garde
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can goad an enemy that can see or hear you into attacking you. Until the start of your next turn, the enemy has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against creatures other than you while it is within 5 feet of you. This effect ends early if your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} ends.

entries.name: Lunge
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can increase your reach by 5 feet with weapons that lack the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} or {@itemProperty V|XPHB|Versatile} properties until the start of your next turn. This effect ends early if your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} ends.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Parry and Riposte
entries: When you use your Graceful Dodge, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to add another roll of your Dance Die to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} for this attack.

Starting at Dancer level 11, if you use this feature and the triggering attack misses you, you can use your {@classFeature Graceful Retaliation|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|11} as a part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

You can take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum of once). You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Superior Flourish
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} or reduce an enemy to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} on your turn, you regain up to 15 feet of expended movement and can make one additional attack on your turn. You can make up to three such additional attacks on a single turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fey Ballerina
entries: {@i Dance With Unearthly Grace and Perfection}

Perhaps the most majestic style of dance originates in the Feywild, where unending waltzes and chaotic ballets intermingle with raw threads of magic. Mortal Fey Ballerinas have proven their merits at dance to a Fey and been bequeathed with a boon: a magical pair of slippers, a charm, or another trinket that further imbues their Dance with supernatural grace.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Misty Waltz
entries: You can cast {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once). Charisma is your spellcasting modifier for this spell. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Sublime Start
entries: During the first round of combat, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled and you automatically succeed on saving throws.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Swan Song
entries: While you're {@status Bloodied|XPHB} and your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} is active, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to begin a Swan Song. You regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} up to half your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the first {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} you make each turn until your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} ends.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fire Dancer
entries: {@i Perform Dazzling Pyrotechnic Displays}

Fire dancing features dazzling displays of torch juggling and spinning, fire eating, and fire breathing. Though these spark-throwing performances are a wonder to behold, they can easily become hazardous, unintentionally sparking a blaze or intentionally catching a foe alight.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fire Breather
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can breathe flames in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Each creature in the {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} makes a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, a creature takes Fire damage equal to three rolls of your Dance Die plus your Dancer level. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Blinding Flare
entries: Once on each of your turns while your {@subclassFeature Pyrotechnics [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Fire Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Pyrotechnics} {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style} is active, when you deal damage to a creature and roll the highest number on a damage die, that target makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Inferno Breath
entries: Your {@subclassFeature Fire Breather|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Fire Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|6} feature improves in the following ways.

entries.name: Ignore Resistance
entries: The damage you deal with this feature ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage.

entries.name: Improved Cone
entries: You can breathe flames in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}.

entries.name: Burning
entries: Each creature that fails its saving throw starts {@hazard Burning|XPHB}. The creature takes Fire damage at the start of each of its turns equal to one roll of your Dance Die. As an action, a creature can extinguish fire on itself by giving itself the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and rolling on the ground. The fire also goes out if it is doused, submerged, or suffocated.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Harlequin
entries: {@i Mock Your Foes with Acrobatic Flair}

Consummate comedians, jugglers, and acrobats, Harlequins perform alongside jesters in royal courts and local taverns alike. Their usual performances feature a mix of barbed jokes at the attendees and daring knife stunts performed with an acrobatic flair. Though they draw plenty of ire from their heckling routine, their nastiest jokes can reliably earn a laugh from the crowd and take down the target a peg or two.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Backflip
entries: When you roll a Dance Die, you can flip the die over and use the number on the bottom. Note that for a balanced die, the top and bottom numbers add up to one more than the die's largest number. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until the start of your next turn.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum of once). You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Vexing Jest
entries: Your {@subclassFeature Jest [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Harlequin|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Jest} {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style} improves in the following ways.

entries.name: Losing Streak
entries: Whenever the target of your {@subclassFeature Jest [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Harlequin|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Jest} misses with an attack roll, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Mocking Misfortune
entries: Until the start of your next turn, whenever the target of your {@subclassFeature Jest [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Harlequin|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Jest} rolls a 20 on the {@dice d20} of a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, the roll instead becomes a 1.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Deft Fling
entries: Once on each of your turns when you miss a target with an attack roll, you can make one ranged attack with a weapon you are Juggling against the same target.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Marionettist
entries: {@i Manipulate Others Like Puppets}

Marionettists are master manipulators with magical strings. Instead of dancing themselves, they prefer to control a puppet or ensnare other creatures with their strings and compel them to dance to a new rhythm.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Manipulator
entries: Your skill in manipulating others grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Stringed Suggestion
entries: You can cast {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} without a spell slot. Charisma is your spellcasting modifier for this spell. Once you cast the spell in this way, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a use of your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} (no action required).

entries.name: Tangle of Lies
entries: Whenever you make a Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check, add your Dance Die to the roll if you don't add it already.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Heartstrings
entries: When a creature fails its saving throw against your {@subclassFeature Puppet Strings [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Marionettist|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Puppet Strings}, it has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition and {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against your allies until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Master of Puppets
entries: When a Beast or Humanoid fails its saving throw against your {@subclassFeature Puppet Strings [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Marionettist|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Puppet Strings}, you can cast {@spell Dominate Beast|XPHB} or {@spell Dominate Person|XPHB} targeting the creature, respectively, without a spell slot. The target automatically fails its saving throw against the spell. Charisma is your spellcasting modifier for this feature's spells.

The spell ends early if your {@subclassFeature Puppet Strings [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Marionettist|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Puppet Strings} is no longer active. Additionally, you can't use the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} of your {@subclassFeature Puppet Strings [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Marionettist|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Puppet Strings} for the spell's duration.

When you reach Dancer level 15, you can use this feature to cast {@spell Dominate Monster|XPHB} when any creature fails its saving throw against {@subclassFeature Puppet Strings [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Marionettist|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Puppet Strings}.

Once you use this feature to cast a spell, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of this feature to cast {@spell Dominate Beast|XPHB} or {@spell Dominate Person|XPHB} by expending two uses of your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mime
entries: {@i Perform a Silent Dance with Invisible Props}

Silent and monochromatic performers, Mimes act out a world of invisible objects and wordless gags. Those that master this artform find that their pantomimes can drive sound from the room, imbue invisible props with solidity, and even raise invisible walls of force around their foes.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Unseen Impact
entries: Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with a melee attack while your {@subclassFeature Pantomime [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Mime|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Pantomime} {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style} is active, you can give the target the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition or push it up to 10 feet away from you.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Invisible Wall
entries: You can cast {@spell Wall of Force|XPHB} without expending a spell slot or spell components. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending two uses of your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2} (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mystical Maul
entries: While your {@subclassFeature Pantomime [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Mime|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Pantomime} {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style} is active, whenever you roll damage with a Melee weapon that deals {@damage 1d4} or {@damage 1d6} damage, you can deal {@damage 2d6} Force damage instead of its normal damage type.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Shadow Dancer
entries: {@i Dance Alongside a Shadowy Duplicate}

Wielding long-forgotten magic, Shadow Dancers animate their shadows to act as dance partners. This Shadowdance is a waltz performed in perfect synchronicity that can fold the darkness around them, obscuring the room or even causing the Dancer to vanish from view.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Shrouded Start
entries: On the first round of combat, you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. The condition ends early immediately after you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Umbral Escape
entries: When the shadow duplicate of your {@subclassFeature Shadowdance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Shadow Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|3} is destroyed, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is entirely in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Vengeful Shadow
entries: When a creature destroys the shadow duplicate of your Shadowdance, lingering shadowstuff covers the creature until the end of your next turn. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attacks against a creature covered in shadowstuff, and whenever you hit such a creature with an attack, you deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage to it.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Steelsinger
entries: {@i Deflect Attacks with Your Armored Dance}

The "Steel Song" is a treatise on combat, detailing the stances and techniques of armed battle. Though the original manual has long since been lost to time, its practitioners have passed down the discipline down through the generations to particularly lightfooted warriors.
Steelsingers demonstrate acrobatic flourishes and mobility, even while laden with relatively bulky weapons and armor, dancing across the battlefield in a lethal cadence.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Armored Redirection
entries: When a creature you can see hits an ally within 5 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force the attack to target you instead. If the attack roll equals or exceeds your AC, the attack hits you instead; otherwise, it misses.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} or begin your {@classFeature Dance|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Improved Armored Deflection
entries: Your {@subclassFeature Deflection [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Steelsinger|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Armored Deflection} {@classFeature Dance Styles|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|2||Dance Style} is improved in the following ways.

entries.name: Improved Deflection
entries: You can treat any roll of 1-3 on a Dance Die for your {@subclassFeature Deflection [Dance Style]|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Steelsinger|ValdaSpire24Extras|3||Deflection} die as a 4.

entries.name: Prismatic Deflection
entries: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, and Thunder damage you take is also reduced. If an attack deals one of these damage types and Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, each damage type is reduced separately.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Retaliatory Slam
entries: You can use your {@subclassFeature Armored Redirection|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|Steelsinger|ValdaSpire24Extras|6} and {@classFeature Graceful Retaliation|Dancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|11} as a part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. When you do so, the target takes extra Bludgeoning damage equal to two rolls of your Dance Die on a hit.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Chronomancer
entries: {@i Manipulate the Flow of Time}

Chronomancy focuses on harnessing and manipulating the energies of flowing time. It is a perilous tradition, as a miscast spell can tear novices to pieces, spread them thinly across millennia, or even drop them wholesale into a new era. When properly cast, however, your magic lets you walk the generations with ease, ending most conflicts before they even begin.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Retroactive Spell
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the roll, you can manipulate history to cast a spell before combat began. Cast a level 1-3 spell targeting yourself, expending a spell slot as normal (no action required). The spell must have a {@filter casting time|spells|level=1;2;3|class=wizard|damage type=!acid;!bludgeoning;!cold;!fire;!force;!lightning;!necrotic;!piercing;!poison;!psychic;!radiant;!slashing;!thunder|cast time=action;bonus|Duration=[&1 Round;&Special]} of an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, a duration other than Instantaneous, and must not deal damage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Lag Spell
entries: When you cast a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can choose to delay its effect. Choose the spell's targets and whether you delay its effect for one, two, or three rounds, and expend the spell slot. Any effects on the spell's targets, including saving throws, are resolved when the spell triggers at the start of your turn after the chosen number of rounds. You can cast a spell with a spell slot on the same turn that the delayed spell triggers.

You don't maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on a delayed spell that requires {@status Concentration|XPHB} until it takes effect. If any conditions change between casting and when the spell takes effect that would make the spell impossible—such as the target leaving the spell's maximum range—the spell dissipates with no effect.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Time Loop
entries: When a creature you can see ends its turn, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to freeze time for everyone but that creature while it takes an extra turn. No time passes for other creatures, including yourself if the target is another creature.
The target's extra turn ends early if one of the actions it takes, or any effects that it creates, affects a creature other than itself or an object being worn or carried by someone other than it.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Familiar Master
entries: {@i Command an Evolved Familiar}

Learning the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell is a rite of passage among fledgling Wizards, as the spell offers a useful, if limited, magical servant. As a Familiar Master or "evolutionist," your studies focus on unlocking the full potential of the humble {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell in the hopes of evolving your familiar into new and more powerful forms.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Servitor's Agility
entries: While you have a familiar, you have one of the following benefits based on your familiar's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. If a familiar has more than one special {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, you choose the benefit in such cases.

entries.name: Burrow Speed
entries: {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} doesn't cost you extra movement.

entries.name: Climb Speed
entries: You have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Fly Speed
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} until the end of the current turn.

entries.name: Swim Speed
entries: You can breathe underwater and have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: No Special Speed
entries: {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Bolster Familiar
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to give your familiar a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Wizard level. When you do, you can also change the familiar's creature type and the form it takes from the list provided in the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Planar Familiar
entries: Your familiar gains a benefit based on its creature type.

entries.name: Celestial
entries: When a creature your familiar can see within 60 feet of itself fails a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, the familiar can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to let the creature reroll the test with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. The creature must use the new roll.

entries.name: Fey
entries: Your familiar can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. {@action Attack|XPHB} rolls against the familiar have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Fiend
entries: When your familiar takes the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, it can replace an attack with a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of hellfire. Each creature within the area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking {@damage 4d6} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Fumaturge
entries: {@i Control the Magic of Smoke and Fog}

Many Wizard apprentices take up pipe smoking, but only a few delve into the connected subschool of Fumaturgy, the magic of smoke and vapor. As a Fumaturge, you can shape any cloud puff of pipe smoke to a {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB} spell as you please, creating animate animals of smoke or mazes of vapor so thick they hinder movement.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Gaseous Escape
entries: Add {@spell Gaseous Form|XPHB} to your spellbook for free. When you take Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can cast the spell on yourself as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} without a spell slot. The spell's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} applies to the triggering damage.
Once you cast the spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can cast the spell in this way again by expending a level 3+ spell slot.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Greater Fogcrafting
entries: Your mastery over Fumaturgy grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Cloud Immunity
entries: You automatically succeed on saving throws you make against {@spell Cloudkill|XPHB}, {@spell Incendiary Cloud|XPHB}, and {@spell Stinking Cloud|XPHB}, and you take no damage from them.

entries.name: Fog Step
entries: While entirely within the area of your {@spell Cloudkill|XPHB}, {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB}, {@spell Incendiary Cloud|XPHB}, or {@spell Stinking Cloud|XPHB}, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space that is also within the area.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Smoke Mage
entries: Whenever you start casting {@spell Gaseous Form|XPHB}, including with your {@subclassFeature Gaseous Escape|Wizard|XPHB|Fumaturge|ValdaSpire24Extras|6}, you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. If you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting, your {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} is equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and you can cast spells while shape-shifted.

Once you use this feature to modify the casting of the spell, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Gastronomer
entries: {@i Become a Wizard of Gourmet Food}

Gastronomy, the oft-satirized subschool of food-related magic, is rarely taught to wizardly apprentices, for even masters of Transmutation can be terrible at cuisine. However, Gastronomy is a nourishing magic which spans all cultures, and is more of an art than an arcane tradition. Your studies have not only taught you the fundamentals of magical cooking, but also how to cook monsters into delicious, nutritious meals.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Condiments
entries: When you make a {@subclassFeature Monster Meal|Wizard|XPHB|Gastronomer|ValdaSpire24Extras|3}, you can cast {@spell Comprehend Languages|XPHB}, {@spell Darkvision|XPHB}, {@spell Longstrider|XPHB}, {@spell Nondetection|XPHB}, {@spell See Invisibility|XPHB}, or {@spell Water Breathing|XPHB} to create a magical condiment. You must have the spell prepared and expend a spell slot as normal. Each creature that partakes in the {@subclassFeature Monster Meal|Wizard|XPHB|Gastronomer|ValdaSpire24Extras|3} gains the benefit of the spell until it finishes a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Heroic Snacks
entries: You can cast {@spell Heroes' Feast|XPHB} without a spell slot or Material components. When you cast the spell using this feature, the spell is modified so that its casting time is an action and it creates a number of Heroic Snacks equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one). A creature can eat a Heroic Snack as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to gain the benefits of the {@spell Heroes' Feast|XPHB} spell, which last for 1 hour.
Once you use this feature to cast {@spell Heroes' Feast|XPHB}, you can't use it again to do so until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Five-Star Condiments
entries: When you make a {@subclassFeature Monster Meal|Wizard|XPHB|Gastronomer|ValdaSpire24Extras|3}, you can cast {@spell Blur|XPHB}, {@spell Enlarge/Reduce|XPHB}, {@spell Fly|XPHB}, {@spell Invisibility|XPHB}, or {@spell Protection from Energy|XPHB} to create a superior magical condiment. You must have the spell prepared and expend a spell slot as normal. Each creature that partakes in the {@subclassFeature Monster Meal|Wizard|XPHB|Gastronomer|ValdaSpire24Extras|3} gains the benefit of the spell until it finishes a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on the spell for each affected creature, and the spell ends for all creatures if you lose {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Magic Missile Mage
entries: {@i Cast Magic Missile Better Than Anyone}

{@spell Magic Missile|XPHB} is a staple wizard spell, beloved for its versatility and unerring accuracy. As a Missile Mage, however, your fondness for the spell borders on obsession. Your studies focus entirely on this spell, exploring every aspect of its casting, resulting in new augmentations and greater power.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Versatile Missiles
entries: You can accurately guide your {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB} darts to strike a target wherever you choose. When you cast {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, you can add one of the following Versatile Missile effects to a target struck by the darts. Each effect has a cost, which is the number of darts you must forgo to add the effect to the target. You can add different effects to different targets, paying the cost for each effect separately.

entries.name: Trip Missile (Cost: 1 Dart)
entries: The target must succeed on Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Blinding Missile (Cost: 3 Darts)
entries: The target must succeed on Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Stunning Missile (Cost: 5 Darts)
entries: The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Shield of Missiles
entries: When you cast {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, you can direct the darts in a tight orbit around yourself, creating a protective 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you, which lasts for up to 1 minute.

You gain a bonus to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equal to the number of darts orbiting you (maximum bonus of +5). Whenever a creature within 120 feet misses you with an attack roll, one dart strikes the attacker, dealing damage as normal and decreasing the number of darts orbiting you by one.

Whenever the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} enters the space of a creature you can see and whenever a creature you can see enters the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} or ends its turn there, you can strike the target with any number of darts orbiting you, dealing damage as normal and decreasing the number of darts orbiting you. You can damage a creature with the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} only once per turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Giga-Missile
entries: When you cast {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, you can enhance the damage of the spell. You deal extra Force damage with each dart equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mystic Strategist
entries: {@i Amplify Your Spells with Magical Maneuvers}

Rather than specializing in a school of magic, Mystic Strategists study tactics and game theory to outfox their foes. You have learned to augment your spellcasting with a suite of magical maneuvers, allowing you to bolster your allies and enhance your magic on the fly.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Assessment
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to appraise the magical abilities and defenses of a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. You learn if the creature has the ability to cast spells and the highest level of spell that the creature can cast. You also learn if the creature has the Magic Resistance or Legendary Resistance traits. For the next minute, or until you use this feature again, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the target creature's spells and magical effects.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Spell Tactics
entries: Your skill with magical maneuvers grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Maneuver Burst
entries: When you use a maneuver that expends one Battle Die, you can expend a spell slot to roll two Battle Dice instead of one without expending the second Battle Die. Add these Battle Dice together and add or subtract the sum of the dice, as appropriate for the maneuver.

entries.name: Strategic Recovery
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend a spell slot to regain a number of your expended Battle Dice up to the level of the spell slot expended.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Supreme Stratagems
entries: You gain the following maneuver options.

entries.name: Inexorable Spell
entries: When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against a spell you cast, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend two Battle Dice to force the target to reroll the saving throw with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sanguine Spell
entries: When a creature fails a saving throw against a spell that you cast, you can expend two Battle Dice as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to render it susceptible to damage. Each time the target takes damage until the end of your next turn, it takes extra Necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Battle Die.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Protomancer
entries: {@i Channel the Raw Essence of Magic}

Magic predates the written word, the founding of Wizard colleges, and even the invention of spells. Long before magic was formalized, mages funneled the bare threads of magic into protospells, fundamental expressions of what would later become the schools of magic. These spells predated the invention of material components and even the spellbook; as such, the first wizards etched protospells into their minds, consuming their memories as an important component of their spells.

The contemporary School of Protomancy seeks to rediscover the art of proto-magic through research and experimentation. Its protomages have no guidance for this forgotten art, but hope to learn from clues left in the structure of schools of magic.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Vital Recovery
entries: When you use your {@classFeature Arcane Recovery|Wizard|XPHB|1}, you can expend a number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} up to your Intelligence modifier. The combined number of spell slots regained by {@classFeature Arcane Recovery|Wizard|XPHB|1} is increased by the number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} expended in this way.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Mnemonic Concentration
entries: When you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on a spell, you take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to succeed on the saving throw instead. When you do so, you un-prepare a Wizard spell of your choice that you have prepared. You can't use this feature to un-prepare a spell that you always have prepared.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Proto-Master
entries: You can cast each spell with the {@filter [Protospell]|spells|subschool=protospell} tag you have prepared once without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell in this way, its effective level is 3.
Once you cast a spell using this feature, you can't cast that spell this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Scroll Scribe
entries: {@i Create and Share Powerful Spell Scrolls}

Any dedicated Wizard can translate one of their spells into a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG}, imbuing a scrap of parchment with the full force of its arcane power. As a Scroll Scribe, however, you focus almost exclusively on crafting scrolls for yourself and others. Your magic is largely recorded in advance, requiring careful preparation but granting extensive arcane power.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arcane Revision
entries: When you use your {@classFeature Arcane Recovery|Wizard|XPHB|1}, you can create a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} using your {@subclassFeature Scribe Scroll|Wizard|XPHB|Scroll Scribe|ValdaSpire24Extras|3}. You can use spell slots recovered with {@classFeature Arcane Recovery|Wizard|XPHB|1} to create a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} in this way. You can also change the spell recorded in each {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} you created, replacing the spell on the scroll with one you have prepared of the same level.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Warding Scrawl
entries: Whenever a creature casts a spell using one of your {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls}, it gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Wizard level plus the level of the spell. Additionally, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws it makes to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on the spell.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Scroll Codex
entries: When you create {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can create a level 1, level 2, and level 3 {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} without expending spell slots for them. These scrolls don't count against your number of {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} and can't be recycled to recover an expended spell slot. You can't have two scrolls at once that contain the same spell.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Somnomancer
entries: {@i Lull Your Enemies to Sleep}

Somnomancy is the arcane subschool of sleep and dreams. As a Somnomancer, your magic can calm a rampaging creature into a stupor, shape the dreams of others, and hypnotize those around you. Few other mages recognize this school's value, however, and believe most Somnomancers are merely sleeping on the job.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Hypnotize
entries: You can perform a repetitive action for 1 minute to hypnotize a willing creature or one that has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, giving it the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. While it has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition from this feature, the hypnotized creature uses the following rules.

entries.name: Suppressed Mind-Affecting Magic
entries: Magical effects that influence the creature's mind or cause it to be {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, cursed, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, or possessed are suppressed while it is hypnotized.

entries.name: Truthful
entries: The creature will truthfully answer any question posed to it, even if it is {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}. While hypnotized, it can perfectly recall its memories.

entries.name: Subconscious Suggestion
entries: You can cast {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} targeting the hypnotized creature, which automatically fails its saving throw against the spell. When you do so, the spell is modified so that it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB} and is triggered by a specified command word. The first time the creature hears the specified command word during the spell's duration, the spell instantly takes effect and the creature pursues the suggestion to the best of its ability. If you use this benefit to modify the {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} spell again, your Subconscious Suggestion ends on any previously-hypnotized creatures.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Lucid Dream
entries: When you take a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can cast one of the following spells while you sleep without a spell slot or Material components: {@spell Divination|XPHB}, {@spell Dream|XPHB}, {@spell Legend Lore|XPHB}, or {@spell Scrying|XPHB}. Casting this spell doesn't interrupt your {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Nightmares
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to deal Psychic damage equal to your Wizard level to each creature with the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. This damage can't end the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition on a creature.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Tyromancer
entries: {@i Wield the Power of Cheesy Puns}

Not all wizards find the right specialization within the conventional schools of magic, and instead turn to even more focused areas of expertise, like the School of Tyromancy. A Tyromancer (often called a "Cheese Wiz") specializes in a subsection of Gastronomy that draws energy from the Semi-Elemental Plane of Cheese to power their magic. The very first Cheese Wiz, Lactose the Intolerable, discovered this magic shortly before his untimely death.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Ferment Spell
entries: When you cast a level 1+ spell with casting time of an action that forces a target to make a saving throw, you can "ferment" the spell. The spell's saving throw becomes Constitution for this casting. On a failed save against the spell, a creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Legen-Dairy Resistance
entries: If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Lactose Intolerance
entries: When you use your {@subclassFeature Ferment Spell|Wizard|XPHB|Tyromancer|ValdaSpire24Extras|6}, you can choose for the spell to deal extra Poison damage equal to half your Wizard level plus your Intelligence modifier.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Universalist
entries: {@i Master Every Branch of Arcana}

Though most Wizards specialize in a single school of magic, the rare and exceptionally gifted might advance their studies into all schools equally. Universalists such as yourself examine magic on a fundamental level and uncover insights to unlock greater arcane power.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Eidetic Memory
entries: You can use your {@classFeature Memorize Spell|Wizard|XPHB|5} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.
You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Spellwarp
entries: When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can change the saving throw from Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution to another of these abilities, or from Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma to another of these abilities.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 4+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Erudite Focus
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to focus your arcane talent. This feature requires {@status Concentration|XPHB} as if you were concentrating on a spell. While you maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on it, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to take the {@action Study|XPHB} action, cast a Wizard cantrip that has a casting time of an action, or use a magic item that requires an action. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells while you maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on this feature.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Wand Wizard
entries: {@i Wield an Arsenal of Deadly Wands}

Wizards with a penchant for life-or-death arcane duels often become Wand Wizards equipped with an array of low-level wands. These personalized wands require vast wells of arcane power, but contain staple adventuring spells that can be cast at a moment's notice.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Wand Slinger
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to activate a wand. You can't take this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} if you've already cast a level 1+ spell on the current turn, nor can you cast a level 1+ spell on this turn after taking this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Warding Shield
entries: Add {@spell Shield|XPHB} to your spellbook for free. When you fail a saving throw, you can cast {@spell Shield|XPHB} without a spell slot. If you do so, you have a +5 bonus to saving throws for the duration, including against the triggering save, potentially turning it into a success.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Remnant Recharge
entries: Whenever you expend the last charge for a wand, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a 5 or 6, the last charge isn't expended.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Arachnoid Stalker
entries: {@i Sling Webs and Crawl Walls}

A life-changing event, such as being cursed by a drider or being bitten by a dangerously transmuted arachnid, has imbued you with the abilities of a spider. This transformation might have left you physically unchanged, or you may have developed a half-dozen eyes, lanky and hairy limbs, or a set of inhuman mandibles. Whatever the side effects, you can now produce deadly poison and ropes of silken web from your palms, and even scale walls with your fingertips.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Wall Crawling
entries: You've become accustomed to moving like a spider, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Climber
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Hiding on Ceilings
entries: If you are on a ceiling and {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|XPHB}, you can take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action as long as any enemy that could see you is below you.

entries.name: Spider Climb
entries: You can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and along ceilings, while leaving your hands free.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Spider Sense
entries: When you make a saving throw and take damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to use your {@classFeature Uncanny Dodge|Rogue|XPHB|5}, halving the damage you take (round down).

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Paralytic Venom
entries: You gain the following Cunning Strike option.

entries.name: Paralyze (Cost: {@dice 4d6})
entries: When you deal Poison damage with your {@subclassFeature Venomous Strike|Rogue|XPHB|Arachnoid Stalker|ValdaPlayerPack|3}, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dungeoneer
entries: {@i Survive the Dungeon}

Only fools would dive headfirst into an abandoned crypt filled with monsters and deathtraps, but it seems only fools emerge from such crypts laden with as much loot as they can carry. The archetypal dungeon delver is a veteran of such suicidal dungeon delves, and has become intimately familiar with the hazards therein. In the course of their adventures, such a Dungeoneer will have adopted countless best practices, along with a litany of unproven superstitions which they believe keeps them alive. Principles from "always be the first one to hit the monster" to "never be the first one to touch a treasure chest" line a Dungeoneer's journal. However, it's probably better to be paranoid and superstitious than lying at the bottom of a pit trap, incinerated by a Fireball, or digested by a mimic.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Dungeon Precautions
entries: You can cast any of the following spells without a spell slot: {@spell Alarm|XPHB}, {@spell Comprehend Languages|XPHB}, {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB}, {@spell Detect Poison and Disease|XPHB}, {@spell Find Traps|XPHB}, {@spell Identify|XPHB}, and {@spell Purify Food and Drink|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this feature (choose the ability when you cast the spell).
You can use this feature five times and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Monster Kill
entries: Once per turn when you hit an Aberration, Dragon, Fey, Fiend, Monstrosity, Ooze, or Undead with an attack with a weapon, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d10} damage to the target. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Avoidance
entries: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Veteran Hero
entries: Your dungeoneering expertise gives you the following benefits.

entries.name: Peerless Heroism
entries: Once per turn when you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can expend {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} to turn the roll into a 20, instead of rerolling the {@dice d20}.

entries.name: Double Inspiration
entries: You can have two instances of {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} at one time. You can use only one {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} per roll.

name: Future You Patron
subclassFeatures: I Could Do With Fewer Scars|Warlock|XPHB|Future You|ValdaPlayerPack|6

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Future You Patron
entries: {@i Manipulate Time with Help from the Future}

Your patron is you in a decades-distant future. Perhaps your future self found an artifact of great power connecting them to the past, which they must now lead you to discover, or perhaps they were taught the mystic arts by their future self long ago, a cycle you will have to continue someday. Your future self has forgotten the fine details of some things and outright refuses to tell you about things you "can't know yet," but nevertheless offers compelling insight and guidance. You're not quite sure what your future self is planning for your future (and for their past), but one thing is certain—they need you alive.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: I Could Do With Fewer Scars
entries: Your future self warns you of particular attacks to watch out for. When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain a +10 bonus to your AC against that attack, potentially causing it to miss.
You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Expect an Ambush
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage on the first round of combat.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Grandfather Paradox
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can goad a creature within 60 feet of you that can see or hear you into causing a paradox. The creature must make an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 10d6} Psychic damage and has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute as it is locked between opposing timelines. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only. The {@condition Stunned|XPHB} creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Oath of Revelry
entries: {@i Work Hard and Party Harder}

Paladins who swear the Oath of Revelry make a solemn vow to party day and night until their hearts give out. The antithesis of stuffy, lawful crusaders, these emissaries of carousal travel the land, crashing parties and raising hell wherever they raise a glass. Authorities bristle at their arrival, but the youth cheer, for a Party Paladin is always accompanied by a good time.
These paladins share the following tenets:

items: Abide by the doctrines of the Codicus Brodicus.
Celebrate every occasion, inviting friend and foe alike.
When necessary, fight for your right to party.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Aura of Fraternity
entries: You and your allies deal an extra {@damage 1d4} damage on attacks using Melee weapons or Unarmed Strikes while in your Aura of Protection. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Merrymaker
entries: When you or an ally within 30 feet of yourself that can see or hear you makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to give that creature {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. If the creature still fails the {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, this use of Merrymaker isn't expended.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Party Animal
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can imbue your Aura of Protection with the many-hued magic of revelry, granting the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Extra Damage
entries: The extra damage from your Aura of Fraternity increases to {@dice 1d8}.

entries.name: Heroic Inspiration
entries: At the start of each of your turns, you can give {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} to one ally within the aura.

entries.name: Immunities
entries: You and your allies have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}, and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions while in the aura.

name: Path of the Muscle Wizard
subclassFeatures: Path of the Muscle Wizard|Barbarian|XPHB|Muscle Wizard|ValdaPlayerPack|3

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Path of the Muscle Wizard
entries: {@i Be a Buff, Angry "Wizard"}

You're a wizard! Perhaps you went to wizarding school on a football scholarship or just picked up a book at the gym and started reading. No matter how you got here, you're a wizard, one that just coincidentally has massive, rippling muscles. You have the big dumb hat and the book filled with gibberish and everything!

You gently remind others, often by beating them to a pulp and cracking their bones, that your magical powers shouldn't be questioned. You're a good wizard—the best one, even! And only a fool would say otherwise.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: "Spells"
entries: Your "magic" is powerful enough to cast every "spell" that exists (and no one can prove otherwise without broken ribs). However, you only prepared the following "spells" today. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you can use each of the following "Spells" once. When you do so, you can't use that "Spell" again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Burning Hands
entries: Your backhand slap is legendary. As an action, you can make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against each creature within your reach. On a hit, this strike deals Bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 1d8} plus your Strength modifier and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack it makes before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Magic Missile
entries: As an action, you can make three ranged attacks using {@item Dart|XPHB|Darts}, {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers}, or other weapons with {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} that use Strength for the attack and damage rolls. Because Magic Missile never misses, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on these attack rolls.

entries.name: Shield
entries: When you are hit by an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to quickly don a {@item Shield|XPHB} to defend yourself. You gain the Shield's AC bonus against the triggering attack, potentially causing it to miss. If the attack hits, the damage dealt to you is reduced by an amount equal to your Barbarian level.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Magic Resistance
entries: You're such an amazing wizard that other wizards can't even touch you. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: I Cast Fist
entries: You can crush your enemies with your ultimate "spell":

entries.name: Fist
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action while your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you can replace one of your attacks with a really hard punch. Make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. On a hit, the target takes Bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 6d6} plus your Strength modifier and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition if it is Huge or smaller. You can use this feature once per active Rage.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Warrior of the Street
entries: {@i Strike with Combos and Special Moves}

"Street fighting" is an urban discipline founded on necessity, whose blindingly fast, unique brand of martial arts has been honed and perfected in back-alley brawls and tournaments alike. Monks who adopt this relatively new technique place comparatively little value on spiritual enlightenment and inner focus; the thrill of split-second timing, rapid combos, and decisive knock-outs drive them to become the best combatants in the world

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Special Moves
entries: You have memorized patterns of discrete movements that allow you to use the following special moves.

entries.name: Energy Blast
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to replace one of your attacks with a blast of energy. One creature of your choice that you can see within 60 feet makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking Force damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die, or half as much damage on a successful save.

entries.name: Guard Breaker
entries: If you make an attack roll with your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and miss the target, you can expend 1 Focus Point to perform a Guard Breaker. This {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} deals damage equal to your Dexterity modifier to the target. This miss doesn't reset your Combo bonus to attack rolls.

entries.name: Uppercut
entries: When you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and deal damage, you can expend 1 Focus point to make an uppercut. You can push the target up to 5 feet away from you and give the target the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition if it is Large or smaller.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: Air Dash
entries: On your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} until the end of your next turn (no action required). You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next melee attack you make before the end of the current turn.

subclassFeaturesFull.name: K.O.
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can attempt to knock the target out. The target takes extra Force damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die. If the target has 100 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or fewer after you deal damage with the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, it has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition for 10 minutes.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending 5 Focus Points (no action required).
